clauses.title: Commit
clauses.body: = append physical redo to the WAL (fsync on a filesystem WAL; in-process buffer for `:memory:`) then **`apply_redo`** onto the in-memory graph. The live graph is never the source of a commit.

clauses.title: Materialize
clauses.body: = load ADR-0005 / ADR-0022 Parquet (manifest parts or legacy `nodes.parquet` / `relationships.parquet`) then replay WAL records with `lsn > checkpoint_lsn`. Open always does this. No empty-graph shortcut that skips the store.

clauses.title: Snapshot
clauses.body: = checkpoint writes those Parquet files from the **already applied** committed graph, then truncates the WAL. Parquet is not written except as a snapshot of WAL-committed state. `:memory:` uses the same types: an in-process object store for Parquet and an in-process WAL. It is still process-ephemeral (nothing on disk) but there is no second code path. `wal: Option<_>` is gone. Every `Database` has a WAL and a store.

clauses.title: Txn id
clauses.body: Each write attempt allocates a monotonically increasing `txn_id` (`AtomicU64`) at start. Unpublished versions on the private snapshot use that id as `xmin`.

clauses.title: Private execute
clauses.body: The writer clones the committed graph under a read lock, executes Cypher on that clone (MATCH+CREATE in one statement still sees its own writes), and drops the clone. The shared graph is not mutated and not exclusively locked during execute or fsync. Node/rel ids come from process-wide atomics so concurrent creates do not collide.

clauses.title: Evaluate at WAL
clauses.body: A commit mutex (the WAL) is acquired. If any committed version in the attempt’s **write set** has `xmin`/`xmax` newer than the attempt’s `snapshot_ts`, the attempt is discarded and the statement is retried on a fresh snapshot. Otherwise `commit_ts = max(last_committed + 1, txn_id)` (always increasing in WAL order), the record is appended and fsynced, then `apply_redo` publishes that `commit_ts` on the shared graph.

clauses.title: Write set
clauses.body: Physical node/rel identities in the redo: `SET` / `REMOVE` / `DELETE` / label changes conflict with any later version of that id. New `CREATE` ids conflict only if the id is already present. A new relationship conflicts if an endpoint visible at the snapshot is no longer live (deleted), not merely property-updated. First committer on overlapping write sets wins. Disjoint creates (typical payment edges) commit concurrently. Readers keep ADR-0013 visibility; they are blocked only for the short `apply_redo`, not for …

clauses.title: Pin
clauses.body: A read or write execute records `snapshot_ts = commit_ts` once at start. MATCH/expand/index use that timestamp for the whole statement, not the advancing published `commit_ts`.

clauses.title: Publish last
clauses.body: `apply_redo` installs versions with `xmin = commit_ts`, then stores `commit_ts`. Readers pinned earlier never observe a torn apply.

clauses.title: No exclusive graph lock for apply
clauses.body: `apply_redo` takes `&Graph` (concurrent maps). The database `RwLock` is taken in **read** mode for queries and for apply. Checkpoint/GC still take the write side so they wait for in-flight statements, then rebuild indexes from versions live at the checkpoint timestamp.

clauses.title: Indexes are a superset
clauses.body: `SET`/`DELETE` do not remove index entries until GC. Lookups re-check labels and properties on the version visible at `snapshot_ts`. WAL protocol (ADR-0014, ADR-0015) is unchanged: append + `sync_all`, then apply, first-committer-wins on the write set.

clauses.title: Assign commit_ts and append in waiter order.
clauses.body: Assign `commit_ts` and append in waiter order.

clauses.title: Conflict-check each attempt against the applied graph and
clauses.body: Conflict-check each attempt against the applied graph **and** earlier records in this group that are written but not yet applied.

clauses.title: Overlapping write sets are not appended; the later waiter gets
clauses.body: Overlapping write sets are not appended; the later waiter gets `Error::Conflict`. Only independent records share the fsync. `apply_redo` still runs **after** the group fsync, in `commit_ts` order (ADR-0014). Readers do not see a commit that is only in the page cache. Suggested approach (implementation detail, not binding): a handoff queue so waiters park without holding the WAL mutex; one leader drains the queue, appends the independent records, `sync_all`s once, applies, and wakes the batch.

clauses.title: Segments
clauses.body: WAL files are `wal/NNNNNNNN.log` (`00000001.log`, …). Append only hits the **open** segment. `should_checkpoint` (64 MiB or 10 000 commits) **closes** that file (fsync, open the next number). `:memory:` keeps one record list; recycle drops `lsn <= checkpoint_lsn`.

clauses.title: Pin
clauses.body: After rotate, `checkpoint_lsn` is the max LSN in **closed** segments and `snapshot_ts` is `graph.commit_ts()` (those records are already applied). The WAL mutex is released.

clauses.title: Dump
clauses.body: Parquet is written from rows visible at `snapshot_ts` under a graph **read** lock. Manifest `commit_ts` / `checkpoint_lsn` match that pin. Writers continue on the open segment (`apply_redo` is a concurrent read lock).

clauses.title: Recycle
clauses.body: After the manifest is durable, delete closed segments with `max_lsn <= checkpoint_lsn`. The live file is never rewritten.

clauses.title: GC
clauses.body: Version GC stays under the exclusive graph lock **after** the dump, so in-flight readers drain first (ADR-0018). `Database::checkpoint()` and last-handle drop wait for an in-flight dump, rotate if the open segment has records, dump, recycle, then GC. Replay is unchanged: load Parquet, apply WAL records with `lsn > checkpoint_lsn` across segments in id order.

clauses.title: Layout
clauses.body: `manifest.json` format_version **3** lists shard parts. Each part is a Parquet file of live rows (same columns as ADR-0005) for an half-open id range `[id_lo, id_hi)`: … Load reads every part, then WAL replay (`lsn > checkpoint_lsn`) as today. format_version 1–2 still load the monolith pair.

clauses.title: Copy-on-write
clauses.body: The graph records dirty node/rel ids on committed mutations. A checkpoint rewrites **only** parts that overlap dirty ids (or new ranges). Unchanged objects are not written. Manifest is published last. Retired part paths are deleted after the new manifest is durable.

clauses.title: Byte budget, derived width
clauses.body: The cap is **bytes**, default 256 MiB (`MEMORYDB_SHARD_TARGET_BYTES`). Id-window width is `W = clamp(target / max(ewma_bytes_per_row, 256), 4096, 1_000_000)` `ewma_bytes_per_row` is updated from written parts (file bytes / row count), separately for nodes and relationships. Until the first measurement, assume 1024 bytes/row (conservative: fewer ids per window). New high-id windows use the current `W`, aligned to `W`.

clauses.title: Split on overflow
clauses.body: If encoding a dirty window exceeds the target and the window has more than one row, split at the median live id, recurse, replace one manifest entry with two. A single row larger than the target is allowed (hard exception). Do not globally rehash or move ids between existing windows except this split (merge of undersized neighbors is follow-on).

clauses.title: Not in this ADR
clauses.body: Community / graph-locality placement. Out-of-core page cache. Delta/tombstone files.

clauses.title: Pins
clauses.body: `execute_read` and optimistic write execute register `snapshot_ts` on the graph (`pin_now` / drop). `gc_horizon` is `min(commit_ts, min in-flight pin)` (or `commit_ts` if none).

clauses.title: Drop
clauses.body: A version with `xmax ≠ 0` is dropped when `xmax ≤ gc_horizon`. Live rows (`xmax == 0`) stay. Each id’s version vec is mutated under that DashMap entry only. Other ids and other statements proceed.

clauses.title: Indexes
clauses.body: When versions of a node are dropped, remove that id from label/property keys that **no remaining version** of the id still carries. No `label_index` / `prop_index` clear+rescan. Adjacency stays a superset (neighbors already filter `rel()`).

clauses.title: Locks
clauses.body: Checkpoint GC uses the graph **read** lock (same as dump / apply). The exclusive write lock is not taken for GC.

clauses.title: Fold
clauses.body: AND-equality `n.k = literal|$param` (either side) and `n:Label` conjuncts on a node **introduced in this MATCH** are merged into that node’s label list / property map so `lookup_nodes` is an IndexSeek. Residual `WHERE` stays on the same clause.

clauses.title: Orient
clauses.body: For a connected path with no path variable, compare seed scores of the **endpoints** only. If the last node is strictly more selective, reverse the path and flip hop directions. Middle starts are out of scope (the matcher is still left-to-right).

clauses.title: Order
clauses.body: Disconnected comma patterns are stable-sorted by the seed score of each path’s `nodes[0]` (after orient), most selective first. Seed score, highest first: already-bound variable, then label+equality map, then label only, then bare node. Logical meaning (realized by the existing executor, not a new IR): **Barriers.** Do not rewrite `CREATE` / `MERGE` / `DELETE` / `SET`. Do not reorder across `WITH` or `UNWIND`. Do not reverse a path that binds a path variable (`MATCH p = …`) — `nodes(p)` / `relationships(p)` follow …

clauses.title: Auto-commit (default)
clauses.body: Unchanged: a write statement appends redo and `apply_redo`s before `query` returns. A read pins `commit_ts` at statement start.

clauses.title: `begin`
clauses.body: Pins `snapshot_ts = last_committed` and allocates one `txn_id`. Nested `begin` is a semantic error (`already in a transaction`).

clauses.title: Statements in the transaction
clauses.body: Every subsequent `query` on that connection — read or write — runs on the shared graph plus the same private `WriteScratch` (ADR-0016). The connection sees the pinned snapshot and its own writes. Other connections do not see uncommitted writes. Stats on `QueryResult` stay per statement.

clauses.title: `commit`
clauses.body: The accumulated redo is one WAL record and one `commit_ts` (ADR-0015, ADR-0017, ADR-0019). Empty redo is a no-op (no WAL append). Write-write conflict discards the overlay and returns `Error::Conflict`. After `commit` (success or conflict) the connection is auto-commit again. `commit` without `begin` is `no transaction`.

clauses.title: `rollback`
clauses.body: Drops the overlay; nothing is appended. Connection drop is implicit rollback. `rollback` without `begin` is `no transaction`.

clauses.title: Failed transaction
clauses.body: A statement error marks the transaction failed. Further `query` / `commit` return `transaction failed; rollback required`. Only `rollback` (or drop) clears it. Partial overlay from the failed statement is discarded with the transaction.

clauses.title: Surfaces
clauses.body: Rust `Connection::{begin, commit, rollback, in_transaction}`; C ABI `memorydb_begin` / `memorydb_commit` / `memorydb_rollback`; Bolt `BEGIN` / `COMMIT` / `ROLLBACK` (RESET rollbacks an open transaction). Language clients wrap the C ABI. CLI meta: `.begin` / `.commit` / `.rollback`. HTTP `POST /query` stays auto-commit per request (no session affinity).

clauses.title: Not a Cypher clause
clauses.body: `BEGIN` / `COMMIT` / `ROLLBACK` are not added to the OpenCypher parser. The pinned TCK has no such statements.

clauses.title: Equality
clauses.body: — existing ADR-0010 `(label, key, literal) → ids`. Unchanged. `{id: $id}` / `n.prop = $q` stay IndexSeek.

clauses.title: Prefix
clauses.body: — per `(label, key)`, a `BTreeMap` of the string value → ids. `STARTS WITH` is a range over that map, then a snapshot visibility + `starts_with` check (indexes remain a superset, ADR-0018).

clauses.title: Trigram
clauses.body: — overlapping character 3-grams of the value (and 1- and 2-grams so needles shorter than 3 can post). `CONTAINS $q` intersects the needle’s grams, then verifies `contains` at `snapshot_ts`. The executor seeds `MATCH (n:Label) WHERE n.prop CONTAINS $q` (or `STARTS WITH`) from these postings when the conjunct is a top-level AND leaf on a node introduced in that MATCH. Residual `WHERE` still runs (false-positive grams, overlay creates, MVCC). Empty `CONTAINS` needle: do not post; fall back to the label scan …

clauses.title: Intern
clauses.body: label, relationship-type, and property-key strings. Live records hold ids. Materialize public maps at `node_at` / `rel_at`, checkpoint encode, and overlay copy-on-write.

clauses.title: Compact node records
clauses.body: — interned labels plus a compact property list (interned keys + `Value`), not a `BTreeMap` per version.

clauses.title: Compact relationship payloads
clauses.body: — the common three-key map `{id: STRING, amount: NUMBER, ts: INTEGER}` is a fixed struct. Any other shape (or a later SET that breaks the shape) uses the same compact property list as nodes.

clauses.title: Typed CSR / per-type chunks
clauses.body: — `out_adj` / `in_adj` are interned `type_id → Vec<RelId>` chunks, not `HashMap<String, …>`. Incremental create appends to the type’s chunk. `rebuild_adj` writes the same shape. Lists stay a **superset** (ADR-0023): delete does not unlink; expand still filters with visibility. No query/result cache. No Parquet or WAL format change. No `CREATE INDEX`. Overlay scratch may stay a flat id list (ADR-0031).

clauses.title: Length 1
clauses.body: — any start→end edge (pattern direction).

clauses.title: Length 2
clauses.body: — intersect 1-hop from start with 1-hop from end (reverse direction on the end).

clauses.title: Length 3
clauses.body: — iterate the **smaller** 1-hop set; for each node, walk one hop toward the other set; **stop at the first** valid meet (after 1 and 2 missed, any 3-hop trail is shortest). Reconstruct one trail from the three (or fewer) relationship ids. The no-rel-reuse rule applies to that trail. `length(...)` still returns the hop count without a `Path` (ADR-0034). Unbound end, `max_hops > 3`, undirected `-`, and `allShortestPaths` stay on ADR-0034 / ADR-0025. A miss still walks the last-layer edges (must prove no 3-hop). It …

clauses.title: Front-end
clauses.body: `Database::query` uses `cypherlite-parser` + `memorydb-front`. The historical parser is available only with `MEMORYDB_PARSER=memorydb` for diagnostics; it is not a product query path.

clauses.title: TCK floor
clauses.body: MemoryDB TCK remains 100% (pin 2024.3, 0 skips). CypherLite’s 3 TCK skips are not imported into that gate.

clauses.title: CIP-eval stretch
clauses.body: Source `cyperlite-original` cip-eval is the language baseline (pass counts only ratchet up). In-tree MemoryDB-backed cip-eval uses `baselines/cip-eval-memorydb.json` until it matches that baseline.

clauses.title: Loadtests
clauses.body: Fraud / identity / checkpoint must not regress vs frozen `baselines/` summaries (`errors == 0`, ops/s ≥ 90%, p99 ≤ 115%, logical bytes ≤ 110%).

clauses.title: Tier 2 theater
clauses.body: `SHOW ROLES/SERVERS/USERS`, `CREATE DATABASE`, composite `USE` are documented deviations, not silent fails. User docs may link this ADR.

clauses.title: Contract
clauses.body: `AGENTS.md` in this tree is the working contract (copied from MemoryDB, updated only via ADR).

clauses.title: memorydb::Database must pass every CIP-eval scenario passed by the
clauses.body: `memorydb::Database` must pass every CIP-eval scenario passed by the checked-in original CypherLite engine. Only scenarios that fail or are skipped by the original may fail or be skipped by MemoryDB.

clauses.title: The gate compares stable scenario identities as well as aggregate
clauses.body: The gate compares stable scenario identities as well as aggregate counts. Live Engine CIP is replaced by the frozen identity set in `testdata/cip-eval/ENGINE_PASSING.json` (ADR-0052). Aggregate CIP counts remain in `testdata/cip-eval/BASELINE.json` and `baselines/cip-eval-memorydb.json`.

clauses.title: Embedded catalog behavior previously excluded by ADR-0046 is now in
clauses.body: Embedded catalog behavior previously excluded by ADR-0046 is now in scope, including SHOW users/roles/servers/databases, database DDL, graph types, Cypher-version selection, and composite USE where the original implements them.

clauses.title: cypherlite-parser remains the only product grammar. memorydb-parser may
clauses.body: `cypherlite-parser` remains the only product grammar. `memorydb-parser` may gain AST/IR types but its parser is diagnostic-only.

clauses.title: Semantics are ported onto the MemoryDB planner, executor, catalog, CSR,
clauses.body: Semantics are ported onto the MemoryDB planner, executor, catalog, CSR, overlay, and WAL. The GraphStore storage path is not grafted onto MemoryDB.

clauses.title: legacy CypherLite surface tests and its CIP reference;
clauses.body: legacy CypherLite surface tests and its CIP reference;

clauses.title: MemoryDB runtime, front-end, and 3897/3897 TCK;
clauses.body: MemoryDB runtime, front-end, and 3897/3897 TCK;

clauses.title: strict MemoryDB-to-original scenario parity;
clauses.body: strict MemoryDB-to-original scenario parity;

clauses.title: formatting and Clippy;
clauses.body: formatting and Clippy;

clauses.title: frozen load-test comparisons.
clauses.body: frozen load-test comparisons. Sibling trees remain read-only historical baselines and are not runtime gate dependencies.

clauses.title: Codec owns store files
clauses.body: A snapshot codec implements `load` (open, before WAL replay) and `dump` (checkpoint, after LSN pin). Parquet keeps dirty id-window copy-on-write (ADR-0022). JSON rewrites `graph.json` in full. Different codecs may have different characteristics.

clauses.title: One codec per database instance
clauses.body: No mixing Parquet objects and `graph.json` in one URI. The codec is recorded in `manifest.json` as `"codec": "parquet" | "json"`. Absent `codec` on existing directories means parquet.

clauses.title: Envelope
clauses.body: `manifest.json` always carries `codec` and `checkpoint_lsn` (WAL recycle). Parquet keeps shard lists, `next_*`, indexes, and constraints in that file. JSON writes a slim envelope plus CypherLite GraphData in `graph.json` (layout: MemoryDB directory `wal/`; not a drop-in `.db` file URI).

clauses.title: Selection
clauses.body: Empty URI: `OpenOptions.snapshot_codec`, else `MEMORYDB_SNAPSHOT_FORMAT`, else parquet. Existing URI: envelope (or inferred from files if the envelope is missing). A mismatched flag is an error.

clauses.title: JSON schema
clauses.body: `graph.json` is CypherLite `GraphData` (`nodes`, `relationships`, `indexes`, `constraints`, `next_node_id`, `next_rel_id`, optional `graph_type` / `read_only`) with `cypherlite-model` `__type` property tags. `read_only: true` fails open. Default JSON dump writes `read_only: false`. WAL, redo, and checkpoint choreography are unchanged.

clauses.title: WASM opens `Database::open(":memory:")` only
clauses.body: JS `CypherLiteDb.create()` accepts omitted / `memory://` / `:memory:`. `idb://…` and bare paths error (use `memory://`). `flush()` is a no-op Promise.

clauses.title: Delete the persist stack
clauses.body: `persist/`, `OpenDb`, IndexedDB crates, `browser_idb` tests, and native file-backed JsonStore wasm tests are gone, not dormant.

clauses.title: Portable snapshots are GraphData
clauses.body: `exportJson` / `importJson` use the ADR-0050 JSON GraphData helpers. Hosts may put that string in `localStorage`. That is not IndexedDB durability.

clauses.title: IndexedDB later, if at all, is an ObjectStore
clauses.body: behind Database — not a codec and not a whole-graph KV blob.

clauses.title: Playground is memory-only
clauses.body: No Storage switch. CI browser smoke is `:memory:` (`RETURN 1`, CREATE/MATCH), not IndexedDB. wasm32 omits the Parquet/Arrow snapshot codec so the playground binary stays within the size budget (JSON GraphData only).

clauses.title: The engine is an embedded library. The public Rust crate
clauses.body: The engine is an **embedded library**. The public Rust crate (`memorydb`) is first-class for Rust users.

clauses.title: The C ABI (memorydb-ffi, documented in docs/api/c/) is the
clauses.body: The **C ABI** (`memorydb-ffi`, documented in `docs/api/c/`) is the multi-language boundary. Wave-1 bindings (Python, JavaScript, Java, Go) wrap that ABI and do not invent a second wire protocol.

clauses.title: A Bolt server (memorydb-bolt) is optional remote transport so
clauses.body: A **Bolt** server (`memorydb-bolt`) is optional remote transport so official Neo4j drivers can `RUN` OpenCypher. Bolt is not Neo4j Cypher parity (ADR-0056). Supported Bolt versions are documented in `docs/api/bolt/`. Do not add a client language until the C ABI for the used features is documented.

clauses.title: Typed payloads
clauses.body: The three catalog-DDL redo ops carry typed, serde-serializable models captured once at DDL-execution time from the parsed clause: `CatalogIndexDetail` carries `redo::IndexDetailSpec` (with `redo::IndexKindSpec` for the index kind) plus the evaluated `OPTIONS` map as tagged JSON (`redo::props_json`). `PutGraphType` and `SetCurrentGraphType` carry `graph_type::GraphTypeSpec`.

clauses.title: No re-parse on replay
clauses.body: `Graph::apply_redo` stores these models verbatim. It never formats a DDL string and never re-parses Cypher text during replay.

clauses.title: Loud decode failure
clauses.body: WAL records written in the old Cypher-text shape fail serde decode at replay: replay returns `Err` and startup fails loudly. There is no silent skip or drop of an undecodable record. (Covered by `legacy_string_payload_no_longer_decodes` in `crates/cypherlite-executor/src/redo.rs`.)

clauses.title: Pre-1.0 rationale
clauses.body: Breaking the old record shape without a migration path is accepted because the crate is pre-1.0 (`0.3.0-alpha`) and no ADR has ever guaranteed WAL payload compatibility — ADR-0012's format discipline covers checkpoint manifests only. The change is a correctness hardening: replay can no longer silently lose index or graph-type catalog state.

clauses.title: Local reference host (unchanged)
clauses.body: Repo-root `baselines/` remains the `make gate` / `make compare-loadtests` comparison set, frozen from the local dev host (ADR-0060). The local gate does not change.

clauses.title: CI host class
clauses.body: The `loadtest-baselines` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` uploads the fresh `target/fraud-loadtest.json` and `target/identity-loadtest.json` reports as a `loadtest-reports` workflow artifact with `if: always()`, then compares against `baselines/ci/` (`make compare-loadtests BASELINES=baselines/ci`). The ADR-0046 bands are unchanged (ops/s ≥ 90%, p99 ≤ 115% + 250,000 ns, logical bytes ≤ 110%); `errors == 0` stays absolute on every host.

clauses.title: Bootstrap rule
clauses.body: When `baselines/ci/fraud-loadtest.json` is absent, the job still runs both loadtests and uploads the artifacts, prints a greppable `seeding run — compare skipped` line, and exits 0. Seeding is: download the artifacts from a green run, summarize with `scripts/summarize-loadtest.py`, commit `baselines/ci/*.json`.

clauses.title: Manual trigger only
clauses.body: Releases are triggered exclusively by `workflow_dispatch` on the Release workflow, with a `bump` choice input (`patch` / `minor` / `major`, default `patch`). The previous tag-push trigger (`on: push: tags: ["v*"]`) is removed. A release is a deliberate, human-gated act.

clauses.title: Tag-after-build
clauses.body: The git tag `vX.Y.Z` is created and pushed by the workflow only *after* the cli, ffi, and python build jobs all succeed. A failed build leaves no dangling tag: the tag is an output of a successful run, never an input to it.

clauses.title: Lockstep Rust + Python versioning
clauses.body: The Rust workspace version (`[workspace.package]` in the root `Cargo.toml`, inherited by all crates) and the Python package version (`pyproject.toml` plus the `__init__.py` fallbacks) are versioned in lockstep and bumped together by the release workflow. The first stable release is **0.4.0**; pre-release versions such as the current `0.3.0-alpha` are skipped going forward.

clauses.title: Independent JS and Java client versions
clauses.body: The JavaScript client (`clients/javascript/package.json`, `0.1.0`) and the Java client (`clients/java/pom.xml`, `0.1.0`) are versioned independently and are **not** bumped by the release workflow.

clauses.title: Automated notes and changelog
clauses.body: Release notes are GitHub auto-generated (`generate_release_notes: true`). CHANGELOG.md rotation is automated in the version-bump commit: the `Unreleased` content moves under a new `## [X.Y.Z] — <date>` section. Because `main` is not branch-protected, the workflow pushes this bump commit directly.

clauses.title: URL
clauses.body: The canonical installer URL is `https://neo4j-labs.github.io/cypherlite/install.sh`. It is **not** `https://cypherlite.github.io/install.sh`: no `cypherlite` GitHub organization exists, and project Pages sites are served from `<org>.github.io/<repo>`.

clauses.title: Hosting
clauses.body: The script lives at `docs/static/install.sh`. The Docusaurus build copies everything under `docs/static/` to the site root, so the existing `gh-pages` deploy publishes it at the URL above. No new CI workflow is added and the GitHub Pages source setting is unchanged.

clauses.title: Platforms
clauses.body: macOS and Linux only, on both `amd64` and `arm64` (`cypherlite-linux-amd64`, `cypherlite-linux-arm64`, `cypherlite-darwin-amd64`, `cypherlite-darwin-arm64`). Windows stays on the manual `.exe` download documented in the README.

clauses.title: Install directory
clauses.body: The script installs to `$HOME/.local/bin`. It does not require `sudo` and does not write outside the user’s home directory.

clauses.title: Assets
clauses.body: The installer downloads the raw release binary for the detected platform directly. Assets are named `cypherlite-<os>-<arch>` (no tarballs) and are verified against the release’s `SHA256SUMS`, which is in macOS `shasum` format (`<hex> <name>`, two spaces). This is the existing release contract; the installer changes nothing in `release.yml`.

clauses.title: Authentication
clauses.body: While the repository is internal, all GitHub API and release-asset requests carry `Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN`. When `GITHUB_TOKEN` is unset the script is a no-op auth-wise, so it works unchanged once the repository is public and the token is unnecessary.

clauses.title: Invocation
clauses.body: The documented one-liner is: … The environment prefix **must** be on `bash`, not on `curl`. An environment prefix on the left of a pipe applies only to that command and never reaches the script on the right-hand side through the pipe; attaching it to `bash` is what makes `$GITHUB_TOKEN` visible to the installer. Implementation of `docs/static/install.sh`, the README install section, and the `gh auth token` guidance is owned by separate changes; this ADR only fixes the distribution decision.

clauses.title: Positional lifecycle commands
clauses.body: `skill`, `upgrade`, and `update` are recognized **only as the first argument** to the `cypherlite` CLI: `cypherlite skill install [--agent NAME]` `cypherlite skill remove [--agent NAME]` `cypherlite upgrade [--yes] [--check]` `cypherlite update` — an alias of `upgrade`. Database paths literally named `skill`, `upgrade`, or `update` stay reachable via a `./` prefix (e.g. `cypherlite ./skill`) or after `--` (e.g. `cypherlite -- skill`).

clauses.title: The --skill/-skill and --agent/-agent flags are removed
clauses.body: This is a breaking change. Because these flags never shipped in a release (they postdate the tree but predate 0.4.0, the first stable release), there is no installed base to migrate and therefore no migration-hint special-casing: the removed spellings hit the generic unknown-flag error like any other unrecognized argument.

clauses.title: Upgrade fetch
clauses.body: The command issues `GET https://api.github.com/repos/neo4j-labs/cypherlite/releases/latest`, attaching `Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN` only when the environment variable is set (the repository is currently internal; this is parity with `docs/static/install.sh`, ADR-0068). The release’s `tag_name` (leading `v` stripped) is semver-compared against the binary’s own `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`; if the latest release is not newer, the command prints an up-to-date message and exits 0.

clauses.title: Asset resolution
clauses.body: Asset ids are parsed from the release JSON with `serde_json` (no shell scraping). The platform binary `cypherlite-<os>-<arch>` and `SHA256SUMS` are downloaded via the GitHub API asset endpoint with an `Accept: application/octet-stream` header.

clauses.title: Verification and dependencies
clauses.body: The sha256 of the downloaded binary is verified against its `SHA256SUMS` entry using a **new** `sha2` workspace dependency. HTTP uses the **existing** workspace `ureq = "3.4"` dependency (already declared, previously unused). No other new dependencies are added.

clauses.title: Atomic self-replace
clauses.body: The verified binary is staged at a temporary path in `current_exe()`’s directory (guaranteeing the same filesystem), chmod 755, then renamed over the running binary. This is macOS/Linux only, the same platform scope as the ADR-0068 installer; on Windows the command errors with a not-supported message pointing at the manual `.exe` download (a running `.exe` cannot be replaced).

clauses.title: Skill refresh after a successful replace
clauses.body: Agents are detected first; if none are detected the step is skipped silently. On an interactive TTY the command prompts `Update installed cypherlite skill? [Y/n]` with yes as the default; `--yes` auto-accepts; a non-interactive run without `--yes` prints a `run: cypherlite skill install` hint instead. On yes, the **new** binary is spawned as `cypherlite skill install` with inherited stdio, so the new embedded skill bundle is what gets installed (the old process only holds the old bundle).

clauses.title: `--check` flag
clauses.body: A read-only current-vs-latest report: it changes nothing on disk and exits 0.

clauses.title: Compile unconstrained
clauses.body: in `rust:1.88-bookworm` (no CPU/memory cap), producing GNU/Linux `target/release/{fraud-loadtest,identity-loadtest,fraud-checkpoint}`.

clauses.title: Run constrained
clauses.body: in `debian:bookworm-slim` with two CPUs of CFS bandwidth on a 10 ms period (`--cpu-period=10000 --cpu-quota=20000`), `--memory=2g`, `--memory-swap=2g` (no extra swap). Prefer bind-mounting the repo so reports land in `target/*.json`. When the Docker daemon cannot bind-mount the repo (Docker Desktop file-sharing), `scripts/baseline-env.sh` streams sources into a named volume and copies reports back.

clauses.title: Store on tmpfs
clauses.body: The run container mounts `--tmpfs /tmp:exec,rw,size=1g`. Default on-disk URIs are `/tmp/fraud-lt` and `/tmp/fraud-checkpoint`. Identity stays `:memory:`.

clauses.title: Make is the entry point
clauses.body: `make fraud-loadtest`, `make identity-loadtest`, `make fraud-checkpoint`, and `make baseline-loadtests` default to this environment (`BASELINE_ENV=docker`). `make baseline-loadtests` refuses `BASELINE_ENV=host`. `BASELINE_ENV=host` remains a debug escape that uses host `cargo run`; those reports must not be frozen or gate-compared.

clauses.title: One comparison set
clauses.body: Repo-root `baselines/` is the only loadtest comparison set. Local `make gate` / `make compare-loadtests` and the CI `loadtest-baselines` job all compare dockerized reports against it with the ADR-0046 bands (script defaults). `baselines/ci/` is withdrawn.

clauses.title: The freeze is a worst-of-N envelope
clauses.body: `make baseline-loadtests` runs each suite `BASELINE_RUNS` times (default 5) and `scripts/freeze-baseline-envelope.py` keeps the lowest throughput, the highest per-use-case p99, and the highest logical bytes. A single run does not pin the tail; the envelope does.

clauses.title: Worker counts are sized for two CPUs
clauses.body: `WORKERS` 50 -> 8, `WORKERS_IDENTITY` 8 -> 4. ADR-0048's counts saturate the container, and queueing delay alone then swings per-use-case p99 by 2-4x run to run (`recent_transfers` p99 2.35 / 5.43 / 3.63 / 4.09 ms against a 1.24 ms envelope). At 8 / 4 the suites still load both CPUs — fraud 6,122-6,647 ops/s, identity 3,312-3,621 ops/s across six runs, both 1.09x spread — and an envelope built from five runs held a sixth, held-out run with no throughput breach and no fraud p99 breach. ADR-0048's 40 MiB budget …

clauses.title: Absolute p99 allowance of 5 ms
clauses.body: The one held-out breach was a sub-millisecond read (`detect_sod`, 0.202 ms envelope, 2.962 ms on the held-out run): at that scale a single queueing delay dominates the measurement. `make compare-loadtests` therefore sets `LOADTEST_P99_JITTER_NS=5000000`, the same value ADR-0064 calibrated for CI, here with ~1.7x headroom over the measured ~3 ms swing. The 1.15x ratio still governs every use case above ~1.7 ms, and `errors == 0`, the 0.90 throughput floor, and the 1.10 logical-bytes ratio are untouched.

clauses.title: Re-freeze
clauses.body: Throughput under 2 CPUs / 2 GB will not match the old unconstrained Mac or CI numbers. This ADR re-freezes `baselines/fraud-loadtest.json`, `baselines/identity-loadtest.json`, and `baselines/fraud-checkpoint.json` from a dockerized `make baseline-loadtests`. Six consecutive verification rounds (`make fraud-loadtest && make identity-loadtest && make compare-loadtests`) passed against that freeze. ### Why a 10 ms CFS period and not `--cpus=2` `--cpus=2` is the same bandwidth on Docker's default 100 ms period …

clauses.title: CI owns the freeze
clauses.body: Committed `baselines/fraud-loadtest.json`, `baselines/identity-loadtest.json`, and `baselines/fraud-checkpoint.json` are produced by the `create-loadtest-baselines` workflow (`workflow_dispatch` on `ubuntu-24.04`, `make baseline-loadtests` with `BASELINE_FREEZE_SOURCE=ci`). The workflow opens a PR with those three files and never pushes to `main`. Local `make baseline-loadtests` still builds a worst-of-N envelope under `target/` for debug; it does not write repo-root `baselines/` unless `BASELINE_FREEZE_SOURCE=ci`.

clauses.title: One environment class, recorded on the report
clauses.body: Each dockerized report is stamped with a sidecar `environment` object (report schema stays 6). The class is the recipe, not the VM: `class`: `cypherlite-loadtest-baseline/v1` `os` / `arch` (`linux` / `uname -m` in the run image) `build_image` / `run_image` as `name@sha256:...` `cpus`, `cpu_period_us`, `cpu_quota_us`, `memory` `ops`, `warmup`, `workers` from the report `config` (checkpoint may omit ops/warmup/workers) `runner`: `github-actions:ubuntu-24.04` on the freeze and gate jobs, `local` otherwise Hostname …

clauses.title: Compare is regression vs incompatible
clauses.body: `scripts/compare-loadtest.py` always checks `errors == 0`, logical bytes, schema, and workload kind. Wall-clock ops/s and p99 use the ADR-0046 bands (and `LOADTEST_P99_JITTER_NS=5000000` from `make compare-loadtests`) **only when** baseline and current `environment` objects match. Missing or differing class fields are **incompatible**: In GitHub Actions (`GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`): hard fail (`compare-loadtest: INCOMPATIBLE: ...`). Do not also emit p99 misses for an incomparable pair. Locally: print the same line …

clauses.title: The PR job and the freeze workflow share a runner class
clauses.body: Both use `ubuntu-24.04` (not `ubuntu-latest`) and `BASELINE_RUNNER=github-actions:ubuntu-24.04`. Wall-clock compare is valid only against a freeze from `create-loadtest-baselines` on that class.

clauses.title: No second baseline directory. No auto-widened bands
clauses.body: Flake recourse is not “re-run until lucky” and not `baselines/ci/`. Incompatible means the class changed (image digest, arch, knobs, runner) — re-freeze via the workflow. A matched-class miss is a performance fail (code or residual GHA noise on that class).

clauses.title: One synchronous `Vfs`
clauses.body: WAL segments and snapshot objects go through `Vfs` / `VfsFile` in `cypherlite-storage`. Paths are virtual `/` strings. The commit path stays synchronous (ADR-0014, ADR-0019). Future WASM OPFS uses `FileSystemSyncAccessHandle`, not an async `Database::open`.

clauses.title: VFS owns how bytes are stored; codecs still own what is written
clauses.body: `manifest.json`, Parquet shards, and `graph.json` keep their names and formats (ADR-0050). A later single-file VFS still presents that tree (`wal/00000001.log`, `nodes/…`). That is not a single-file codec.

clauses.title: URI selects the backend
clauses.body: Advertise only schemes `Database::open` can open (ADR-0044). `:memory:` / empty → `MemoryVfs` (not durable; no checkpoint timer). WAL uses the same `MDBWAL01` framing as disk; process exit still discards everything. Filesystem path or `file://…` → `NativeVfs` (default). Layout, `sync_all`, and Windows-safe tmp+close+rename stay as today. Other schemes keep failing until a backend exists. Do not document a URI the engine rejects.

clauses.title: `LOAD CSV` and other user paths stay on the OS filesystem
clauses.body: They are not database files.

clauses.title: Follow-on backends (not this change):
clauses.body: `opfs://<name>`; an object-store VFS (likely feature-gated, or owned by a client implementing embedded Relate, so the default crate still does not pull AWS). Naive object `put` is still not a WAL `fsync` (ADR-0012). Single-file packing is ADR-0074.

clauses.title: TTY only
clauses.body: rustyline is constructed only when stdin is a terminal. Piped stdin still `read_to_string`s the batch; one-shot `QUERY` / `--command` is unchanged.

clauses.title: Editing and in-session history
clauses.body: Emacs bindings (arrow keys, Home/End, Delete, Ctrl-A/E/K/U/W, and the rest of rustyline's default emacs map) and up/down history for the current process. History is **in-memory**: a completed statement (or dot-command) is one history entry. There is no history file and no tab completion.

clauses.title: Prompt contract unchanged
clauses.body: `cypher>` on an empty buffer, ` ...> ` while `input_is_complete` is false. Statements still submit on a terminating top-level `;`; dot-commands still submit on their newline.

clauses.title: Ctrl-C cancels
clauses.body: During a prompt, Ctrl-C clears the pending multi-line buffer and returns to `cypher>`. It does not exit the process. Ctrl-D / EOF keeps today's behavior: execute any non-empty pending buffer, then exit 0. `.quit` / `.exit` still exit immediately.

clauses.title: Fallback
clauses.body: If the editor cannot be constructed, the shell prints a one-line warning to stderr and uses the previous `read_line` loop so a TTY session still works.

clauses.title: No new flags
clauses.body: Line editing is not optional and is not a lifecycle command. Reinstating tab completion or a persistent history file needs a later ADR.

clauses.title: One host file
clauses.body: Dual superblocks, the inode catalog, WAL extents, and snapshot objects live in a single regular file. No sidecar `-wal`/`-shm`, no OS `wal/` directory, no OS `.tmp` files. Virtual `{path}.tmp` is an inode in the same container; `atomic_write` rename is a catalog pointer swap.

clauses.title: URI selection
clauses.body: After stripping `file://`, if the path ends with `.cl` (ASCII, case-insensitive, ignoring a trailing `/` or `\`) the engine opens `BundleVfs`. Every other filesystem URI stays `NativeVfs`. `:memory:` is unchanged. No `bundle://` scheme.

clauses.title: Create vs open
clauses.body: A missing `foo.cl` creates a new container. An existing **directory** named `*.cl` is an error. An existing regular file without bundle magic is an error.

clauses.title: `OpenOptions.wal_dir` is rejected
clauses.body: on `.cl` URIs. A second host WAL would break “one file.”

clauses.title: Durability (ADR-0077)
clauses.body: The container fd uses the same platform barrier as Native (`fdatasync` / `F_BARRIERFSYNC` / `sync_all`). Group-commit `durability_barrier` writes WAL tail pages, then a superblock generation (WAL-tail shortcut: inode id + logical length + file page count). Catalog pages are rewritten only when extents or names change (create, rename, delete, rotate’s new segment). Crash recovery takes the higher valid superblock checksum; unreachable pages join the freelist.

clauses.title: Not in this change:
clauses.body: shrink/compaction, mmap as source of truth, OPFS, object-store VFS.

clauses.title: `full`
clauses.body: — append the WAL record, barrier the accepted group, apply redo, then acknowledge. An acknowledged commit is covered by the platform barrier.

clauses.title: `everysecond`
clauses.body: — append, apply redo, and acknowledge immediately. A background worker barriers all dirty WAL records approximately once per second. A host, OS, or storage failure can lose acknowledged commits from the latest approximately one-second interval. Scheduling delays, a slow barrier, or a storage failure can extend that interval.

clauses.title: `snapshot`
clauses.body: — append, apply redo, and acknowledge without a WAL barrier. Only a completed checkpoint is durable. A crash can lose every acknowledged commit since the latest completed checkpoint. `full` uses the platform's cheapest correct barrier: The checkpoint clock defaults to 300 seconds. `--checkpoint-interval-secs N` tunes the normal `snapshot` loss window; `0` disables only the timed checkpoint. Explicit checkpoints, clean-close checkpointing, and the 64 MiB / 10,000-commit thresholds remain active. WASM has no fsync …

clauses.title: Scope: CLI binary only
clauses.body: Telemetry lives in `crates/cypherlite-cli`. The embedded library (`cypherlite::Database`), the C ABI (`crates/cypherlite-ffi`), and `cypherlite-bolt` never phone home. Bolt may adopt metrics later via a new ADR; nothing here precludes it.

clauses.title: Sink and transport: Mixpanel over the existing `ureq`
clauses.body: Events are sent as `POST https://api.mixpanel.com/track` (default endpoint constant `DEFAULT_ENDPOINT`; the EU-residency host is `https://api-eu.mixpanel.com/track`) with a JSON array body of `{"event": ..., "properties": {"token": ..., "time": ..., "distinct_id": ..., "$insert_id": ..., ...}}` objects. The HTTP client is hand-rolled over the existing workspace `ureq = "3.4"` dependency (already used by `upgrade`, ADR-0069); install-ID and `$insert_id` randomness come from the existing workspace `rand` dependency …

clauses.title: Identity: random install ID, not a machine ID
clauses.body: A random UUID is generated once and persisted as the install ID in state under the XDG config directory — `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/cypherlite/` when `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is set, otherwise `~/.config/cypherlite/`. clauses.title: Events v1 (minimal taxonomy)
clauses.body: Event names carry the `CYPHERLITE-CLI_` app prefix so the tracked surface is explicit in Mixpanel; a future Bolt adoption gets its own prefix (e.g. `CYPHERLITE-BOLT_`) rather than sharing the CLI's. clauses.title: Delivery: non-blocking, best-effort, invisible
clauses.body: Events go onto a bounded channel that drops on overflow; a single background thread drains it with a 2-second HTTP timeout; a bounded `flush()` runs on exit so the CLI is never perceptibly slowed. All telemetry errors are swallowed: nothing on stdout or stderr, exit codes unaffected.

clauses.title: Documentation in the same change

clauses.body: Fetch, extract, and upsert live in `cypherlite-load`. The public `cypherlite` crate does not grow HTTP or Neo4j types. Seeding, authentication, named secrets, and any Bolt fallback stay with clients implementing embedded Relate.

clauses.title: Package
clauses.body: `crates/cypherlite-wasm` builds with `wasm-pack build --target web`. The output package is the distributed artifact.

clauses.body: A `wasm` job runs `cargo check -p cypherlite-storage --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo check -p cypherlite-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, and `wasm-pack build --release --target web`. Failure blocks the merge.

clauses.title: Examples
clauses.body: `examples/wasm-playground/` is an example consumer. It has no privileged status and no separate CI gate beyond the `wasm` job producing a package it can `import`.

clauses.title: Docs
clauses.body: The public surface has `docs/api/wasm/{spec.md,description.md,examples/}` per AGENTS.md §2. The wasm32 build split it depends on is recorded in ADR-0085.

clauses.title: CI gate (from ADR-0084)
clauses.body: The `wasm` job runs `cargo check -p cypherlite-storage --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` and `cargo check -p cypherlite-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` in addition to `wasm-pack build`, so any dep upgrade that breaks wasm32 fails the merge.

The existing catalog-free WAL-tail shortcut is outside this replacement protocol. This does not guarantee recovery of WAL records already present in a live, partially filled physical page if a concurrent/later append tears that page. After …

The referenced map must exist and decode: a missing …

clauses.body: Serialize, exclusively create, write, sync and durably name the new map before publishing `manifest.json`. Do the same for every new Parquet shard per ADR-0089. Put the selector and all shard references in the manifest; its durable atomic replacement is the *only* publication decision. Load the selected snapshot and selected map before streaming WAL replay, which still applies pull identity ops from their original graph commits (ADR-0080). Do not rewrite the legacy `pull-identity.json` after manifest publication. …

clauses.body: A v3 manifest *without* the field continues loading `pull-identity.json` if present, or an empty map if absent; v1/v2 snapshot behavior remains supported. This fallback applies **only** when the selector is absent. A checkpoint of a legacy store writes a new immutable map and selects it with the next manifest; no eager migration on open and no format-version bump. clauses.body: On the first write in an unbarriered group that would modify a physical WAL page reachable through the selected durable superblock (notably an append into a partially filled last page), read that page, allocate a different page outside every selected live range, copy and patch the new page, then map that logical page to the replacement. Split the WAL inode's ordered extent around that logical page if necessary, and coalesce physically adjacent extents where possible. Mark the mapping and logical length …

clauses.title: Publish the mapping before reuse
clauses.body: Write the replacement WAL pages and a fresh v1 catalog containing the ordered extents and new inode length; the catalog-free WAL-tail shortcut is forbidden for a remap. Pass a first host-file contents barrier for the data **and catalog**, then write the alternate v1 superblock (new generation, catalog root/length, file page count, WAL inode/length) and pass a second host-file publication barrier. Never overwrite the prior selected superblock slot or reallocate pages it selects before that second barrier succeeds. …

clauses.title: Fence uncertain writes
clauses.body: An error after a potentially partial page write, catalog write, contents barrier, superblock write or publication barrier fences subsequent writes on that handle until reopen establishes the authoritative valid generation. In particular, never sync partially modified in-memory extents after an earlier failed append and never release quarantined pages on an ambiguous barrier. A checksum-invalid alternate superblock leaves the old generation selected; a fully written alternate superblock around an uncertain second …

clauses.title: Keep format-v1 readers
clauses.body: Continue to open existing v1 bundles without an eager rewrite, including catalogs whose stored WAL length predates the selected superblock's WAL-tail hint (`apply_wal_tail`). New catalog extent mappings and superblock fields use that same v1 representation; new readers recover either valid selected generation. Previously shipped v1 writers can still read these bundles but can append to a selected partial page *unsafely*; this safety guarantee applies only to writers implementing this protocol. Preventing …

clauses.body: Fault-inject the old-page read/copy; torn/failed first, second and third WAL `write_all` (CRC, length, payload); new catalog write; contents barrier; torn/fully written alternate superblock; and publication barrier before/after physical completion. Reopen each case and assert old raw page bytes and old WAL records survive pre-publication faults, and that a successfully selected new generation replays the new record exactly once. clauses.title: One pre-append acceptance boundary
clauses.body: While holding the serialization boundary covering WAL order and the graph state being checked, select the group's candidate slots in queue order with ADR-0019's existing conflict checks against the graph and earlier eligible slots and the existing per-slot memory-capacity reservation policy. Conflict and capacity errors stay per waiter; those slots do not enter the WAL preflight. Assign the would-be commit timestamps and LSNs in that same order, rejecting invalid timestamps, LSN overflow, unsupported IDs …

clauses.title: Bound the preflight rather than buffering a group
clauses.body: Use the exact WAL serde representation twice: first serialize each candidate to a byte-counting, limit-enforcing sink that stops at 64 MiB + 1 without retaining JSON, then serialize that same immutable candidate at append through the same encoder with a 64 MiB bound. Distinguish a size-limit error from a serde error. The append still needs only one bounded payload at a time to compute its CRC and frame it; never retain a `Vec` of encoded payloads for the whole group. Track only the touched IDs/catalog state needed …

clauses.title: Replica before-sync applicability
clauses.body: At `Database::apply_replicated`, under the same stable serialization boundary, preflight the exact record's timestamp, ID range, LSN, encoded size/serde result and full ordered redo applicability through that same Graph validator before WAL append or sync. `CreateRel` must see both live endpoints after all preceding operations in its record; a missing endpoint or one deleted earlier in the redo is a typed pre-append rejection, with unchanged LSN/WAL bytes and prior data reopenable. A valid mixed record, including …

clauses.title: Uncertain physical publication and a shared fence
clauses.body: The all-or-nothing rejection promise applies to *deterministic preflight errors before any append*. Remember the **last safe commit horizon**: the LSN and timestamp of the last *contiguous* WAL prefix whose barrier was confirmed and whose redo was fully applied, before this attempted group/replica publication (not the numerically highest timestamp of any later record). Once the first frame write is attempted, a write or sync failure (including an error reported after a barrier), an unexpected apply failure, or a …

clauses.body: `redo/mod.rs` `validate_ids`'s inner `check` calls `cypherlite_core::validate_persisted_id`, so `Wal::validate_redo_ids` and replay inherit the same rule.

clauses.title: graph/mod.rs checked_persisted_id becomes a thin wrapper: it calls the
clauses.body: `graph/mod.rs` `checked_persisted_id` becomes a thin wrapper: it calls the canonical predicate, then returns `Ok(id + 1)` for its callers' `fetch_max` allocator advance. The predicate stays a boolean range check; the `+1` allocator step is graph-local behavior and is not folded into the shared predicate.

clauses.title: wal.rs's pub(crate) validate_persisted_id is deleted; the snapshot
clauses.body: `wal.rs`'s `pub(crate) validate_persisted_id` is deleted; the snapshot pull-identity sites call the core predicate directly.

clauses.title: codec/parquet.rs's valid_id is deleted in favour of the core predicate
clauses.body: `codec/parquet.rs`'s `valid_id` is deleted in favour of the core predicate at its write and read call sites.

clauses.title: codec/json.rs's inline .any() sentinel checks are replaced by the core
clauses.body: `codec/json.rs`'s inline `.any()` sentinel checks are replaced by the core predicate (or a thin bulk helper that calls it per ID); the negative next-counter guards remain their own next-ID check. **Why `cypherlite-core` is the home.** Both `cypherlite-storage` and `cypherlite-executor` already depend on `cypherlite-core`; `cypherlite-core` depends on neither. `NodeId`/`RelId` are defined in core, so the range rule that constrains them belongs beside its types. `cypherlite-storage` gets a single-ID predicate …

clauses.title: Acquire before accessing database contents
clauses.body: Every persistent `Database::open`/`open_with` (and storage URI parse used to open a store) takes nonblocking exclusive OS ownership during URI parsing, before `BundleVfs::open_or_create` can initialize or load a bundle, before codec resolution, and before Native manifest, WAL, or snapshot access. Only the minimal creation of missing directory components and the lock target itself may precede acquisition; no WAL or bundle bytes may be initialized, truncated, or recovered first. A failed acquisition must close its …

clauses.title: Native identity, including WAL overrides
clauses.body: Create/open a stable regular `.cypherlite.lock` file inside the Native database root, then acquire its exclusive lock. The marker filename is unique to CypherLite: unrelated `.lock` files created by other tools (for example a `pytest-0/.lock` in a parent directory) are not database identities and must never be treated as an ancestor or nested-owner marker. Only `.cypherlite.lock` names a CypherLite identity. Never unlink or replace this file on ordinary close: a newly created inode could admit a second owner while …

clauses.title: Bundle identity
clauses.body: For `.cl`, open the existing regular host file for read/write without truncation, or atomically create a missing one with `create_new`; acquire the exclusive lock on that **same file handle** before handing it to bundle initialization/load. Retain the locked handle (or a clone sharing its lock ownership) inside the bundle/lease. Do not reopen by path for initialization. `OpenOptions.wal_dir` remains rejected for `.cl` (ADR-0074). There is no bundle lock sidecar, OS WAL directory, or other additional host file.

clauses.title: Aliases and lifetime
clauses.body: Resolve relative paths and supported existing symlink aliases to their actual filesystem targets before opening the stable lock file or bundle file; verify targets are directories/regular files as appropriate. Existing hard links to a bundle, `file://`, and relative/absolute spellings must contend on file identity, not spelling. Dangling or cyclic symlinks and links to a nonmatching file type fail without creating through the link. Open the resolved lock target without following a symlink in its final component …

clauses.title: Private new paths, unchanged existing paths
clauses.body: On Unix create every newly made Native database directory (root, `wal`, shard directories, and any new parent components made for the database) with mode `0700`; create new Native database files (including `.cypherlite.lock`, WAL, snapshot, and temporary files) and the `.cl` host file with mode `0600`. Apply the explicit creation mode even with a permissive umask; a restrictive umask may remove permissions, and such an open may then fail. Do not silently `chmod` existing paths or migrate their permissions. …

clauses.title: Distinct public contention error
clauses.body: Add `cypherlite_core::Error::Locked(String)` (display: `storage locked: {0}`), visible as `cypherlite::Error::Locked` from `Database::open` and other public storage-open paths. Use it only when nonblocking acquisition reports actual contention, whether in the same process or another process, for the root, WAL directory, or bundle. Permission failures, unsupported locking, corrupt files, bad path types, and other I/O errors remain `Error::Io`/`Error::Storage` as appropriate; do not map every lock syscall failure to …

clauses.title: Exclusive, unpredictable temporary name
clauses.body: For each `atomic_write`, choose a fresh name in the *destination's containing virtual directory*, derived from the destination only as a recognizable prefix and suffixed with at least 128 bits from an OS-backed cryptographically secure random source. Never use the fixed `{path}.tmp`, timestamps, process IDs, or a counter as the sole source of uniqueness. Attempt exclusive create without truncation or following an existing final-component symlink. Native uses `OpenOptions::create_new(true)` (and mode `0600` for new …

clauses.title: Write, publish, clean up
clauses.body: Create destination parents as needed, write all bytes to the owned temp, sync that temp file, and **close its write handle before rename**, including on Windows. Rename within the same containing directory, replacing the destination as one VFS namespace operation; do not unlink the destination first. On a pre-publish write, sync, close, or rename failure, attempt to remove only the temp successfully created by this operation, after closing its handle. Surface the original failure (and cleanup failure if any) …

clauses.title: Native namespace persistence
clauses.body: On Linux and macOS, after the successful same-directory rename, open the containing host directory and `sync_all` it; propagate any open/sync failure. This is in addition to syncing and closing the temp *before* rename. If `atomic_write` created new parent directories, sync each newly created directory's parent, from the first newly created component through the destination parent, so the new path components are also durable before reporting success. Do not promise this sequence for a filesystem that rejects …

clauses.title: Backend-specific persistence
clauses.body: Memory retains the same virtual replacement behavior with exclusive temp names but has no host sync or crash-durability guarantee; its parent-sync operation is a no-op. Bundle keeps both the temp and destination as virtual inodes in its *single* host file (ADR-0074). Its temp-file sync and rename use the existing host-file catalog/superblock durability barriers: the rename persists the catalog pointer swap, so no separate host directory entry is renamed or synced for each virtual replacement. Bundle's virtual …

clauses.title: Post-rename sync failure
clauses.body: A failed Native directory sync returns an I/O error even though the new bytes may already be visible. The old name cannot safely be restored and the caller must not infer either old or new data after a crash from that failed call. Retain the synced new destination in place and let recovery/readback establish current state; do not silently report success or automatically retry a potentially non-idempotent operation. Tests must fault-inject each stage and verify this ordering and distinction, as well as collision …

clauses.title: Database::memory_usage(&self) -> Result<(u64, Option<u64>)>. Acquire
clauses.body: `Database::memory_usage(&self) -> Result<(u64, Option<u64>)>`. Acquire `read_guard()?`, then return the live logical bytes and the configured cap exactly as before (`None` limit means unlimited). A poisoned/fenced handle returns `Error::Storage` instead of `(0, None)`.

clauses.title: Connection::pull_lookup(&self, source: &str, kind: PullKind,
clauses.body: `Connection::pull_lookup(&self, source: &str, kind: PullKind, remote_id: &str) -> Result<Option<i64>>`. Acquire `read_guard()?`, then run the existing lookup logic unchanged; `Ok(None)` keeps meaning "no live mapping", while a poisoned handle is `Err`. All in-tree callers are updated in the same change: binaries and loadtests propagate with `?` (or map into their own error type), tests and examples use `.unwrap()`/`?`. The public docs under `docs/api/rust/` record the new signatures and error contract.

clauses.title: cargo build -p cypherlite-wasm --lib --profile release-wasm --target
clauses.body: `cargo build -p cypherlite-wasm --lib --profile release-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` — a new profile in the workspace `Cargo.toml` that inherits `release` and adds `opt-level = "z"`, `lto = "fat"`, `codegen-units = 1`, `panic = "abort"`, `strip = "symbols"`. It is only referenced by the wasm build entry, so native builds are unaffected.

clauses.body: `wasm-bindgen --target web` on the resulting `.wasm`, matched to the `wasm-bindgen` crate version in `Cargo.lock` (currently 0.2.128).

It takes a `--mode` flag: `--mode release` (default) runs the full size-tuned pipeline above. Used by CI, `make build-wasm`, the playground's `build:wasm:release` npm script, and the Pages deploy workflow — the workflow runs it explicitly before `npm run build`, so shipped playground bundles always contain the small wasm. `npm run build` itself does not run cargo, so local Vite-only iterations stay fast. `--mode dev` uses …

clauses.title: A bundle is a named Cargo feature that only enables
clauses.body: A bundle is a named Cargo feature that only enables other features. Every feature only **adds** capability. There are no negative (`no-*`) features, so Cargo's feature unification can never remove something another dependent relies on.

clauses.title: full is the default feature. A plain cargo build or
clauses.body: `full` is the `default` feature. A plain `cargo build` or `cargo install` produces exactly today's binary.

clauses.title: Release artifacts (GitHub releases, install script, Homebrew) stay
clauses.body: Release artifacts (GitHub releases, install script, Homebrew) stay `full`-only for now. Smaller bundles are built from source (`cargo build -p cypherlite-cli --no-default-features --features agent`). Publishing other bundles as artifacts needs its own ADR.

clauses.title: A command word whose feature is compiled out is still
clauses.body: A command word whose feature is compiled out is **still recognized as a command**. As the first argument (not after `--`, not `./`-prefixed), it prints `Error: the '<command>' command is not included in this build of cypherlite` to stderr and exits with code **2**. The argv grammar from ADR-0069 is therefore identical in every bundle: `cypherlite pull` never silently opens a database named `pull`, and `./pull` or `-- pull` is the escape in every build.

clauses.title: The hand-written --help text lists only the commands compiled into
clauses.body: The hand-written `--help` text lists only the commands compiled into the binary. `docs/api/cli/spec.md` documents every command with the feature that provides it, plus the bundle table below, so a given build's `--help` matches the spec for that feature set.

clauses.title: CI builds, runs clippy on, and tests every named bundle
clauses.body: CI builds, runs clippy on, and tests every named bundle (`full`, `agent`, `minimal`), not only the default. Tests for a gated command are gated on the same feature. The compiled-out path (rule 4) is tested in the bundles that exclude the command.

clauses.title: Later engine-level features (for example Parquet checkpoints or a .cl
clauses.body: Later engine-level features (for example Parquet checkpoints or a `.cl` bundle VFS) follow the same rules. Each gets its own ADR that names the feature, what it gates, and which bundles include it. ### CLI features A shared dependency (`ureq`) is linked when any feature that needs it is on. ### CLI bundles The core query-engine run (flags, output modes, params, storage knobs) is never gated; every bundle can run queries against in-memory and persistent databases.

clauses.title: New stores default to JSON
clauses.body: The default for *new* stores becomes a function of the build: Parquet when the codec is compiled in, JSON otherwise.

clauses.title: An absent `codec` field still means Parquet
clauses.body: Serde decoding of `manifest.json` stops using `SnapshotCodecKind::default()` and gets an explicit default function that always returns `Parquet`. A pre-ADR-0050 Parquet store therefore never decodes as JSON, and an empty-graph Parquet store is never silently converted.

clauses.title: Fail closed at open
clauses.body: A store whose resolved codec is Parquet (directory or `.cl` bundle), in a build without the codec, fails in `Database::open` with a typed `Storage` error. The message names the missing feature: `parquet snapshot codec is not compiled into this build (enable the "parquet" feature)`. It does not fail lazily at first checkpoint.

clauses.title: No silent fallback for explicit requests
clauses.body: Asking for Parquet through `OpenOptions.snapshot_codec`, `CYPHERLITE_SNAPSHOT_FORMAT=parquet`, or the CLI `--snapshot-format parquet` in a build without the codec returns the same error. The CLI `--help` lists only the codecs compiled into the binary (ADR-0104 rule 5). ### Pull does not require Parquet Pull identity is codec-neutral since ADR-0106, so `cypherlite-load`'s normal dependency does not enable `cypherlite/parquet` and the CLI `pull` feature is only `dep:cypherlite-load`. The `agent` bundle (`skill` …

clauses.title: Inline field
clauses.body: Add an optional `pull_identity` field to the JSON `GraphData` envelope in `graph.json`: … `PullIdentityEntry` is the existing `cypherlite_executor` type (`source`, `kind` as lowercase `node`/`rel`, `remote_id`, `local_id`). No new wire type and no format-version bump.

clauses.title: Dump
clauses.body: JSON `dump` writes `Graph::pull_identity_entries()` into the field as part of the same full `graph.json` rewrite. An empty map writes nothing.

clauses.title: Load
clauses.body: JSON `load` restores the field with `Graph::restore_pull_identity` before WAL replay. A missing field is an empty map. WAL `PullIdentityPut` replay is unchanged (ADR-0080).

clauses.title: Validation
clauses.body: Every `local_id` is checked with `PullIdentityEntry::validate_local_ids` on dump and on load, the same shared check the Parquet path uses. Entries are part of `graph.json` and share its existing read path; no separate size envelope is added.

clauses.title: Parquet unchanged
clauses.body: The ADR-0092 manifest-selected sidecar, its selector validation, legacy fallback and cleanup stay as they are. The JSON `manifest.json` envelope is unchanged.

clauses.title: Record identity when validating
clauses.body: `CsvPolicy::target` returns the canonical path together with the physical `FileIdentity` observed at validation time. The existing rejections (out-of-root canonical target, non-regular file, malformed URL) are unchanged; recording an identity is added to the same inspection, not a second separate check.

clauses.title: Open without following the final component
clauses.body: `CsvPolicy::read` opens the recorded canonical path through `std::fs::OpenOptions` via the shared `cypherlite_core::file_identity::nofollow` helper, whose Unix arm adds `libc::O_NOFOLLOW` to `custom_flags` and whose Windows arm adds `FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT`, so a symlink substituted at the final component is refused at open on Unix, and opened as the link itself on Windows where the identity check in (3) denies it.

clauses.title: Verify the opened handle, then read
clauses.body: Before the bounded read, require `cypherlite_core::file_identity::of_file(&file)` to equal the identity recorded in (1), and require the same `fstat` to report a regular file. A mismatch, a non-regular opened object, or an identity-query failure denies the read. The bounded `limit + 1` read and the per-statement memo are unchanged.

clauses.title: Keep denials generic
clauses.body: Any mismatch denies with the existing generic typed `LOAD CSV file unavailable` error; no path, canonical path, errno, or OS error text is added.

clauses.title: Share the identity primitive
clauses.body: Move `file_identity` from `cypherlite-storage` to `cypherlite-core` as a `pub` module. `cypherlite-core` gains a `cfg(unix)` `libc` target dependency and a `cfg(windows)` `windows-sys` target dependency (0.61, `Win32_Foundation` and `Win32_Storage_FileSystem`); `cypherlite-storage` drops its `windows-sys` target dependency and keeps `libc` for its own no-follow opens. The `O_NOFOLLOW` open in `CsvPolicy::read` reuses `cypherlite_core::file_identity::nofollow`, so `cypherlite-executor` needs no `libc` dependency of …

clauses.title: rustls performs no revocation fetching
clauses.body: There is no first-class, upstream-supported revocation client for the rustls path `ureq` uses, so "enable revocation" is not a configuration toggle — it is new code and a new dependency.

clauses.title: Browsers abandoned live OCSP
clauses.body: Live OCSP checking soft-fails open in practice, and the industry moved to CRLite and short-lived certificates precisely because online revocation checks are unreliable and privacy hostile. Requiring what browsers no longer require would overstate the protection.

clauses.title: Short-lived managed certificates shrink the exposure window
clauses.body: The endpoints in question (GitHub releases API, Mixpanel, the configured Query API host) use short-lived managed certificates, so a revoked-but-unexpired certificate is a narrow window.

clauses.title: The endpoints are pinned by configuration
clauses.body: These are not arbitrary URLs pulled from user input: the GitHub releases API and Mixpanel hosts are fixed, and the Query API host comes from operator-supplied `NEO4J_URI` configuration.

clauses.title: A network-position attacker can block revocation signals anyway
clauses.body: An adversary able to serve a revoked certificate is already on the network path and can equally suppress CRL/OCSP fetches (or block them outright), so revocation checking does not remove that adversary's capability. Only revocation is out of scope. Expired, self-signed, untrusted-CA, hostname-mismatch, and incomplete-chain certificates remain rejected by the `ureq` defaults, and no client, trust-store, or pinning change is made here.

clauses.title: Only a failed checksum is a torn tail
clauses.body: At the active segment's physical EOF, a complete final frame that fails its CRC stays a tolerated relaxed append (ADR-0086 §1, ADR-0077). A complete frame whose CRC matches but whose payload does not decode is corruption in every segment and position. Open fails with a storage error that names the segment and says the record may have been written by a newer CypherLite. Nothing is trimmed. `records_after` applies the same rule.

clauses.title: Check the version before WAL recovery
clauses.body: `open_store` reads and validates the snapshot's format marker before `Wal::open`: the Parquet manifest's `format_version`, and the JSON `graph.json` `value_encoding` and `read_only` guard. An unsupported value fails open with the existing typed error and leaves every WAL segment untouched. A store without a snapshot yet (a fresh directory, an empty bundle, `:memory:`) opens as today.

clauses.title: Golden stores
clauses.body: Commit small stores in the current format under `testdata/stores/`: a Parquet directory, a JSON directory and a `.cl` bundle, each with a checkpoint and a WAL tail. Tests open each one, assert its contents, checkpoint, and assert the result is still manifest v3 (or `value_encoding: 2`) with `MDBWAL01` segments. Later format ADRs add to this set instead of replacing it.

clauses.title: Signature format
clauses.body: Sign the `SHA256SUMS` manifest with `ssh-keygen -Y sign` and verify with `ssh-keygen -Y verify`, i.e. the OpenSSH SSHSIG format. The key is **Ed25519** and the signature namespace is **`cypherlite-release`**.

clauses.title: One keypair, one secret
clauses.body: There is exactly one release signing keypair. The private key is an unencrypted OpenSSH private key stored only as the GitHub Actions secret **`RELEASE_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY`**. The corresponding public key is pinned in the source, in **both** `upgrade_cmd.rs` and `install.sh`; verification never fetches the key from the release.

clauses.title: CI signs the manifest
clauses.body: In `release.yml`, after `SHA256SUMS` is generated, a step runs `ssh-keygen -Y sign -f <keyfile> -n cypherlite-release SHA256SUMS` and publishes the resulting **`SHA256SUMS.sig`** as a release asset. The key is written to a `umask 077` temporary file and removed on exit. The step fails when `RELEASE_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` is unset, so a release cannot ship unsigned.

clauses.title: `install.sh` verifies before checksumming
clauses.body: The installer downloads `SHA256SUMS` and `SHA256SUMS.sig` and verifies the signature with the stock **`/usr/bin/ssh-keygen`** (`ssh-keygen -Y verify`), which is present on macOS and near-universal on desktop Linux, **before** the existing checksum step. No tool is installed and no network fetch of the key occurs.

clauses.title: The Rust binary verifies before checksumming
clauses.body: `upgrade_cmd.rs` verifies `SHA256SUMS` against its pinned public key using the RustCrypto **`ssh-key`** crate (0.6, features `alloc` + `ed25519`, MSRV 1.65) and only then checks the downloaded binary against the verified manifest.

clauses.title: Fail closed
clauses.body: If the `SHA256SUMS.sig` asset is missing, the signature is invalid or does not match the pinned key, or the verifier is unavailable, the install/upgrade aborts and the existing binary is left untouched. There is no "signature optional" or warning-only path.

clauses.title: Durable atomic replacement
clauses.body: `atomic_file::write_atomic` must `sync_all` the staged file before the rename, and on unix fsync the containing directory after a successful rename, so the verified bytes are durable before the operation reports success.

clauses.title: Key custody and rotation
clauses.body: Custody of the private key (protected Actions secret, no local copy) and the rotation procedure are documented in `RELEASING.md`.

clauses.title: Three fixed namespaces
clauses.body: Every store has exactly these. None can be created, dropped or renamed, and names match case-insensitively.

clauses.title: Administration commands follow CE
clauses.body: These are supported: `SHOW DATABASE[S] [name]`, `SHOW DEFAULT DATABASE`, `SHOW HOME DATABASE`, and `ALTER DATABASE <name> [IF EXISTS] SET DEFAULT LANGUAGE CYPHER 5|25` as the only clause and without `WAIT`. Every other database administration command fails with `UnsupportedAdministrationCommand`: `Unsupported administration command: <statement>`. The statement is echoed verbatim, without a leading `CYPHER n`. This covers: `CREATE [OR REPLACE] [COMPOSITE] DATABASE` and `DROP [COMPOSITE] DATABASE`; every other …

clauses.title: `USE` routes a statement
clauses.body: A statement targets the namespace named by its `USE` clause, or else the connection's session namespace (ADR-0117, ADR-0118). Graph references resolve before execution: A static name must be one of the fixed namespaces. `graph.byElementId(<string>)` resolves through the element id scheme in (7); an id that names no namespace fails as in Neo4j (42NA7). An unknown name fails with `DatabaseNotFound`: `Graph not found: <name>` (GQLSTATUS 42N00). `graph.byName`, `graph.names` and `graph.propertiesByName` fail with …

clauses.title: Namespace rules
clauses.body: `system`: anything other than SHOW commands, supported administration commands and standalone procedure calls (`CALL … YIELD … RETURN`) fails with `SemanticError` and CE's 42N17 text, `The following unsupported clauses were used: <clauses>. …`. The existing `USE system` rules for composing SHOW commands stay. `system_ontologies`: any write fails with `WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase`: `No write operations are allowed on this database. The database is in read-only mode.` (GQLSTATUS 42N18). Writes include data …

clauses.title: Transactions read any namespace and write only `neo4j`
clauses.body: This is Neo4j's query-router rule (read many, write one); `neo4j` is the only namespace Cypher can write. `BEGIN` pins `neo4j` as it does today and also captures the current `system_ontologies` graph, so every statement in the transaction reads one consistent snapshot of both. A connection's session namespace changes only between transactions.

clauses.title: SHOW output is real
clauses.body: `SHOW DATABASES` returns the three rows with: `currentStatus` and `requestedStatus` set to `online`; `access` as in the table in (1); `default` and `home` true only for `neo4j`; empty `aliases` and `constituents`; the stored `defaultLanguage`. `SHOW DEFAULT DATABASE` and `SHOW HOME DATABASE` return `neo4j`, and an unknown name returns no rows. `db.info()` reports the namespace the statement targets.

clauses.title: Element ids name their namespace
clauses.body: The format is `<kind>:cypherlite[.<namespace>]:<n|r><id>`. `neo4j` keeps the bare `cypherlite` segment, so `4:cypherlite:n5` and every id already handed out keep their meaning. `system_ontologies` uses `cypherlite.system_ontologies`, for example `4:cypherlite.system_ontologies:n5`. `system` has no elements and no segment. `db.nameFromElementId` maps the middle segment to the namespace name and keeps today's error for anything else. Ids keep exactly three `:`-separated parts.

clauses.title: Settings stay in the existing catalog
clauses.body: A namespace's default language stays in `TheaterData.databases` and the `PutDatabase` redo op; neither the WAL nor the snapshot format changes. Entries for other names, written by earlier `CREATE DATABASE` calls or by an older binary, are ignored on load and replay and left out of the next checkpoint image. A fixed namespace without an entry defaults to `CYPHER 25`. As today, the default language is stored and shown but does not select the parser version. **Later references**: ADR-0276 moves the table out of …

clauses.title: Errors
clauses.body: Messages match CE's text. The engine gains the error kinds `UnsupportedAdministrationCommand` and `WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase`; `DatabaseNotFound` already exists. Bolt keeps ADR-0260's codes, so these errors reach drivers as `CypherLite.Error` with CE's message. **Later references**: ADR-0307 replaces those codes with Neo4j status codes: `DatabaseNotFound` is `Neo.ClientError.Database.DatabaseNotFound` (a typed engine variant now), the other CE errors `Neo.ClientError.Statement.SemanticError`; CE's messages are …

clauses.title: Engine shape
clauses.body: `Shared` holds one slot per namespace: `neo4j` is today's live graph, `system` an empty graph, and `system_ontologies` an immutable graph that is replaced as a whole (ADR-0120). The planner lifts the static `USE` target into the plan, and the connection resolves it and enforces the rules above. Executor operators do not change. Registered procedures and the LOAD CSV policy (ADR-0081) move from the graph to the store, and the memory limit (ADR-0042) covers every namespace. `pull` (ADR-0080) keeps writing `neo4j`.

clauses.title: Default
clauses.body: Connecting without a namespace keeps today's behaviour: the session namespace is `neo4j`.

clauses.title: Rust
clauses.body: Add `Database::connect_namespace(&self, name: &str) -> Result<Connection>`, `Connection::set_namespace(&mut self, name: &str) -> Result<()>` and `Connection::namespace(&self) -> &str`. `set_namespace` fails while a transaction is open: `Cannot change the namespace while a transaction is open.`
