clauses.body: Add two functions without changing any existing signature: … The bundled handle API (`cypherlite_open`) is unchanged and selects namespaces with `USE`. The JS, Java and Go clients expose `connect(namespace)` and `setNamespace(name)` over these two functions only.

clauses.title: WASM

clauses.title: Unknown names

clauses.title: Bolt
clauses.body: For each auto-commit `RUN` and each `BEGIN`, the session namespace is the extra's `db`, or `neo4j` when `db` is absent, `null` or `""`. It does not carry over from an earlier request. A `RUN` inside an explicit transaction carries no `db`, per the Bolt specification, and uses the namespace chosen at `BEGIN`. An unknown `db` produces a `FAILURE` with the text from (6) and the code `CypherLite.Error` (ADR-0260). The final `SUCCESS` of `PULL` or `DISCARD` includes `db`, the namespace the query ran in. `HELLO` is …

clauses.title: Flag
clauses.body: `--namespace NAME` sets the session namespace for the run. Every statement without `USE` targets it, in one-shot (`-c` or a positional query), piped and interactive use. `NAME` is `neo4j` (the default), `system` or `system_ontologies`, matched case-insensitively.

clauses.title: Validation
clauses.body: Any other value fails before the store is opened, the same way other invalid flag values do: `Error: invalid --namespace: unknown namespace '<name>' (expected neo4j, system or system_ontologies)`, followed by the usage text on stderr, with exit status 2.

clauses.title: Scope
clauses.body: The flag is part of every query run, so it is not a Cargo feature and exists in the `full`, `agent` and `minimal` bundles (ADR-0104). `pull` does not accept it, because `pull` always writes `neo4j`; it reports `--namespace` as an unknown flag.

clauses.title: The document is the source of truth
clauses.body: The stored state is the validated ontology JSON for `neo4j`, kept verbatim. There is at most one.

clauses.title: The graph is derived
clauses.body: The `system_ontologies` graph is built from the document at open and after each committed set or drop, and then replaces the previous graph atomically. Statements and transactions keep the graph they captured (ADR-0116 §5). The build is deterministic: node and relationship ids follow document order, so element ids (ADR-0116 §7) stay the same across restarts and change only when the ontology is replaced. The derived graph carries a fixed graph type that describes the ontology model.

clauses.title: WAL operations
clauses.body: Two new store-level redo ops, which are not graph ops: `OntologySet { database, spec }` and `OntologyDrop { database }`. The document is limited to 16 MiB, the ADR-0086 object envelope, and the limit is checked before the commit is written.

clauses.title: WAL segment magic `MDBWAL02`
clauses.body: The frame layout does not change. A segment created while the store holds an ontology, committed or still pending in the WAL, starts with `MDBWAL02`. Other segments start with `MDBWAL01`. When an ontology op commits while the active segment is `MDBWAL01`, the WAL first rotates to a fresh `MDBWAL02` segment. An ontology op in an `MDBWAL01` segment is corruption. A short header repaired under ADR-0086 §1 becomes `MDBWAL01`. Such a segment holds no frames, and ontology ops are never appended to it. Native ownership …

clauses.title: Parquet snapshot
clauses.body: The manifest gains an optional `ontology_path` that selects one immutable `ontology/<128-bit-hex>.json` object. The object is written and published under the pull-identity rules of ADR-0092 and ADR-0089: exclusive create, sync and a durable name before the manifest, and old objects retired only after publication. A manifest with `ontology_path` has `format_version: 4`; one without it stays at 3. Readers accept 1 to 4.

clauses.title: JSON snapshot
clauses.body: `graph.json` gains an optional inline `ontology` string, for the same reasons ADR-0106 inlines pull identity. A `graph.json` that carries it is written with `value_encoding: 3`, which means value encoding 2 plus the ontology field; one without it keeps 2. The JSON `manifest.json` envelope is unchanged.

clauses.title: Bundles
clauses.body: A `.cl` store keeps the ontology object at a virtual path. The bundle container and its single WAL stream are unchanged (ADR-0074).

clauses.title: The format follows the content
clauses.body: A store that never sets an ontology stays byte-for-byte in today's format and readable by older binaries. Once a store holds an ontology, older binaries fail at the `MDBWAL02` segment, the v4 manifest or `value_encoding: 3`, each time before modifying that data. After the ontology is dropped and a checkpoint publishes, new segments are `MDBWAL01` again. Once the `MDBWAL02` segments are recycled and the manifest is back at v3, older binaries can open the store again.

clauses.title: Signatures follow Neo4j
clauses.body: `db.ontology.set(database :: STRING, ontology :: STRING)` validates the document against a supported Ontology Spec version and replaces the stored ontology. A newer spec version fails, naming the highest supported version. `db.ontology.get(database :: STRING) :: (ontology :: STRING)` returns the stored document unchanged, or `null` when none is set. `db.ontology.drop(database :: STRING)` removes it. Dropping when none is set succeeds. `db.ontology.apply(database :: STRING)` converts the stored ontology to a graph …

clauses.title: One database
clauses.body: `database` must name `neo4j`, matched case-insensitively. An unknown name fails with `DatabaseNotFound` and `Database does not exist. Database name: '<name>'.`. `system` and `system_ontologies` fail with `Ontologies can only be stored for the user database 'neo4j'.`

clauses.title: Transactions
clauses.body: `set` and `drop` run only in implicit (auto-commit) transactions. Inside an explicit transaction they fail with `'db.ontology.set' can only be executed in an implicit transaction, but tried to execute in an explicit transaction.` (or the same text naming `drop`). The wording follows Neo4j's error for `CALL { … } IN TRANSACTIONS`. A statement that calls `set` or `drop` may not write anything else. Otherwise it fails with Neo4j's `Writing to more than one database per transaction is not allowed.` (42N03). `get` …

clauses.title: No privileges
clauses.body: Any caller may run every procedure. The proposal's `EXECUTE BOOSTED` grants and property-based access rules do not apply.

clauses.title: The mapping follows Neo4j
clauses.body: The document-to-graph mapping and the ontology graph type implement Neo4j's published mapping for Ontology Spec v1. That includes the `ontology` property naming the database on every node and relationship, so queries against `system_ontologies` work the same in both products. CypherLite ships no mapping of its own, and implementing these procedures waits until Neo4j publishes it.

clauses.title: Always built
clauses.body: The procedures are part of the Cypher surface in every build: all CLI bundles, the Rust crate, the language bindings, Bolt and WASM. They are not a Cargo feature. The mapping lives in a new engine crate, `cypherlite/cypherlite-ontology`, that `cypherlite` always depends on. That follows ADR-0103's R1, and the crate adds no heavy dependency (R6).

clauses.title: Listed like other procedures
clauses.body: `SHOW PROCEDURES` lists them with their signatures and modes.

clauses.title: One shared composite action
clauses.body: A single composite action at **`.github/actions/macos-notarize/action.yml`** performs signing and notarization. Both darwin legs of the `cli` job invoke it; there is no duplicated signing logic per leg.

clauses.title: Per-arch codesign
clauses.body: For each artifact the action codesigns the binary with `codesign` using a **Developer ID Application** identity, with **`--force`**, **`--options runtime`** (hardened runtime), and **`--timestamp`**. Each architecture is signed separately on its own runner; there is no post-hoc `lipo` merge or universal binary.

clauses.title: Zip and notarize
clauses.body: The action zips the signed binary and submits it with **`xcrun notarytool submit --wait`**, so the release fails if the submission is rejected rather than publishing an un-notarized binary.

clauses.title: Invocation point
clauses.body: The action runs in the darwin legs **after the "Rename binary" step and before `actions/upload-artifact`**, so only signed, notarized bytes ever leave the runner. The `create-release` job still checksums and SSHSIG-signs the published assets unchanged.

clauses.title: Credentials come from repository secrets
clauses.body: , with the same names used by the sibling `neo4j-cli` repository: `MACOS_SIGN_P12`, `MACOS_SIGN_PASSWORD`, `MACOS_NOTARY_KEY_ID`, `MACOS_NOTARY_ISSUER_ID`, and `MACOS_NOTARY_KEY`. The action imports the `.p12` into a temporary keychain and removes it afterwards.

clauses.title: Online Gatekeeper check only; no stapling
clauses.body: Notarization is verified by Gatekeeper over the network at first launch. The action does not staple a notarization ticket.

clauses.title: Fail closed
clauses.body: If credentials are missing or signing or notarization fails, the darwin leg fails and no artifact is uploaded; an unsigned macOS binary cannot ship from a green release.

clauses.title: Trigger
clauses.body: `.github/workflows/release-notes.yml` runs on `release: [published]` — the event `release.yml` already fires through `softprops/action-gh-release`, and the same event `update-website.yml` consumes — and additionally on `workflow_dispatch` for a dry run.

clauses.title: Runner: `opencode run` (OpenCode V2 CLI)
clauses.body: The workflow installs a pinned OpenCode release using the tarball-plus-sha256 pattern from `.github/workflows/opencode-review-reusable.yml`: a pinned `OPENCODE_VERSION`, a `curl` download of `opencode-linux-x64.tar.gz` from `opencode.ai/files/bin`, and `sha256sum -c` against a pinned `OPENCODE_SHA256` before extraction, so a swapped or corrupted tarball aborts the install before anything runs. Authentication is a `FIREWORKS_API_KEY` repository secret (ADR-0258).

clauses.title: Model: `fireworks-ai/accounts/fireworks/routers/kimi-latest`
clauses.body: This full path is a real models.dev catalog key under the `fireworks-ai` provider. ADR-0258's caveat — that the bare `kimi-latest` shorthand does not resolve on a cold runner — applies to that shorthand, not to this fully-qualified `accounts/fireworks/routers/…` catalog path; release notes are not a merge-gating check, so tracking the router's current Kimi is acceptable here where ADR-0258 pinned `kimi-k3` for the review gate.

clauses.title: Prompt file: `.github/prompts/release-notes.md`
clauses.body: The generation prompt is maintained in-repo and versioned with the workflow, alongside the other `.github/prompts/` files.

clauses.title: Agent artifacts: target/release-notes/notes.md and
clauses.body: The agent writes the markdown notes and the Slack message payload to these paths; the workflow reads them back to publish, so the publishing steps do not re-invoke the model.

clauses.title: Graceful Slack skip
clauses.body: If `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` is unset, the workflow logs a skip and continues without posting to Slack; the missing webhook is not a failure and never fails the release-notes run.

clauses.title: Idempotent GitHub release update
clauses.body: The workflow prepends an `## Release notes` section to the GitHub release body. Re-running replaces the existing section in place rather than appending a second one, so the release body stays stable across retries and re-runs.

clauses.title: Dry run
clauses.body: `workflow_dispatch` generates and reports the notes without publishing; a `publish` input defaults to `false`, so a manual run is a dry run unless `publish` is explicitly set true.

clauses.title: Source: `CHANGELOG.md` first, git log fallback
clauses.body: The prime source is the per-version section in `CHANGELOG.md` matching the released tag. When that section is empty or missing, the workflow falls back to the git log range for the release. The `0.8.0` section is currently empty, so the fallback is mandatory, not optional.

clauses.body: The generated section in the GitHub release body is delimited by `<!-- release-notes:start -->` and `<!-- release-notes:end -->` instead of a `---` horizontal rule. The `---` heuristic had a verified silent-truncation hole: a body starting with `## Release notes` and containing a hand-written `---` rule later would lose the hand-written content on re-run, because the replacement logic could not distinguish the generated delimiter from human-authored rules. HTML comments render invisibly on GitHub and cannot …

clauses.body: `notes.md` missing or empty always hard-fails — the GitHub release update is the primary artifact. `slack-payload.json` missing or invalid hard-fails only when publishing AND `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` is set; otherwise the workflow warns and continues. clauses.title: One version registry in `cypherlite-storage`
clauses.body: A single module names, per subsystem, `CURRENT_VERSION` (what this binary writes) and `MIN_READABLE_VERSION` (the oldest version this binary can load), plus the full readable set between them. The initial registry: The JSON codec's version dimension **is** `value_encoding`; the JSON envelope gets no separate `format_version` field. Future format ADRs change this registry and nothing else to declare a new version; when ADR-0120 is implemented it adds `format_version` 4, `value_encoding` 3 and `MDBWAL02` as readable …

clauses.title: Detection is the marker the loader already decoded
clauses.body: The codec loaders decode the version marker as part of their ordinary work, so detection costs no extra I/O: there is no separate pre-read of `manifest.json`, no re-read/re-parse of `graph.json`, and no standalone WAL header scan. Each loader reports the marker it decoded, and one per-marker classification in the registry — `Current | Legacy(version) | Unreadable` — backs every gate: the ADR-0114 unknown-version rejection, the ownership admission checks, and migrate-on-open all consult the same classification. …

clauses.title: One legacy reader per readable version, plus the current writer
clauses.body: There is no hop table and no chain of single-hop pure functions. For every version in the readable set the registry names the legacy reader that decodes it (the existing v1/v2 manifest fallback is the first instance); the only writer is the current writer. Migrating a store at `MIN_READABLE_VERSION` is not a composition of transforms: it is load with the named legacy reader, then write with the current writer. The codec loaders return the decoded marker alongside the decoded state, so the version is named where …

clauses.title: Execution: one open flow, then checkpoint + rotate + recycle
clauses.body: Migration is the ordinary open sequence — load with the reader for the reported marker, `Wal::open`, replay — followed, only when a loader reported a legacy marker and the VFS is durable, by a checkpoint at `CURRENT_VERSION`, a WAL rotation to a fresh segment with the current magic, and recycling of the legacy segments, all on the handles already open. There is no second load, no second `Wal::open`, no second replay. Before any query is served the store is at current format. Publication follows the manifest-last …

clauses.title: WAL compatibility story
clauses.body: `MDBWAL01` is the de-facto WAL version 1 and, today, the only readable magic, so WAL migration can never trigger and there is no separate WAL detection pass: one `version::wal::is_readable` classification backs both `scan_seg` and the native-ownership admission. Any future `RedoOp` shape change bumps the segment magic **and** ships a legacy decoder for the previous magic, instead of failing loudly with no path. When ADR-0120 lands, `MDBWAL02` becomes the first second WAL magic and WAL legacy-magic detection moves …

clauses.title: Bundle container stays frozen, gated only by `read_super`
clauses.body: A `.cl` store migrates the payload files inside the container (manifest, shards, WAL segments) under the rules above; the container format itself — magic `MDBCLB01`, superblock `VERSION = 1` (ADR-0074) — is bumped only for a true container layout change, never for a payload change. The container version is gated only by `read_super` (reached via `parse_uri` → `BundleVfs::open_or_create`), which does full A/B superblock selection with checksums; there is no second, weaker superblock parser for version detection.

clauses.title: Edge cases
clauses.body: `:memory:` is a no-op: no durable state, nothing to detect or migrate. A corrupt or partial old store fails loudly, with the offending version marker (or its absence) named in the error; a truncated v2 manifest or a half-written legacy segment is corruption, not a migration input. A store written by a **newer** CypherLite is still rejected at the ADR-0114 gate with the unsupported version in the error; the golden newer-version-rejected test is kept. A read-only open (ADR-0136) serves a migratable store **through …

clauses.title: The migration report is a `pub(crate)` value; no log line yet
clauses.body: The report is a plain value whose semantics are "subsystem X was at version N, now current"; an empty report means no migration happened (it is not an `Option<MigrationReport>`). The report type and its return channel stay internal to `cypherlite-storage`, keeping them out of the public-API documentation rules. No log or trace line is emitted on open: `cypherlite-storage` has no logging facility today, and adding one (`log`/`tracing`) is a heavy-dependency decision that needs its own ADR under AGENTS.md rule R6. …

clauses.title: Contract tests
clauses.body: Golden fixture stores per supported version (extending the ADR-0114 `testdata/stores/` set) plus per-version legacy reader unit tests — the reader tests are the compatibility proof, since there is no hop chain to test; the newer-version-rejected test stays. A fixture opens, migrates, serves queries, and reopens at `CURRENT_VERSION` byte-identical to a natively written store.

clauses.body: `update-website.yml` gains a `workflow_call` trigger and drops the dead `release: [published]` trigger; `workflow_dispatch` (manual run) stays.

Recipes are distilled, self-contained versions of the examples; each links its full program through the `companion` front-matter field. **Tests.** A new …

clauses.title: Running a script
clauses.body: `cypherlite::run_script_wire(conn, script, params_json)` splits with `cypherlite_splitter::split_executable_statements` (the splitter's scan drops comment-only pieces), runs each statement with the same parameters (decoded by `cypherlite::params_from_json`, the decoder the C ABI uses too), and returns one wire envelope per statement run, stopping after the first error. A blank or comment-only script returns none. Each statement commits on its own, so a failure leaves earlier statements applied.

clauses.title: Rendering a result

clauses.title: Identity lock is shared; the writer lease is exclusive
clauses.body: Every live native opener takes `LOCK_SH` on the existing root `.cypherlite.lock` and, when the WAL directory is distinct, on its `.cypherlite.lock`, for the life of the process. A writable open also creates and exclusively locks a stable `.cypherlite.writer` beside each of those markers. The writer file is mode `0600` when newly created, is never unlinked on close, and is not a database identity: nested scans still key only on `.cypherlite.lock` and `.cl`. A second writable open fails that lease with …

clauses.title: Read-only open does not create or repair
clauses.body: `OpenMode::ReadOnly` and CLI `--read-only` open an existing native directory or `.cl` file. A missing store is `Error::Storage` and creates nothing: no directory, marker, segment, or writer lease. The native reader opens markers read-only and takes only the shared identity locks. A `.cl` reader takes `LOCK_SH` on the existing host file; the writer still holds `LOCK_EX` on that file, so a bundle reader and a bundle writer do not run together. `:memory:` with `read_only` is a write fence and takes no file lock.

clauses.title: The loaded graph is a snapshot
clauses.body: Read-only open loads the manifest and shards, replays complete WAL frames, and stops at a torn tail without truncating it. If the manifest bytes change during the load, or a read fails because a checkpoint removed a file mid-load, the open retries a bounded number of times and then returns `Error::Storage`. After a stable load the process does not read the files again. Migrate-on-open, orphan sweep, checkpoint timers, the durability timer, and persist-on-drop do not run. Legacy snapshots are served through the …

clauses.title: Mutations fail
clauses.body: `try_wal_commit`, `checkpoint`, and `apply_replicated` return `Error::Semantic` (`database is read-only`). Reads stay available.

clauses.title: `--follow` is read-only plus a tail
clauses.body: `OpenMode::Follow` is the read-only tail. CLI `--follow` selects it. The mode is refused for `:memory:` and `.cl` with `Error::Semantic`. The handle still never appends, checkpoints, migrates, trims, or sweeps. A mid-batch apply failure reloads the graph, and if that reload fails the follower stays failed until the process reopens it; a snapshot pin that blocks reload past a short bound is reported as a follow error until the pin drops and the swap completes.

clauses.title: Poll the WAL; do not pin recycle
clauses.body: A thread on the follower lists native segments and reads the active segment length. It applies only complete CRC-valid frames with `lsn` greater than the applied LSN, via `Graph::apply_redo`, and it does not append. There is no inotify. Statement snapshots keep the pins they already hold.

clauses.title: Reload only across a gap
clauses.body: Caught up means the applied LSN is at least the manifest `checkpoint_lsn` before recycled segments disappear. The follower keeps tailing whatever WAL remains. If a segment the follower still needs is gone, or the active segment shrinks under the cursor (a crash trim), the follower stops applying and loads the current manifest, shards, and surviving WAL beside readers still using the installed graph. The exclusive publication lock covers only the swap: it waits out snapshot pins, which outlive `read_guard`, then …

clauses.title: No durable-LSN file
clauses.body: A follower may apply a frame the writer has not synced yet. A later trim of that tail is a gap and takes the same reload as a checkpoint the follower missed.

clauses.title: The routing-context `address` the client sent
clauses.body: , when present and non-empty. That address reached this server for this client, so it is routable for this client.

clauses.title: Otherwise, the connection's local socket address — the fallback for
clauses.body: Otherwise, **the connection's local socket address** — the fallback for clients that send an empty or absent routing context (some non-browser drivers do). Everything else in ADR-0269 stands: the three roles (`ROUTE`/`READ`/`WRITE`), ttl 300, the `db` echo, and ROUTE being answered regardless of failed state behind the ADR-0126 auth gate.

Each phase is wrapped in `tokio::time::timeout_at` (or equivalent) against the **same** accept-time deadline; a phase that starts with no budget left fails immediately. When the magic/version exchange completes, the deadline is discharged and the ADR-0110 idle per-read timeout (default 300 s) governs the session from then on, unchanged.

clauses.title: `dbms.components` returns three rows, in this order:

Row 1 must therefore be first **and** named `Neo4j Kernel`. Row 2 keeps its existing name and versions and feeds Desktop's `cypherVersions` (found by name `Cypher`). Row 3 identifies CypherLite to consumers that iterate …

clauses.title: SHOW DATABASES rows carry concrete values
clauses.body: in both the `neo4j` and `system` namespaces (ADR-0116): `name`, `type`, `aliases` and `constituents` are unchanged. `address` is the constant `'localhost:7687'`: Desktop builds the instance id `name@address` and rejects an empty address (evidence 4 above), and the engine does not know the Bolt bind address, so the value is a display/instance-id placeholder — correct for the default Bolt bind and the published Docker port, cosmetic-only otherwise.

clauses.title: `dbms.info()` returns one row
clauses.body: `{id: 'cypherlite', name: 'system', creationDate: '1970-01-01T00:00:00Z'}`. `name` is the constant `'system'`: the procedure arm sees only the graph, not the session's current database, and the engine is single-database. `creationDate` is a documented placeholder: the engine tracks no creation time, and the Desktop UI merely displays the fields (evidence 5 above).

Neo4j's `dbms.listConfig` exposes the full settings registry and accepts an optional `searchString` filter; CypherLite has no general settings registry, so the documented scope is the Browser-relevant subset, and no input arguments are accepted. Same …

No current client ever calls it — the Browser guards on server-reported `edition === 'enterprise'` plus semver `>= 5.7.0`, and ADR-0142 reports `community` on every row — so the procedure is defensive completeness for future or …

clauses.title: `opfs://<name>` is a wasm-only open
clauses.body: `name` is one segment of 1–64 characters from `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`. `Database::open` / `parse_uri` still reject the scheme. The browser calls `CypherliteDb.open`, which prepares handles and then `Database::open_vfs`. `:memory:` stays `new CypherliteDb()`.

clauses.title: Slot pool, then a synchronous VFS
clauses.body: `prepareOpfs` (shipped as `js/opfs.js`) runs in a dedicated worker. It creates `cypherlite/<name>/` under the origin's private directory and takes a `readwrite` sync access handle on a catalog file plus 64 slot files. After that, `OpfsVfs` in `cypherlite-wasm` implements `Vfs`: the catalog maps a virtual path to a slot id (directories are prefixes), and every read, write, truncate, and flush is a sync handle call. `cypherlite-storage` does not depend on `wasm-bindgen`.

clauses.title: Durability
clauses.body: `durable()` is true. `sync_all` and `durability_barrier` flush the slot. Creating, renaming, or removing a name rewrites and flushes the catalog before returning, so a WAL segment exists in the namespace before its bytes are acknowledged. `sync_dir` and `create_dir_all_for_atomic` flush the catalog again. The catalog handle is exclusive across agents; a second opener fails with `Error::Locked`. An exhausted pool is a storage error. `reset()` on an OPFS handle drops the database, wipes the virtual tree, and reopens …

clauses.title: Engine hook
clauses.body: `StoreTarget::from_vfs` / `from_vfs_with_codec` build a store whose snapshot and WAL share one VFS (`wal/…`, no native directory). `Database::open_vfs` is `open_with` after that construction. `wal_dir` and follow do not apply. The codec is the build default unless `OpenOptions.snapshot_codec` says otherwise (JSON on wasm32).

clauses.title: Playground
clauses.body: The example engine stays in a dedicated module worker and opens the default in-memory database (`new CypherliteDb()`). A reload starts empty. Cookbook recipes stay `:memory:` too. `open` remains available for a host that wants `opfs://<name>`.

clauses.title: NVL draws the graph view
clauses.body: `scripts/cookbook/runtime/graph.js` renders a step's graph result with `@neo4j-nvl/base` and `@neo4j-nvl/interaction-handlers`, pinned to 1.2.2 (the playground's version), on the canvas renderer with NVL's `d3Force` layout (the one NVL recommends for small graphs; it settles around a dragged node as Browser's does) and nodes of radius 40, so a result fitted to the pane is drawn large enough for NVL to show captions. It is created with `disableWebWorkers: true` and `disableTelemetry: true`, and the build replaces …

clauses.title: Interactions
clauses.body: A pinch, or the wheel with Ctrl/⌘ held, zooms; the plain wheel scrolls the page past a graph until the reader clicks into it, then zooms until the pointer leaves it, so a long recipe never traps the reader's scrolling. Dragging the canvas pans; dragging a node moves it; hovering a node or relationship shows its labels or type and its properties in an inspector, and clicking one keeps it there until it is closed or the canvas is clicked. Buttons zoom in, zoom out, fit the graph to the pane, and put back the step's …

clauses.title: Double-click expands a node from the page's database
clauses.body: The graph view asks the page's session for the node's neighbours, and the session runs two read statements in the engine worker: `MATCH (n)-[r]-(m) WHERE id(n) = $id RETURN r, m LIMIT 100`, then the relationships between the new neighbours and every node the view draws. The new nodes and relationships are added to the view, starting next to the expanded node. The queries and the merge live in `scripts/cookbook/lib/graph-model.mjs`.

clauses.title: Expanding runs the steps the database needs first
clauses.body: If the steps up to the one whose graph is on screen have not all run, expanding runs them first, in order, the way Run does (a step that has run does not run again), then expands. The double-click is the reader's click that ADR-0130 Decision item 4 requires before anything runs, and a failed step stops it the same way it stops a Run. Expansions are view state: they last while the reader switches between a step's tabs, and a run that gives the step a new result starts its graph view over from that result.

clauses.title: Limits
clauses.body: A result draws its first 300 nodes, as before. One expansion adds at most 100 neighbours, and a view stops growing at 1,000 nodes, NVL's canvas-renderer comfort zone.

clauses.title: The build checks the expand queries
clauses.body: When the build replays a recipe through the browser build of the engine (the WASM parity check, ADR-0130 Decision item 2), it also expands the first node of every graph result right after its step runs, and fails if the queries error or miss one of that node's relationships the step recorded.

clauses.title: `Database::clone_directory` copies a native directory
clauses.body: The CLI command is `cypherlite clone [--wal-dir DIR] SOURCE DEST` (ADR-0069: an exit-after verb is a positional command, not a flag). `:memory:` and `.cl` are refused before any lock is taken, for both the source and the destination. The source is always a frozen read-only open, never a follower. `CloneOptions` is `wal_dir` only, and it applies only to that source open. The destination is written in the codec that open observed. Clone does not take a codec.

clauses.title: The cut is the LSN visible when the read-only load finishes
clauses.body: The clone does not tail later commits. The source is not appended, checkpointed, migrated, trimmed, or recycled.

clauses.title: The destination is a new store
clauses.body: It must not already exist and must not be the source directory. The clone publishes `checkpoint_at` into that directory at the loaded LSN and `commit_ts`, using the source codec, then creates an empty WAL segment there so a later read-only open succeeds. The next commit on the clone is `lsn + 1`. The destination WAL is always `<dest>/wal`, even when the source WAL is external.

clauses.title: A failed clone removes the destination it created
clauses.body: , while it still holds the destination writer lease. A failure before the destination exists leaves nothing behind.

clauses.title: One pull process, streaming statements
clauses.body: `cypherlite pull --from ENVFILE --query VALUE DATABASE` executes a *list* of statements in one process: `VALUE` is split on `;` into statements (the engine's statement splitter), executed in order, all against the same connection; `VALUE` may name a file (`pull.cypher`) — its content is the statement list; `VALUE` `-` reads the statement list from stdin. One process = one transaction flow = **one checkpoint and one fsync at the end**, regardless of statement or batch count.

clauses.title: Streaming materialization
clauses.body: The loader reads the Query API v2 response body as a stream (chunked transfer), extracts result rows from the `values` array incrementally, and materializes them into ADR-0155 UNWIND batches as they arrive. No full-response buffer; no manual `SKIP`/`LIMIT` paging in callers. A statement without `LIMIT` may return the whole database; the response cap no longer bounds a pull.

clauses.title: Pull refuses non-empty destinations
clauses.body: `pull` into a database that already has elements or stored state fails with a typed error. There is no `--incremental` escape yet — incremental/idempotent re-pull semantics (MERGE on constraint-derived keys) stay a separate future decision.

clauses.title: The pull identity map is load-scoped memory, not persisted state
clauses.body: The map (source element id → local id) exists only during the pull process, where it resolves endpoints and cross-statement references (nodes created by an earlier statement in the list are the `a`/`b` endpoints of a later statement's relationships). It is dropped when the process ends. Persisted pull-identity objects (ADR-0092) are no longer written, read, or validated; existing ones are ignored on open.

clauses.title: One new CLI lifecycle verb `snapshot`
clauses.body: Following ADR-0069, it is an exit-after positional command recognized only as the first argument. Its single positional argument is the native directory `DATABASE`, and exactly one of two direction flags is required: `cypherlite snapshot DATABASE --to FILE.cl` exports a native directory database to a single-file `.cl` bundle. `cypherlite snapshot DATABASE --from FILE.cl` imports a `.cl` bundle into a fresh native directory `DATABASE`. `--wal-dir DIR` is allowed only with `--to` (the external WAL of the directory …

clauses.title: The source is always opened read-only via the ADR-0136 path
clauses.body: (`OpenMode::ReadOnly` / `open_store_readonly`): stable-cut manifest retry, bounded reads, fail-closed on corruption. The command never writes to or exclusively locks the source. A writer-held `.cl` source fails with a lock error, since a bundle writer holds `LOCK_EX` on the host file (ADR-0136).

clauses.title: The destination must not exist
clauses.body: — the same contract as `clone` (ADR-0156). A failed run removes any partially created destination, file or directory.

clauses.title: The destination keeps the source's snapshot codec in both
clauses.body: — json stays json, parquet stays parquet. There is no codec conversion.

clauses.title: Engine: two new public `Database` methods
clauses.body: `snapshot_to_bundle(source, dest, SnapshotOptions)` and `restore_from_bundle(source, dest, SnapshotOptions)` generalize the `clone.rs` publish path across the dir/`.cl` boundary. `SnapshotOptions` carries `wal_dir: Option<PathBuf>`, used only by `snapshot_to_bundle`.

clauses.title: The command is compiled into every CLI bundle like clone
clauses.body: This deviates from the ADR-0104 rule that a new capability gets its own feature: snapshot/restore is as fundamental to moving data as clone, adds no dependencies, and keeping it always-available avoids a bundle in which a user's backup tool vanishes.

clauses.title: Publish destination creation is create-exclusive end to end
clauses.body: A new `cypherlite_storage::parse_uri_creating` (beside `parse_uri_opening`) drives it; `publish_into` uses it for clone, snapshot, and restore. `.cl` bundles: `BundleVfs::open_create_exclusive` creates the host file with `create_new(true)` and **no `AlreadyExists` fallback**; `resolve_bundle_path` never canonicalizes a symlinked final component in this mode. An existing entry — file, directory, or a symlink raced into the window — fails with an `Error::Storage` whose message starts with the exported …

clauses.title: Ordinary opens are unchanged
clauses.body: `parse_uri`, `parse_uri_opening`, `BundleVfs::open_or_create`, and `Database::open` keep adopting existing stores; only the publish path opts into exclusivity.

clauses.title: `remove_created`'s invariant is enforced by construction
clauses.body: When the exclusive create reports destination-already-exists, publish created nothing, so `publish_into` returns the error (re-wrapped with the verb, e.g. "snapshot destination already exists: PATH") **without** calling `remove_created`. The loser of a create race deletes nothing; the winner's in-progress destination survives byte-identical. The `reject_destination` pre-check stays as a fast path with the verb-naming message.

clauses.title: The destination store handle is dropped before `remove_created`
clauses.body: In the publish error paths the store (flock + open handles) is dropped first, so partial-destination cleanup also succeeds on Windows.

clauses.title: QueryResult gains a public query_type field of a new public
clauses.body: , set for every statement — plain runs, EXPLAIN, and PROFILE alike — at result construction, exactly like `namespace` (ADR-0117 §7). The enum is re-exported by the `cypherlite` facade like `Namespace`. The value set is pinned to Neo4j's (LABS-175): `Read` / `Write` / `ReadWrite` / `Schema`, with wire codes `"r"`, `"w"`, `"rw"`, `"s"`.

clauses.title: Classification is plan-based and total
clauses.body: It is derived from the logical plan above the EXPLAIN/dispatch split in `Connection::run_query`, reusing `clause_kind::is_write_clause` and the `call_is_write` procedure hook, extended to tell schema DDL (index/constraint create/drop) apart from data writes: no write or schema clause → `r`; data writes without reads → `w`; reads and data writes → `rw`; schema DDL → `s`. Every other string goes through `str::parse::<f64>()`, which accepts fractional and scientific forms such …

clauses.title: `Null` and `Map` are armed defensively
clauses.body: Neo4j property values are scalars or homogeneous lists of scalars, so neither tag can occur as a property; the decoder still maps them (`Value::Null`, recursive `Value::Map`) so the tag table and the recursion are total. They are the only two keys beyond the 19 captured tags.

clauses.title: Slots and seeds
clauses.body: Planning runs over **slots**, a type of its own (`layout::Slot`), not over manifest records: a **kept** slot is a previous manifest part with its file, a **window** an id range with no previous file. `ShardPart` stays a plain manifest record. Only kept slots supply copy sources and retired paths; a window is never retired or written to the manifest. A kept slot that overlaps a dirty id seeds a unit, and so does every window: `cover_ids` adds one for uncovered ids, including every window of the first sharded …

clauses.title: Absorption
clauses.body: A unit absorbs its immediately adjacent slots on either side in id order, clean kept slots included, while three bounds hold. The merged id range `[lo, hi)` spans `hi - lo <= 1,000,000` ids (`MAX_WINDOW`, ADR-0022's widest window). The unit's kept slots' manifest `rows` sum to at most `Kind::page_envelope_rows()` (see Page envelope) and their published `bytes` to at most the cap a file is written into, `min(target_bytes, 1 GiB)` (Decision 3); both are read from the manifest, without a graph walk. And the unit's …

clauses.title: Write
clauses.body: Planning cuts each unit into files in the walk that measures it, and the writer writes those **planned cuts** in order without measuring again. A unit within the target is **one file**. A lone seed over the target is cut where the next row would pass the target or the decoded envelope, so each file is `<= target_bytes` decoded unless it is a single over-target row. A seed wider than `MAX_WINDOW` ids (a healed window, or a file written from one) absorbs nothing and is first cut every `Kind::page_envelope_rows()` …

clauses.title: Untouched parts
clauses.body: Every kept slot outside every unit is kept unchanged: its manifest entry is reused verbatim (ADR-0089 Decision 1), zero I/O.

clauses.title: No manifest format change
clauses.body: `format_version`, `Manifest` and `ShardPart` keep their fields. A merged range spans at most `MAX_WINDOW` ids, like an ADR-0022 window. A healed window (Decision 1) can span more, but each of its files holds at most `Kind::page_envelope_rows()` rows (Decision 3). Either way a part's rows stay within the `read_manifest` bounds (`<= MAX_WINDOW` and `<=` its id width), and v0.11.5 opens the new layout.

clauses.body: Pick the `i` with the smallest sum; ties go to the lowest `i`.

clauses.title: Top-level help is a command index
clauses.body: `cypherlite --help` prints the usage lines … then a `Commands:` section with a one-line entry for every compiled-in command — `clone`, `info`, `pull`, `skill`, `upgrade` (naming its `update` alias), `telemetry`, `lab` — then all query-run options as before, and ends with the footer … No lifecycle command’s flags appear in it; only the query run keeps full flag detail there.

clauses.title: Per-command help
clauses.body: `-h`/`--help` anywhere after a compiled-in command word prints that command’s help (synopsis plus its flags/actions) to stdout and exits 0. `cypherlite update --help` prints the `upgrade` help; `lab` help omits the hidden `neo` action; a help flag before the command word still prints top-level help. A command word whose feature is compiled out keeps the not-included error (exit 2).

clauses.title: Usage errors are scoped
clauses.body: A usage error (exit 2) prints `Error: <msg>`, the relevant command’s synopsis line(s) as `Usage: cypherlite …`, and `Run 'cypherlite <command> --help' for more information.` — with the canonical name `upgrade` for `update`. Top-level parse errors (unknown flag, unexpected positional, invalid `--namespace`) use the query-run synopsis and `Run 'cypherlite --help' for more information.` The two literal stderr shapes are … …

clauses.title: Errors that print no usage today keep their stderr byte-for-byte
clauses.body: A missing flag value, an invalid `--mode`/`--param`/`--fetch-params` value, and `--command` combined with a positional query are unchanged.

clauses.title: Per-command help emits the existing telemetry events
clauses.body: (`CYPHERLITE-CLI_STARTUP` with kind `help`, and `CYPHERLITE-CLI_HELP`) — no schema change.

clauses.title: Each command synopsis is defined once in source

The rejected argument travels as data, so no message text is ever …

clauses.body: No new dependency: the edit distance is a ~12-line local function.

clauses.title: --version prints one JSON object on stdout when the resolved
clauses.body: `--version` prints one JSON object on stdout when the resolved output mode is `json` (`--json`, `-json`, `--mode json`, in either argument order): … Keys are sorted alphabetically and their order is not part of the contract. `version` is the crate version without the `v` prefix; `os` and `arch` are Rust's `std::env::consts::{OS, ARCH}`. clauses.title: Every other mode, and no mode, keeps the text form
clauses.body: Every other mode, and no mode, keeps the text form `CypherLite v<version>` byte for byte.

clauses.title: No commit or build_date field. Both need a build script,
clauses.body: No `commit` or `build_date` field. Both need a build script, which the CLI crate does not have, and a build date makes builds non-reproducible. They can be added later as additive fields.

clauses.title: --version still reads no config and opens no database, and
clauses.body: `--version` still reads no config and opens no database, and `--help` still wins when both are given.

clauses.title: Exit-code map
clauses.body: The query run (one-shot, piped stdin, store open) adopts `neo4j-cli`'s closed enum: The engine error variant decides the class (`Syntax`/`Semantic`/`Type` → 6, `Conflict`/`Locked` → 5, everything else → 1). A batch that stops on its first failure, or runs on in the REPL, exits with the code of the last failing statement.

clauses.title: Envelope
clauses.body: In `json` and `jsonl` output modes a failure also prints one compact JSON object on stdout, after any rows already written: … `code` and `exit_code` are the table above; `kind` is the engine variant (`syntax`, `semantic`, `type`, `execution`, `conflict`, `capacity`, `storage`, `locked`, `io`, `internal`); `retryable` is true only for `conflict` kind (a write-write conflict, which a retry can resolve). The `message` is the same sanitized text printed on stderr. Fields may be added; existing ones are never renamed …

clauses.title: stderr is unchanged
clauses.body: The human line (`syntax error: …`, `Failed to open CypherLite: …`) is printed exactly as before, in every mode, so existing stderr greps keep working.

clauses.title: Scope
clauses.body: Usage errors (exit 2) and the lifecycle commands (`clone`, `pull`, `info`, `skill`, `upgrade`, `telemetry`, `lab`) keep their current plain output and their 0/1/2 codes; their envelope is a follow-up. Interactive sessions are unchanged: a query error returns to the prompt.

clauses.title: A new output mode, spelled envelope, prints one JSON object
clauses.body: A new output mode, spelled `envelope`, prints one JSON object per result set: … `columns` lists the result columns in order, including for an empty result (`{"columns":["n"],"rows":[],"truncated":false}`); `rows` holds one object per row, built exactly as `--json` builds them; `truncated` is `false` here and is set by the row cap (LABS-230). The object is compact and is printed on one line, so a multi-statement run is JSON Lines of envelopes.

clauses.title: Selected with --mode envelope. There is no boolean shorthand yet;
clauses.body: Selected with `--mode envelope`. There is no boolean shorthand yet; the output-flag vocabulary (`--format`, LABS-232) is a separate decision. `--json`, `--jsonl` and every other mode print exactly what they printed before.

clauses.title: The envelope mode is a machine-readable mode: a failure also
clauses.body: The envelope mode is a machine-readable mode: a failure also prints the ADR-0194 error envelope on stdout, the same as `json` and `jsonl`.

clauses.title: No arrays_truncated field. neo4j-cli truncates long arrays inside
clauses.body: No `arrays_truncated` field. `neo4j-cli` truncates long arrays inside cells; CypherLite has no such cap, and an always-zero field is noise. It can be added later as an additive field.

clauses.title: Telemetry (ADR-0079) is unchanged: the output_mode dimension reports
clauses.body: Telemetry (ADR-0079) is unchanged: the `output_mode` dimension reports `json` for this mode, so the closed value set does not grow.

clauses.title: `--max-rows N`
clauses.body: limits the rows printed per statement. `0` means unlimited. Any explicit value, in any run, is honored.

clauses.title: Default cap: 100 rows, only under an agent harness
clauses.body: With no `--max-rows` and no `CYPHERLITE_MAX_ROWS`, the cap is 100 when an agent harness is detected and stdout is not a terminal; otherwise it is unlimited. Interactive shells and terminals are never capped by default, and scripts outside a harness see no change.

clauses.title: Detection
clauses.body: is by environment variable, the list `neo4j-cli` uses (which follows `unjs/std-env`): `CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE`, `REPL_ID`, `GEMINI_CLI`, `CODEX_SANDBOX`, `CODEX_THREAD_ID`, `OPENCODE`, `AUGMENT_AGENT`, `GOOSE_PROVIDER`, `CURSOR_AGENT` (any non-empty value), plus case-insensitive substrings `devin` in `EDITOR`, `kiro` in `TERM_PROGRAM`, and `.pi/agent` in `PATH`.

clauses.title: `CYPHERLITE_MAX_ROWS=N`
clauses.body: sets the default for a session or a script the same way `CYPHERLITE_MEMORY_LIMIT` does; a bad value exits 2 like a bad flag. The flag overrides the variable.

clauses.title: A capped result announces itself
clauses.body: The first `N` rows print, and the `envelope` mode (ADR-0195) sets `"truncated": true`; a stderr line names the statement and the opt-out: `warning: result truncated to 100 rows (the statement returned 100000); pass --max-rows 0 for all rows`; the exit code is unchanged (`0`): truncation is not a failure.

clauses.title: The cap limits output, not engine work
clauses.body: The engine materializes a statement's full result before the CLI prints it; the cap protects the reader's context, not memory. A server-side `LIMIT` remains the way to bound the work.

clauses.title: One or two examples per page
clauses.body: The top-level `--help` and each command's `<command> --help` end with an `Examples:` section holding one or two invocations, each a `# comment` line above a `cypherlite ...` command line. The top level shows a plain read as JSON and a `--read-only` exploration with `--mode envelope`; each command shows its common case.

clauses.title: One source
clauses.body: The per-command examples live next to the command table (`CommandSpec::examples`) and the top-level pair in `examples.rs`, which also owns the `Examples:` rendering and the environment gate; the help text is built from them, so a page and its test cannot drift.

clauses.title: They are tested
clauses.body: A unit test pins the shape (one or two per page, a comment, a `cypherlite` command line, present in the page). An e2e test runs the examples that are safe to run (the top-level pair, `clone`, `info`) against a temp database and requires success. `pull` (network), `skill` (home directory), `upgrade` (network), `telemetry` (config) and `lab` (imports a directory) are checked for shape only.

clauses.title: `CYPHERLITE_HELP_EXAMPLES=0` hides them
clauses.body: `0`, `false`, `off` or `no` (case-insensitive) drops the `Examples:` section from every help page; any other value, or unset, shows it. Only the examples change: the synopsis, the flags, stdout versus stderr and the exit code are identical. The variable is read once, when the page is rendered, and is not a flag.

clauses.title: No exit-code section in `--help`
clauses.body: The audit also asked for exit codes in help. They are documented in the spec and README (ADR-0194) and the usage line already points at `--help`; repeating the table on every page would grow the pages this ADR is trying to keep short.

clauses.title: `WITH *` registers grouping keys (s20)
clauses.body: **`WITH *` registers grouping keys (s20).** When a `WITH`/`RETURN` projection combines `*` with aggregating expressions, every variable carried by `*` is a grouping key, so non-aggregated leaves inside aggregate-containing expressions (such as `z` in `collect(n.x) + [z]`) resolve against them. This matches Neo4j's expansion of `*` to all in-scope variables and the openCypher grouping model: one group per carried row, exactly as when the variable is projected explicitly.

clauses.title: Aggregates in CASE arms belong to the enclosing projection (p-case)
clauses.body: An aggregate function call inside a CASE branch — or any other ordinary expression position, such as a list literal (already supported) — belongs to the enclosing aggregating projection. Validation must walk these positions when classifying aggregate calls instead of falling back to the scalar-expression path that rejects them. Both rulings are against Neo4j CE 2026.09.0 live-probe ground truth and are pinned by the evidence above: LABS-199, the battery results (commits 780b0343/f5b0c119 in this branch's git …

clauses.title: Report progress when a multi-statement run fails
clauses.body: A run with more than one statement (one-shot `-c`, piped stdin, an interactive line holding several) that stops on a failed statement reports where it stopped. A run of a single statement, and a run that succeeds, print exactly what they print today.

clauses.title: Stderr gets one extra line
clauses.body: , after the existing error line and before anything else: `statement 2 of 3 failed; 1 completed and committed; 1 not run`. Inside an open `.begin` transaction the middle clause reads `1 completed, not committed (open transaction)`.

clauses.title: The error envelope gains three optional fields
clauses.body: (additive to ADR-0194), present only for a multi-statement run: …

clauses.title: What counts as a statement
clauses.body: is what the splitter yields and the run executes: a Cypher statement or a `.`-command, so the index matches what was typed. Empty fragments are not counted; `statements` is the number of runnable fragments, so a trailing `;` does not add one. **Only a failed Cypher statement reports.** A failed `.`-command (for example `.commit` with no open transaction) stops the run as it does today, with its existing error line and exit code and no envelope (ADR-0194 keeps dot-commands outside the error object); giving them one …

clauses.title: No change to execution
clauses.body: A failure still stops a piped or one-shot batch at the first error (ADR-0194's exit code is that statement's class). This ADR adds reporting only.

clauses.title: Interactive sessions
clauses.body: report nothing extra. A line holding several statements keeps going after a failure in the shell, so "N not run" would be false there, and the user sees the state at the prompt. Only a run that stops at its first failure (`-c`, piped stdin) reports.

clauses.title: `query` is a first-positional command word in every bundle
clauses.body: It is a statement-session verb, not an exit-after lifecycle command (ADR-0069). A directory named `query` is `--database query` or `--database ./query`.

clauses.title: Grammar:
clauses.body: `cypherlite query [STATEMENT] [--database PATH] [session flags]`. `STATEMENT` is one Cypher statement or a `;`-separated list, the same slot as `-c` / `--command`. The two spellings cannot be combined. On the path-first form, no `QUERY` prints help and exits; it does not open the shell or read stdin. `query` with no `STATEMENT` keeps the session trichotomy: a terminal opens the shell and any other stdin is the script list.

clauses.title: `-d` / `--database PATH`
clauses.body: is the store on `query`, on the path-first form, on `pull`, and on `info`. `-d` is the short form of `--database`. Omitted on a statement session, the store is `:memory:`. `pull` and `info` require it and reject `:memory:`. A value that starts with `-` is still a path (`-d -dashed_db`).

clauses.title: The path-first form is
clauses.body: `cypherlite [OPTIONS] [--database PATH] [QUERY]`. The only positional is the statement. A second positional is a usage error. `clone SOURCE DEST` stays two positionals (ADR-0156). `lab fs-to-graph` keeps `--db` (ADR-0286).

clauses.title: `query --help`
clauses.body: prints the command synopsis and the same query-run options as top-level help, including `--database`, from one shared options block.

clauses.title: One bounded retry of the whole pull, on the transient
clauses.body: In `testing/cypherlite-graph-examples/src/suite.rs`, `pull_fresh_copy` routes the attempt through a `with_one_transient_retry` helper. The transient predicate (`is_transient_failure` in `testing/cypherlite-graph-examples/src/pull.rs`, next to `pull_once`) anchors on the single stable substring of cypherlite-load's mid-statement read error, `failed mid-statement` (see `mid_statement_read_error` in `surfaces/cypherlite-load/src/response.rs`); the io-error tail (`Peer disconnected`, `Connection reset by peer`, …) …

clauses.title: The harness captures reference container logs into the report dir
clauses.body: A new `docker::capture_reference_logs(report_dir)` writes `docker logs` for every container matching the `cypherlite-graph-examples-reference` name prefix to `<report_dir>/reference-<id>.log`, best effort. The infrastructure failure paths in `tests/differential.rs` (the `verdict()` panic and the boot panic) call it before panicking. The files land next to `report.txt`, inside the workflow's existing `reference-*.log` upload glob — no workflow change. No credential stripping is needed: `docker logs` carries only …

clauses.title: No memory bump
clauses.body: Evidence first: the same 4G container served the other fifteen pulls in the failing run, so there is no signal that heap was the cause. The diagnostics capture from (2) is exactly what provides evidence if this recurs.

clauses.title: Null-skipping stays as is
clauses.body: — every aggregation except `count(*)` skips null input values; this is confirmed by unit tests pinning the existing behavior (mixed null/number, all-null, `collect` ignoring nulls, `count(x)` vs `count(*)`).

clauses.title: `sum()` accepts `DURATION` values
clauses.body: Durations accumulate component-wise (`months`/`days`/`nanos`, via the existing `temporal::add_duration`) and the result is a `DURATION`. Mixing numbers and durations in one `sum()` is a type error. `sum()` over zero non-null values stays `0` (INTEGER) in every path — the grouped evaluator, the horizontal evaluator, and the ADR-0036 one-hop fold (which previously returned `null` there).

clauses.title: `avg()` accepts `DURATION` values
clauses.body: the same way, returning the accumulated duration scaled by `1/n` (`temporal::scale_duration`, the engine's duration-division semantics). Mixing numbers and durations is a type error; `avg()` over zero non-null values stays `null`.

clauses.title: count, collect, min, max, stDev, stDevP,
clauses.body: keep their current (TCK-passing) semantics; only their null-skipping is pinned harder by tests.

clauses.title: A transactional delta-store design
clauses.body: must exist first: compressed committed chunks plus a small uncompressed per-chunk write delta, merged at read time and compacted into the compressed form at checkpoint. Until that design is implemented and measured, the live store keeps uncompressed `AdjHop` chunks.

clauses.title: The tiered-arena layout must be prototyped first
clauses.body: (one `Vec<AdjHop>` arena per node-direction + a `(type_id, offset, len)` index): it is strictly negative memory and touches the sorted-insert invariant, so it is the cheapest structural rehearsal of the layout changes compressed chunks would force. **SIMD is explicitly not part of the recommendation** — the measured NEON decoder fails to beat scalar (0.72–1.07x, one 1.22x outlier) because scalar decode already outruns every consumer; the SIMD path stays prototype-only. The two scalar schemes remain as measured …

clauses.title: Eligibility is plan-based and conservative
clauses.body: A statement is batchable only when all of the following hold: auto-commit (no explicit transaction), single-part plan, no UNION, no `NEXT`; every `MATCH` is non-optional, carries no `WHERE`/`SEARCH`, and consists solely of *bare* patterns: single-node patterns `(<var> [:labels…])` (no properties, no element predicates, no label expressions, no path variable) or single-relationship patterns `()-[<var> [:types…]]->()` (fixed length, no properties, no predicates); any `WITH` clauses between the matches and the write …

clauses.title: Two-phase execution
clauses.body: Phase 1 pins a snapshot and collects the *target identity space* only: one sorted id vector per matched variable (node ids filtered by labels, relationship ids filtered by types). Memory is O(Σ matched entities), never O(Π) — the cross-product shape stores its factors, not its combinations. Phase 2 replays the combinations in chunks of bounded *work* (target entities plus, for `DETACH DELETE`, their incident relationships — estimated from adjacency degrees), each chunk on a fresh scratch committed through the …

clauses.title: Small statements keep the existing path
clauses.body: Below a work threshold (10 000 estimated touched entities) the statement runs unbatched, so the common case pays no extra commits. The batched path also runs only on the auto-commit route; explicit transactions keep their boundaries.

clauses.title: Semantics
clauses.body: On the success path the final store state and the statement's write statistics are identical to the unbatched run: the match set is fixed before any write (stronger than the unbatched read-own-writes order, but these shapes' writes cannot change their own match set — the matches bind only bare nodes/relationships and the write-clause expressions cannot observe sibling rows). On the error path a batched statement may leave earlier batches committed — exactly the documented `CALL { } IN TRANSACTIONS` trade-off. One …

clauses.title: Observability
clauses.body: The returned `QueryResult` carries the summed `QueryStats` over all batches and no rows (the eligible shapes have no `RETURN`), identical in shape to the unbatched result. EXPLAIN output is unchanged; batching is an execution strategy, not a plan rewrite.

clauses.title: Terminal-projection walk skips non-projection write clauses
clauses.body: Terminal-projection walk skips non-projection write clauses In `local_stage_output_vars` (`cypherlite-front/src/validate/scope.rs`), `Clause::Delete`, `Clause::Set`, `Clause::Remove` and `Clause::Foreach` reset the tracked terminal projection to `None`, exactly as `Clause::Create` and `Clause::Merge` already do. A `WITH`/`RETURN` later in the body still establishes a projection, so `CALL { WITH n RETURN n }` keeps raising `VariableAlreadyBound`, while a body whose last projection is followed only by writes exports …

clauses.title: A concluding CALL { … } projects the body's exported
clauses.body: A concluding `CALL { … }` projects the body's exported columns `finish_part` and `execute_part_read_seeded` share one concluding-CALL helper that also covers `Clause::CallSubquery`: when the concluding subquery body has a terminal `RETURN`, the statement result is the produced rows projected to the body's exported columns (`call_export_columns`). A `REPORT STATUS AS <var>` column never appears here: the planner rejects REPORT STATUS without a following RETURN, so the status column only surfaces through that …

clauses.title: Per-batch commits fold each batch into the base graph
clauses.body: Per-batch commits fold each batch into the base graph `IN TRANSACTIONS` semantics are independent inner transactions: a committed batch stays committed even when a later batch fails under `ON ERROR FAIL`. The executor gains a batch-commit step: after a batch succeeds (constraint validation included), its redo ops are drained from the statement scratch and committed through a `BatchCommit` sink the facade injects into the execution request; the scratch is then rebased to a fresh `WriteScratch` at the new commit …

clauses.title: Element grammar keeps the `=>` requirement
clauses.body: In a node/edge type specification the `{ <property types> }` block is accepted only after the `=>`/`IMPLIES` marker — current Neo4j behavior, pinned by the CIP-178/181/183 negative scenarios: without the marker the label is not an explicitly denoted identifying label and the statement is a compile-time syntax error (the error message says exactly that). Canonical rendering is unchanged (`(:`Tag` => {`name` :: STRING})`).

clauses.title: `IS` as a property-type introducer
clauses.body: A property declaration accepts `<name> IS [::] <value type>` as equivalent to `<name> :: <value type>`. Disambiguation against the existing inline-constraint form is lexical: `IS` followed by `KEY`/`UNIQUE` (optionally preceded by the `NODE`/`REL`/`RELATIONSHIP` qualifier) keeps its inline-constraint meaning; anything else after `IS` starts the value type.

clauses.title: `ALTER CURRENT GRAPH TYPE SET GRAPH TYPE <name>`
clauses.body: A new `SET` sub-form copies the named, previously `CREATE GRAPH TYPE`-declared type's body into the current graph type, passing the same validation and derived-constraint installation as `SET { ... }`. An unknown name fails with `GraphTypeNotFound` (the same error `SHOW GRAPH TYPE <name>` reports). `CREATE GRAPH TYPE` still does not make its type current — declared and current remain separate (matching Neo4j's declared-vs-current separation); the new sub-form is the supported path from one to the other.

clauses.title: Documentation
clauses.body: `docs/reference/cypher-syntax.md`'s graph-types section documents the relaxed property declarations, `SET GRAPH TYPE <name>`, and `SHOW CURRENT GRAPH TYPE AS GRAPH [SINGLE | SEPARATE]`.

clauses.title: `Record`
clauses.body: (`cypherlite.Record`): a `dict` subclass with attribute access (`r.name`), `.data()` (plain-dict copy), `.keys()`, and iteration in column order. Cursors yield `Record` everywhere a row comes out (`fetchone`, `fetchmany`, `fetchall`, iteration, `single`, `peek`). `dict` equality and `isinstance` keep working, so existing code and the existing test suite are unaffected.

clauses.title: Cursor result conveniences
clauses.body: (driver parity): `cursor.data()` — all remaining rows as a list of `Record`s (consumes). `cursor.single()` — the one record; raises the new `ResultNotSingleError` (a `ProgrammingError` subclass) on zero or more than one remaining row, like the driver's `Result.single()`. `cursor.peek()` — the next record without advancing, `None` at the end. `cursor.fetch(n)` — alias of `fetchmany(n)` (the driver's spelling). `cursor.keys()` — alias of `.columns` (the driver's naming).

clauses.title: `cursor.to_df()`
clauses.body: — remaining rows as a `pandas.DataFrame` (`pd.DataFrame(rows)`, consuming like `fetchall`). Raises `ImportError` with install instructions (`pip install neo4j-cypherlite[pandas]`) when pandas is absent — same pattern as `cypherlite.viz`. Polars/narwhals are deliberately out of scope (see Alternatives).

clauses.title: Not in scope: consume()/ResultSummary (the engine's stats carry no
clauses.body: Not in scope: `consume()`/`ResultSummary` (the engine's stats carry no statement timing; a summary object without timings is a hollow copy), `graph()` (covered by `cypherlite.viz.to_visualization_graph`, which already accepts materialized results).

clauses.title: `Result` object
clauses.body: `conn.query()` returns a `Result` with `columns`, `stats` (the canonical 11 counters, snake_case), `queryType`, `namespace`, and **rows as objects keyed by column name** — a breaking change from positional arrays (pre-1.0 npm package, recorded in the CHANGELOG). The result is fully materialized at query time; there is no fetch position.

clauses.title: Driver conveniences
clauses.body: (synchronous — the engine is in-process, so there is nothing to await; Kùzu's Node API is synchronous for the same reason): `single()` (throws `ResultNotSingleError` on zero or >1) and `consume()` → a `ResultSummary` with `counters`, `queryType`, `namespace`, and `elapsedMs` measured at the client edge with `performance.now()` (ADR-0215's rationale verbatim: in-process, the client edge is the execution edge). `peek()`/`fetch(n)` are deliberately absent: unlike the Python cursor there is no fetch position — `rows` …

clauses.title: `graph()`
clauses.body: returns a `ResultGraph` (`nodes`, `relationships`, id-ordered, de-duplicated by id) extracted from the wire JSON shapes — `{"id","labels","properties"}` nodes, `{"id","type","start_node", "end_node","properties"}` relationships, paths as alternating arrays — walking nested arrays/objects, mirroring ADR-0214.

clauses.title: FFI
clauses.body: : the tabular C ABI gains `cypherlite_result_stats(result) -> str` returning the canonical counters JSON (`stats_to_wire_json` via `query_stats_to_wire`), stamped into the result at pack time. The committed header is hand-maintained C (cbindgen's default output is C++ and drops the ownership/threading/panic-safety contract block, so `make gen-ffi-header` was removed in favor of hand-maintaining the declaration); every other C-ABI client may adopt it in its own change (cross-surface metadata rule).

clauses.title: TypeScript
clauses.body: : a hand-written `index.d.ts` ships in the package — full types for `Database`, `Connection`, `Result`, `ResultSummary`, `ResultGraph`, and the wire entity shapes.

clauses.title: Library skill
clauses.body: : `.agents/skills/cypherlite/SKILL.md` ships inside the npm package (library-skills.io convention, like the Python wheel), and the CLI bundle's `client-javascript.md` reference updates in the same change.

clauses.title: The class lives once
clauses.body: , in `cypherlite-ir` next to `AGGREGATES`: `SINGLE_INPUT_AGGREGATES = ["sum", "avg", "min", "max", "collect", "stdev", "stdevp"]`. `stdev`/`stdevp` join the class ADR-0225's normative "every single-input aggregate" wording already described — the reference behavior is the same `42I13` error. `count` stays out (the parser's keyword path already guarantees its arity) and the percentiles stay out (two arguments, their own call-site check). `cypherlite-front::agg` re-exports it, as it does `AGGREGATES`.

clauses.title: Front validation
clauses.body: consumes the shared table unchanged in reach: any member call with arity other than one is `ErrorKind::InvalidNumberOfArguments`, over RETURN/WITH items, GROUP BY keys and ORDER BY expressions, with one message clause (`name(input) requires exactly one argument, got N`).

clauses.title: The executor backstop
clauses.body: draws every aggregate's arity contract from one home: `cypherlite-ir` holds a single `(name, AggregateArity)` table from which `AGGREGATES` and `SINGLE_INPUT_AGGREGATES` (the `SingleInput` class minus `count`) derive — an aggregate without a contract, or a class table that disagrees with the vocabulary, is unrepresentable — and `aggregate_arity(name)` returns the contract — `SingleInput` (exactly one argument, the `InvalidNumberOfArguments` shape) for `count` and the `SINGLE_INPUT_AGGREGATES` members …

clauses.title: Plan-time label statistics
clauses.body: `cypherlite-planner` gains a `MatchStats` trait (`label_count(&self, label) -> Option<u64>`) and a `plan_with_stats` entry point; `plan` delegates with a `NoStats` null object (every count `None`), keeping every existing caller and the stats-free behavior unchanged. The facade (`cypherlite/src/connection.rs::plan_gate_classify`) already plans under the graph read guard, so it passes an adapter over `cypherlite-executor`'s `Graph::label_count` — the label-index set size, an O(1) approximation (it includes ids not …

clauses.title: Tie-break orientation by cardinality
clauses.body: In `orient_path`, the coarse rank still dominates (a bound node always wins, a property-equality end still beats a label-only end). When both ends rank equal and statistics are available, the end with the smaller minimum label cardinality seeds the part: the path reverses only on a strictly smaller estimate, so equal or unknown estimates keep the written order.

clauses.title: Order independent parts cheap-end first
clauses.body: After the stable sort by descending seed rank, `order_patterns` floats a part ahead of its predecessors while they rank equal and the part's cheapest end (min of first/last label counts) is strictly smaller than theirs — a constrained adjacent-swap pass, not a re-sort: a part never passes a neighbor it shares a variable with, because that neighbor may be what binds it (LABS-157). Among equal ranks, a part that will scan 10 nodes runs before one that will scan 200 000. The cartesian product itself is mandated by …

clauses.title: `Connection.query` doubles as a template tag
clauses.body: When the first argument is a template strings array (a call-site tag invocation), the tag builds the Cypher text with each interpolated value replaced by an auto-named `$p0, $p1, …` parameter and runs the existing `query(cypher, params)` path. The string form `query(cypher, params?)` stays the documented primary.

clauses.title: Value dedup
clauses.body: The same primitive value interpolated twice maps to one parameter (`SameValueZero` equality, `Map`-keyed); objects dedup by identity. Parameter names stay contiguous over the unique values.

clauses.title: Unsupported values reject — in both forms, at any depth
clauses.body: `undefined`, functions, symbols and non-finite numbers (`NaN`, `±Infinity`) throw a `TypeError` (the tag names the interpolation index, the string form the params key; nested leaves are named by their key path) — they have no JSON/Cypher representation, and silently stringifying them would drop the key (object) or null the slot (array) and corrupt the statement. The check walks nested objects and arrays; cyclic values terminate the walk and hit `JSON.stringify`'s own error. The plain-object rule applies at every …

clauses.title: No fragment composition
clauses.body: Interpolated values are always data; there is no nested-template or raw-fragment escape hatch — that would reopen the injection hole the tag exists to close.

clauses.title: Docs and types land together
clauses.body: : the template-tag overload in `index.d.ts`, `docs/api/javascript/` spec + description + a tested example, the README, the CLI bundle's `client-javascript.md` reference, the npm-bundled library skill, and the CHANGELOG.

clauses.title: Front validation (primary)
clauses.body: `validate_aggregation_semantics` (`cypherlite-front/src/validate/aggregation/mod.rs`) gains `check_aggregate_arity`: every single-input aggregate call (`sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `collect`, after canonical-alias resolution) with an argument count other than one raises `ErrorKind::InvalidNumberOfArguments`, modeled on Neo4j's 42I13 (it names the function and the expected signature). It runs over the RETURN/WITH item expressions, the GROUP BY keys and the ORDER BY expressions, riding the module's shared expression …

clauses.title: Executor defense (secondary)
clauses.body: `agg_eval` replaces the constant-`1` empty-argument arm with an `InvalidNumberOfArguments` error, checked before the row loop so an empty group cannot slip a zero-argument call through. No IR construction — the planner-ir diagnostic parser included — can evaluate a zero-argument aggregate.

clauses.title: Document → system_ontologies graph
clauses.body: Document → `system_ontologies` graph Every node and relationship in the derived graph carries the property `ontology :: STRING` with the value `'neo4j'` (ADR-0121 §5), naming the database the stored ontology belongs to. The graph mirrors the document as written, one graph element per document construct: Absent optional fields produce absent graph properties (the spec's "absent means none"). The shorthand flags stay flags: they are boolean properties on `:OntologyProperty`, and only explicit constraint objects …

clauses.title: Ontology → graph type (db.ontology.apply)
clauses.body: Ontology → graph type (`db.ontology.apply`) The split follows the spec's enforcement table. **Enforceable** fields compile into the graph-type body: Node entries: identifying label from `label` or `labels.identifier`, implied labels from `labels.implied` — the CIP-176 `(:<Ident> => :<Implied&…> { … })` form, with the local id as the element alias where endpoint references need it. Property `type` tokens map to the CIP-176 value type of the same name: bare scalars as-is, `LIST<X>` to the corresponding list type …

clauses.title: How apply fails on violating data
clauses.body: How apply fails on violating data Like all four procedures (ADR-0227, following CIP-287), `db.ontology.apply` takes no database argument: it reads the stored ontology of, and sets the graph type on, the database it is executed against — the session database or the `USE` target — which ADR-0121 §2's rule restricts to `neo4j` (`system` and `system_ontologies` reject the procedures before this point). It validates first, then commits: It builds the resulting graph-type body through the mapping in (2) and derives its …

clauses.title: Only on success does the existing SET path run: the
clauses.body: Only on success does the existing SET path run: the SET purge, `sync_derived_constraints`, and the `RedoOp::SetCurrentGraphType` push (`TheaterData::set_current_graph_type` on commit). Validation and the catalog write are computed from the same captured snapshot and commit atomically under the store's normal commit protocol. The mapping itself (document model → graph-type body) lives in `cypherlite/cypherlite-ontology` (ADR-0121 §6); the snapshot scan lives in `cypherlite-executor` next to …

clauses.title: Signatures follow CIP-287
clauses.body: `db.ontology.set(ontology :: STRING)`, `db.ontology.get(format = "yaml" :: STRING) :: (ontology :: STRING)`, `db.ontology.drop()` and `db.ontology.apply()`. There is no database argument: each procedure acts on the database it is executed against — the session database or the `USE` target (ADR-0116 §3). Executed against `system` or `system_ontologies`, the procedures fail with ADR-0121 §2's `Ontologies can only be stored for the user database 'neo4j'.`, now applied to the session/USE target rather than to a …

clauses.title: JSON or YAML in; the stored bytes stay verbatim
clauses.body: `set` accepts a document in JSON or YAML 1.2. The submitted string is stored verbatim — ADR-0120 §1's "the validated ontology JSON kept verbatim" is amended to "the validated ontology document, JSON or YAML, kept verbatim" — and the ADR-0120 §3 16 MiB envelope limit applies to the submitted string regardless of syntax. The store records no JSON-vs-YAML marker — only the bytes.

clauses.title: `get` returns the requested format
clauses.body: `format` is `"yaml"` (the default — CIP-287's choice: more compact than JSON, so cheaper in agent context) or `"json"`; any other value fails with an argument error naming the two. When the requested format matches the stored one, `get` returns the stored bytes unchanged — YAML in, YAML out, comments and formatting included; likewise JSON. Otherwise it parses the stored document into the value model of (4) and serializes it canonically in the requested format: compact UTF-8 for JSON, block style with two-space …

clauses.title: One parse path
clauses.body: The string is parsed once as YAML 1.2 (a superset of JSON) into a JSON-equivalent value model: maps with string keys in source order, lists, strings, integers, floats, booleans, null. Source key order is preserved — ADR-0226's deterministic id assignment and (3)'s canonical serialization depend on it. Anything outside that model — non-string mapping keys, custom tags, non-finite floats — is rejected at parse time. Validation, version gating, graph derivation and format conversion all consume this one model, so …

clauses.title: YAML crate: `saphyr`
clauses.body: `cypherlite/cypherlite-ontology` depends on `saphyr` (with `saphyr-parser`) for YAML parsing and serialization. R6 justification: pure safe Rust, no build script and no native code, a small transitive tree, YAML 1.2 semantics matching the spec's examples, and the actively maintained line of the yaml-rust family. `set` never re-serializes; the only product-path serialization is a converting `get` (3), which emits from the parsed value model and leaves the stored bytes alone.

clauses.title: Hand-rolled validation against the vendored schema
clauses.body: The pinned draft schema is vendored as `ontology-graph-spec.schema.json` in `cypherlite/cypherlite-ontology` (source: `neo4j/graph-spec` @ `2f8dcbdf2dab51ebf2d760e00904a8f2b0518f59`, the same pin ADR-0226's mappings target). Validation is hand-rolled structural checking of exactly that schema, over the value model from (4): the required root fields (`schema`, `id`, `version`); `additionalProperties: false` at the levels the schema pins; `version`, `dimension` and the endpoint count fields as integers with their …

clauses.title: Spec-version gate
clauses.body: The root `schema` field must equal exactly `https://neo4j.com/ontology-graph-spec/1.0.0/schema.json` — the pinned 1.0.0 draft — and is checked before structural validation, so a newer-version document fails with the version error rather than incidental structural errors. Any other value fails with `Unsupported ontology spec version: '<uri>'.
