clauses.title: `--timeout DURATION` bounds each statement's wall-clock time
clauses.body: The grammar is a bare number of seconds or a number with an `ms`/`s`/`m` suffix; fractions are allowed (`1.5s`). `0` (any unit) disables the bound, matching `--max-rows 0`. The flag parses in every bundle and is a query-run flag only — lifecycle commands never run it. clauses.title: Enforcement is the engine's cancellation, not a client-side guess
clauses.body: The CLI spawns a watchdog thread per timed statement that cancels an ADR-0111 `CancelToken` after the duration; the query runs through `query_with_params_cancellable` and aborts at the next cancel point. The watchdog retires the instant the statement finishes, so it never outlives what it watches. Cancellation is cooperative: a pathological plan that never reaches a cancel point can overshoot, as with any cooperative scheme.

clauses.body: The scheduled browser-smoke lane's from-source `cargo install wasm-pack --version 0.13.1 --locked` (~2–4 min of compile) is replaced by a prebuilt install via `taiki-e/install-action` at the same pinned version, and `scripts/install-wasm-bindgen.sh` learns the same prebuilt-first path (falling back to the `cargo install --locked` build when no prebuilt tarball exists for the host) — the npm-smoke and cookbook lanes were each spending ~2 min compiling wasm-bindgen-cli per run.

clauses.title: No per-row Value clones
clauses.body: The scan collects `(element_id, score)` pairs only. `Value::Node`/`Value::Relationship` is materialized solely for the ≤ `offset + limit` window survivors at the end. When CIP-235 `WITH` filters are present, a `Value` is materialized per *filter-checked* candidate (as before) because `vector_filter_passes` evaluates properties through the expression evaluator — the filtered path keeps today's per-row clone, the common unfiltered path drops it.

clauses.title: Bounded binary heap of size `offset + limit`
clauses.body: replaces the full sort. Ordering contract is unchanged: score descending, then element id ascending on ties (`sort_and_window`'s comparator), realized as a min-heap whose root is the worst retained candidate. `SKIP`/`OFFSET` and `LIMIT` windows therefore cost `O(n log k)` and no full-length collect.

clauses.title: Scan-path kernels over Value coordinate lists, no per-row
clauses.body: The scan scores candidates straight from the property's `Value` list — eight partial-sum lanes for the dot, the candidate norm, or the squared distance — with the query norm hoisted once per search. The per-candidate `Vec<f64>` allocation of `vector_operand` is gone from the scan (query-side parsing keeps it). The float32-rounding contract of the CIP-121/CIP-214 scores (Neo4j parity) is preserved: an equivalence test asserts the kernels round to the same `f32` value as the sequential pre-ADR-0256 reference over …

clauses.title: No index structure
clauses.body: (no IVF, no bit quantization, no MRL tricks) ships in this change; all three remain rejected at embedded scale per the #311 benchmarks, and any future approximate path must layer on top of this scan (prefilter + exact rescore), not replace it.

clauses.title: Max query-text size: 4 MiB (4 194 304 bytes)
clauses.body: Enforced in `cypherlite_parser::parse`, *before lexing*. The single choke point covers the Rust API, the C ABI, the CLI, the TCK, and Bolt with one check. 4 MiB is far above any legitimate hand-written or generated analytical query we know of, and bounds worst-case token amplification at ~65–90× to ~270–380 MB of transient allocation — large but finite and survivable, versus unbounded today. (The lexer amplification constant can be reduced later as perf work; see Alternatives.)

clauses.title: Max nesting depth: 500
clauses.body: Enforced in two places: the parser (expression/primary nesting) and the front-end lowering boundary (statement/structural nesting). The value must sit comfortably *below* the empirically observed abort thresholds — ~1000 nested `NOT`s in front-end lowering and ~5000 nested parens in the parser — with margin, because debug builds use substantially larger stack frames and must not abort under test. 500 gives ~2× headroom against the tightest observed threshold (~1000) and ~10× against the parser threshold, on …

clauses.title: Runner: `opencode run` (OpenCode V2 CLI) headless in GitHub Actions
clauses.body: The review is a headless OpenCode invocation with a skill-driven prompt, not claude-code-action. OpenCode shells out to `gh` for PR commenting.

clauses.title: Model: `fireworks-ai/accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k3` (Kimi K3)
clauses.body: The shorthand `fireworks-ai/kimi-latest` does not resolve on a cold runner — it is not a models.dev catalog key — so the pinned catalog ID is used. Authentication is a `FIREWORKS_API_KEY` repository secret surfaced through the models.dev catalog environment variable (verified against the catalog). One secret covers all three review workflows.

clauses.title: Skills vendored in-repo at `.agents/skills/`
clauses.body: The three review skills live at `.agents/skills/{stellar-review,rust-reviewer,security-review}/SKILL.md` — a path OpenCode V2 discovers natively as a project skill source. stellar-review is copied from neo4j-cli; rust-reviewer and security-review come from the author's local OpenCode skill set.

clauses.title: One workflow per skill
clauses.body: Three workflows — `.github/workflows/opencode-review-stellar.yml`, `opencode-review-rust.yml`, and `opencode-review-security.yml` — each running exactly one review per skill per push, so each review kind is an independent check. The three are thin `pull_request` callers of one shared reusable workflow (`.github/workflows/opencode-review-reusable.yml`, `on: workflow_call`) so the shared steps live in exactly one place; this does not change the separation — each caller is its own workflow, run, and check, and the …

clauses.title: Severity gate: Critical/High/Medium fails
clauses.body: A review fails its check when any finding is Critical, High, or Medium; a review with only Low findings or no findings passes. The gate is enforced fail-closed by `.github/scripts/enforce-opencode-verdict.sh`, ported from neo4j-cli's `enforce-claude-verdict.sh`: verdict file → `<!-- opencode-verdict: ... -->` HTML comment → marker-line phrase → fail-closed error. If any stage of that chain is missing or malformed, the check fails rather than silently passing.

clauses.title: Comments as `github-actions[bot]` via `GITHUB_TOKEN`
clauses.body: No GitHub App or OAuth token exchange; the workflow's built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` is sufficient for OpenCode's `gh`-based commenting. Each review kind keeps exactly one summary comment per PR via discover-then-edit: the workflow finds its own previous summary comment (identified by a marker) and edits it in place instead of posting a new one.

clauses.title: Reviews are read-only
clauses.body: Findings are posted as comments only; the review never commits or pushes to the PR branch.

clauses.title: Prompts and scripts maintained in-repo
clauses.body: Review prompts live under `.github/prompts/` and the enforcement script under `.github/scripts/`, versioned with the workflows that use them.

clauses.title: Bolt genericizes `Internal`, `Storage`, `Io`, `Locked`
clauses.body: A `FAILURE` for one of these variants carries the fixed client message `internal error` and the status code `CypherLite.InternalError`. The original `e.to_string()` is written to the server's own stderr (`eprintln!`) so operators keep full detail. No path, errno, panic payload, or OS text reaches the client.

clauses.title: Bolt passes every other variant through verbatim
clauses.body: `Syntax`, `Semantic`, `Type`, `Execution`, `Conflict`, and `Capacity` keep their own message under the existing pinned code `CypherLite.Error`. The `write-write conflict` (Conflict) and `capacity exceeded: …` (Capacity) messages remain exactly as pinned in `docs/api/bolt/spec.md`, and the unknown-tag `FAILURE` is unchanged.

clauses.title: The generic code uses the `CypherLite` namespace, not `Neo.*`
clauses.body: **The generic code uses the `CypherLite` namespace, not `Neo.*`.** Bolt is a transport (ADR-0057), not Neo4j feature parity; CypherLite does not claim Neo4j's status-code taxonomy. The genericized code is `CypherLite.InternalError`, consistent with the existing `CypherLite.Error`.

clauses.title: cypherlite-load strips userinfo before formatting URI errors
clauses.body: The missing-host and missing-scheme messages in `query_api_url` redact the `user:pass@` userinfo component before the URI is interpolated, so no credential reaches stderr. The rest of the message and the parse behavior are unchanged. This is a boundary-hygiene change only: the engine still produces typed errors with full messages, and server-side diagnostics are not reduced.

clauses.title: Foreign targets are never touched
clauses.body: Each Foreign target is reported with the `foreign_note` line and the `foreign_remediation` line. A `--force` flag never reaches a Foreign directory from inside `upgrade`.

clauses.body: With no Foreign target present: one `skill install` spawn, passing `--force` iff any target is Legacy (the common case — both the marker and the frontmatter name are cypherlite's own, so forcing only ever replaces our content). With a Foreign target present: **one `skill install --agent <name>` spawn per non-foreign agent**, passing `--force` iff *that* agent is Legacy. Targeting each agent individually keeps the forced replacement scoped to our own directories so a force never reaches the Foreign dir.

Non-interactive without `--yes`: print `hint_install` and install nothing. The upgrade exit code stays **0** in every post-replace path. A failed skill install never undoes the binary upgrade: it warns and the upgrade still reports success. The four pinned message templates …

clauses.title: `release-notes.yml` gains a `workflow_call` trigger
clauses.body: Inputs: `version` (required string, the bare `X.Y.Z` version) and `publish` (boolean, default `false`). The existing `workflow_dispatch` dry-run trigger is kept unchanged. The dead `release: [published]` trigger is dropped.

clauses.body: It has `needs: [version, create-release]` and calls `./.github/workflows/release-notes.yml` with `with: {version: <bare X.Y.Z>, publish: true}` and `secrets: inherit`, so notes generation runs explicitly after the release exists — mirroring how the inline `docs` job ("Sync installer to gh-pages") is chained with `needs:` in the same pipeline.

clauses.title: Harness
clauses.body: Adopt `proptest = "1.11"` and `proptest-state-machine = "0.8"` as **dev-dependencies of `cypherlite/cypherlite-storage` only**. They are not added to any crate's normal dependency list and not to any other engine crate. A later need in a different crate gets its own ADR.

clauses.title: rand dual-major, test build only
clauses.body: Accept the second rand major. The workspace stays on `rand 0.8`; only the `cypherlite-storage` test build links `rand 0.9` through proptest. No test may pass a `rand 0.8` `Rng` into a proptest strategy or vice versa; a test that seeds both an engine RNG and a proptest generator keeps the two streams separate. Bumping the workspace to `rand 0.9` is a separate change and not implied by this one.

clauses.title: Regression files committed
clauses.body: `.proptest-regressions` files (one per test source, proptest's `SourceParallel` persistence) are committed to the repository. A counterexample is a permanent regression test. No `.proptest-regressions` file is deleted, or its entries removed, without a tracked reason (an issue or a later ADR); `PROPTEST_DISABLE_FAILURE_PERSISTENCE` must not be set in CI.

clauses.title: R6 does not apply
clauses.body: proptest is a *dev*-dependency, and its tree is light: no native/C++ build, no async runtime, no networking, and a handful of small pure-Rust crates (the six listed above, plus optional `regex-syntax`/`rusty-fork`/`tempfile` only if those features are enabled). That is below R6's heavy-dependency trigger. This ADR is still recorded because the rand-major split and the committed-regression-file policy are decisions worth having in the log, not because R6 compels it.

Round N+1 scope is exactly: units whose hash changed, plus units whose **dependencies' public signatures** changed, plus units carrying still-open findings (for a closed-form "addressed? yes/no" resolution check — not a re-review). Every other unit is **sealed**: it cannot produce new findings that round. Waived findings stay waived until their unit changes. …

clauses.body: The CI ledger round-trips as a trimmed block inside the existing self-updating `github-actions[bot]` summary comment (hidden HTML comment), read and written by scripts — not by the model. Unit state is stored compactly (`uid → "hash:sighash"`); past a size budget the block is zlib+base64 compressed, and at the extreme the unit map is dropped entirely — sealing then degrades to merge-base-relative scoping (bigger rounds, never wrong), because units absent from the ledger count as changed only when they differ from …

clauses.title: Static review agents, no prompt pasting
clauses.body: The review passes become project agent definitions (`.opencode/agents/stellar-*.md`, mirrored to `.claude/agents/` for local Claude runs) whose own prompt text carries their mandate and doctrine. The orchestrator dispatches them with a short pointer prompt (facts file, assigned units) instead of serially generating the doctrine into every sub-agent prompt. The old `orchestration` pass is absorbed into the sites-based boundaries mandate; a **comparison pass** replaces the verify pass — it receives similarity groups …

clauses.title: Closed-form judgment over facts, not diff search
clauses.body: Passes receive the facts pack and their assigned unit list with pre-extracted context, and emit verdicts per checklist item. Open-ended "read the diff and find problems" — the low-recall, high-variance mode that caused the trickle — is no longer part of the pipeline.

clauses.title: Scripted posting and verdict
clauses.body: The model's only output artifact is `.stellar/findings.json` (schema-validated). A poster script (`tools/post.py`) dedupes findings, maps severities (blocker → High, medium → Medium, nit → Low), posts all inline comments in **one** `POST /repos/.../pulls/N/reviews` call, writes `.opencode-verdict.txt` itself, and updates the summary comment (discover-then-edit) including the ledger block. The model never calls `gh` for posting and never writes the verdict; the existing fail-closed enforcement chain (ADR-0258) is …

clauses.title: Shared core for CI and local use
clauses.body: The same tools and agent definitions drive the GitHub workflow and local invocations of the `stellar-review` skill; CI only adds the ledger-in-comment round-trip and the posting step. The gbuild plugin's auditor is unaffected and may adopt the machinery later, in its own repository.

The principal rides the existing internal context channel: `Connection` stores it, `run_query`/`dispatch` pass it into the executor's `ExecCtx` …

clauses.title: Docs burden
clauses.body: The two new public methods ship with the full AGENTS.md §2 treatment on the `rust` surface: `docs/api/rust/spec.md` (contract: `set_principal`/`principal`, lifecycle, that the value is display-only and confers no authorization), `docs/api/rust/description.md`, and a runnable doctest example; `docs/api/bolt/` documents the per-mode table above, including that `--auth none` never forwards the unverified HELLO principal. The implementing node writes these; this ADR mandates them.

clauses.title: The poster enforces scope
clauses.body: `post.py post` drops any new finding whose `unit` is not in the round's `review_units` (or, for unit-less file-level findings, whose `path` is not in `review_files ∪ dependency_dirty_files`). Dropped findings never enter the ledger, never count toward the verdict, and are reported in the summary ("Dropped by the scope filter: N"). Without a scope document the filter is off — the same documented permissive bootstrap as resolutions.

clauses.body: In round ≥ 2 (`scope.full == false`), a new finding's line range must intersect a hunk of the `last_head…head` diff. clauses.title: `lab` is a new first-positional command word
clauses.body: in the hand-rolled `cypherlite` parser, alongside the ADR-0069 lifecycle verbs. Its shape is `cypherlite lab <action> [--flags]`. A database path literally named `lab` stays reachable via a `./` prefix or after `--`, exactly as ADR-0069 provides for `skill`, `upgrade`, and `update`.

clauses.title: lab is reserved in every build, including builds where its
clauses.body: (ADR-0104 rule 4). A build without the `lab` feature recognizes `cypherlite lab …` as a command and prints the shared not-included error with exit 2; it never falls through to opening a database named `lab`. The escape hatch (`./lab` or `-- lab`) is identical in every build.

clauses.title: Actions are either visible or hidden
clauses.body: A **visible** action is listed in the hand-written `--help` text and in the command tables of `docs/api/cli/spec.md`, and is covered by tests. A **hidden** action works, but is deliberately never listed in `--help` or in any spec table. It is an easter egg: not part of the documented surface, and not owed compatibility or a changelog entry. Hidden actions still get tests, because no behavior ships without tests (AGENTS.md §4). The first visible action is `fs-to-graph` (ADR-0157). The first hidden action is `neo`.

clauses.title: `--help` lists only visible actions that are compiled in
clauses.body: A build with the `lab` feature lists `lab fs-to-graph` and never `lab neo`; a build without the feature lists `lab` only as a recognized, not-included command (or omits it, matching how ADR-0104 handles other gated commands).

If the pinned openCypher TCK corpus contains scenarios for these positions they join the allowlist per the AGENTS.md §4 procedure; no scenario moves to the skip list.

clauses.title: Documentation
clauses.body: `inf`/`nan`/`infinity` are documented as CIP-55 float-literal keywords that resolve to literals in expression position even when a variable of that name is in scope, with the backtick escape as the workaround, alongside the JSON-mode encoding note in `docs/api/cli/spec.md`.

clauses.title: `cypherlite clone SOURCE DEST` covers the full dir/`.cl` matrix
clauses.body: : dir → dir (unchanged, ADR-0156), dir → `.cl`, `.cl` → dir, and `.cl` → `.cl`. The format of each side is inferred from the `.cl` suffix on its path — the same classification `Database::open` applies everywhere — so there is no `--format` flag.

clauses.title: One engine API: `Database::clone(source, dest, CloneOptions)`
clauses.body: It replaces `clone_directory`, `snapshot_to_bundle`, and `restore_from_bundle`; `SnapshotOptions` goes away with them. `CloneOptions.wal_dir` names the source's external WAL and is rejected with `Error::Storage` when the source is a `.cl` bundle — a bundle embeds its WAL, so ADR-0160's rationale carries into the fold.

clauses.body: The command leaves `COMMAND_WORDS` in `surfaces/cypherlite-cli/src/flags.rs`, the `--to`/`--from` snapshot parsing and docs rows go with it, and there are no deprecation shims or migration hints: the verb shipped in internal releases only, so it breaks cleanly. clauses.title: The shared machinery stays
clauses.body: `publish.rs`, the storage `OpenMode`/`OpenAdmit` layer, the ADR-0136 frozen read-only source open, and ADR-0161's exclusive, crash-safe destination creation are unchanged; clone keeps depending on them in all four directions. clauses.body: — errors, usage text, and the `DESTINATION_EXISTS`-prefixed publish messages name `clone`, never `snapshot`.

clauses.body: The FFI reads result rows (column count/name, row count, value JSON) and nothing else; the one existing result-metadata field, `namespace` (ADR-0117 §7), has no accessor. `query_type` follows that precedent.

clauses.title: stderr shows the caret
clauses.body: For a syntax error whose message has the first shape, stderr prints the first line exactly as before (up to and including the message, so existing greps keep matching), then the excerpt and the caret on their own lines, indented two spaces, as the parser rendered them: … Every character of the excerpt passes through the same sanitizer as any other engine text: control characters are removed and the excerpt stays one line, so the safety property of `print_error` is unchanged. The caret is rebuilt from the column …

clauses.title: The envelope gains optional fields
clauses.body: For a syntax error, `error.column` (1-based, in characters of the echoed line) and `error.source` (the echoed line, sanitized) are added when the message has the first shape; `error.line` and `error.column` are added from `at line L, col C` when it has the second shape and `L` is at least 1. A field is absent, never `null` or `0`, when the position is unknown. `message` keeps its current flattened text. The fields are additive: existing ones are never renamed.

clauses.title: `line` is statement-relative
clauses.body: The parser numbers lines within the statement it was given, and the first shape does not carry one at all, so the envelope does not invent a script line number. A caller that needs the script position of a statement tracks statement boundaries itself (per- statement progress, LABS-240, is the place that can report it).

clauses.title: Recovery is by shape, and falls back
clauses.body: Recognition is a single function over the engine text. Anything that does not match either shape is reported exactly as today: flattened message, no position, no extra stderr lines.

clauses.title: Scope
clauses.body: Syntax errors from the query run only, as in ADR-0194. Other error kinds, the lifecycle commands and the interactive shell are unchanged.

clauses.title: Extras
clauses.body: : the suite gains an `extras` module — plain-Cypher rewrites of the skipped apoc statements, one per rewritten adoc block, keyed by the original adoc line. They run differentially (both engines, same comparison as adoc statements) after every adoc statement of the dataset, so the extras' writes (the `apoc.periodic.iterate` rewrite) cannot shift any adoc comparison. Extras carry `apoc: false`: they are plain queries, not part of the apoc capture.

clauses.title: Coverage policy
clauses.body: : rewrite only what plain Cypher 25 expresses **and** the engine runs today — probed against the built CLI before an extra is added. The blocked and not-rewritable functions are documented in the module with their reasons (LABS-261 for `date.format`); their extras join when the blocker lands.

clauses.title: Schema DDL runs
clauses.body: : `CREATE INDEX` / `CREATE CONSTRAINT` leave `DIALECT_PREFIXES` and classify as plain statements. A syntax the reference accepts but the engine rejects surfaces as a DIFF, not a skip — the skip list only shrinks (ADR-0144's contract).

clauses.title: Apoc statements stay skipped
clauses.body: until PR #105 merges; then, with `CYPHERLITE_GRAPH_EXAMPLES_APOC=1`, they run on both engines. The extras do not replace that — they are the apoc-free ground truth the implementation is additionally tested against, and they keep running after apoc lands (a regression in `coll.max` or `count {}` must still fail the walkthrough shape).

clauses.title: Changed-files focus is a script invariant
clauses.body: `compute_scope` treats a unit as changed only if it differs from the merge base *and* from the ledger; a rebase can no longer dirty code the PR did not touch. `tools/incremental.py` computes the anchoring diff from the smallest covering base: `last_head` if an ancestor, else `merge-base(last_head, head)`, else none (empty patch, ledger-hash scope) — never the main merge-base — restricted to PR-changed files.

Clusters that touch files under human work are held, not dropped. The planner only emits runnable work inside 03:00–07:00 Europe/Berlin (DST-aware) unless forced; 25+ open findings sets `escalate`.

Existing `nightshift/<key>` branches/PRs are skipped (work in …

clauses.title: Prevention over review
clauses.body: The top recurring patterns from the #263/#278/#288/#295 rounds are codified in AGENTS.md and the stellar checklist; `tools/recurrence.py` reports recurrence per checklist id.

clauses.title: Squash before review
clauses.body: Stellar rounds assume one squashed commit per PR; `stellar-prep.sh` emits a CI warning when a PR has more than one commit.

clauses.title: A dedicated branch named `ADR-NUMBER-MINT-DO-NOT-DELETE`
clauses.body: holds a single file `NEXT` containing the next unclaimed four-digit ADR number. The branch is the single source of truth for numbering; it carries no other content.

clauses.title: Minting is performed by `scripts/adr_mint.py`
clauses.body: : fetch the counter branch; compute `claimed = max(NEXT, highest NNNN prefix in docs/adr on main + 1, 0300)`; commit `NEXT=claimed+1` with a commit message recording the claim (e.g. `claim 0300`); push `<commit>:refs/heads/ADR-NUMBER-MINT-DO-NOT-DELETE`. Git ref updates are atomic compare-and-swap on the server: a non-fast-forward rejection means a lost race — refetch, recompute, retry (bounded at 10 attempts).

clauses.title: Floor rule
clauses.body: : a minted number is never below 0300 — the claimed number is `max(NEXT, main's max prefix + 1, 0300)`, and the counter initializes `NEXT = max(main's max prefix + 1, 0300)`. The 0243–0299 range is headroom for in-flight branches that grabbed numbers under the old rule before the mint existed; a rebuilt counter also restarts at 0300, never lower.

clauses.title: Self-heal rule
clauses.body: : the minted number is never below the max prefix already merged on `main`, even if `NEXT` lags behind because someone added an ADR without minting.

clauses.title: Each pushed commit records the claimed number
clauses.body: , so the remote branch is an append-only ledger of claims; nobody else can claim the same or a smaller number.

clauses.title: The mint claims and records the number only
clauses.body: — the caller names its own `docs/adr/NNNN-<slug>.md` file.

clauses.title: A PR CI check
clauses.body: (`scripts/check_adr_numbers.py`, wired as an `adr-numbers` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`) flags conflicts from additions that bypassed the mint.

clauses.title: Every PR that adds an ADR carries a `Claim: <40-hex>` header line
clauses.body: in the ADR file, after the `Status:` line and before `## Context`. The SHA is the claim commit for that number on `ADR-NUMBER-MINT-DO-NOT-DELETE`.

clauses.title: `scripts/adr_mint.py` prints the claim SHA
clauses.body: as the second stdout line; the claimed number stays the first line, so a caller that reads only the first line is unaffected.

clauses.title: `scripts/check_adr_numbers.py` fails an added ADR
clauses.body: whose header is missing, whose SHA is not an ancestor of the counter-branch tip, or whose claim commit's subject is not `claim <same number>`.

clauses.title: The `adr-numbers` CI job explicitly fetches the counter branch
clauses.body: before running the checker, because the default checkout does not carry `ADR-NUMBER-MINT-DO-NOT-DELETE`.

clauses.title: Validity is time-independent
clauses.body: The proof references the append-only ledger, not `main`'s moving state: once a claim commit is on the ledger, "this number was minted" is a fact that cannot go stale when other PRs merge, so a green cannot be invalidated by a later merge and no merge queue is needed for ADR numbers. Exclusivity lives at authoring time in the mint's compare-and-swap push (ADR-0300), so a second PR can never mint the same number.

clauses.title: This ADR is the first proof-carrying one
clauses.body: : its own `Claim:` header proves itself, and the checker verifies it like any other.

clauses.title: A proposal 00 RR mm MM covers Bolt 4.4 when
clauses.body: A proposal `00 RR mm MM` **covers Bolt 4.4** when `MM = 4` and `mm - RR <= 4 <= mm`. The subtraction is unsigned and saturates at 0, so a range wider than the minor reaches down to minor 0. The reserved first byte is not inspected.

clauses.title: The first covering proposal, in client order, decides the reply,
clauses.body: The **first** covering proposal, in client order, decides the reply, which is `00 00 04 04`. The session then starts as before.

clauses.title: When no proposal covers 4.4, the reply is 00 00
clauses.body: When **no** proposal covers 4.4, the reply is `00 00 00 00`. The connection then closes without reading anything further and without starting a session. The server logs one stderr line naming the proposals.

clauses.title: Manifest proposals never match
clauses.body: `00 00 01 FF` has `MM = 0xFF`, so rule 1 rejects it. The server does not speak the manifest handshake, and a client that sends a manifest proposal next to `00 00 04 04` (or a range covering it) gets the plain 4.4 reply.

clauses.title: The selection is a pure function of the 16 proposal
clauses.body: The selection is a pure function of the 16 proposal bytes. The handshake's outcome is typed: serve, version unsupported (answered `00 00 00 00`, close), or aborted (the ADR-0141 deadline). It is not encoded as an error string.

clauses.title: The ADR-0141 deadline is unchanged. The 00 00 00 00
clauses.body: The ADR-0141 deadline is unchanged. The `00 00 00 00` reply is written inside the same negotiation phase as the 4.4 reply, under the same budget.

clauses.title: The Bolt compatibility corpus is boltkit-format .bolt scripts, with
clauses.body: The test harness is the client. It sends a script's `C:` lines to a real `cypherlite-bolt` process and checks the server's replies against the `S:` lines. Scripts live under `surfaces/cypherlite-bolt/tests/compat/scripts/`, and every `*.bolt` file found there recursively is part of the corpus. Each script runs against its own server, started through the `tests/common` `start_server`. The default flags are `--uri :memory: --auth none`, and a `!: SERVER_ARGS` line replaces them.

clauses.title: The grammar follows boltkit where it applies to a client,
clauses.body: Kept from boltkit: `!:`, `C:` and `S:` lines, continuation lines, JSON fields, the Bolt 4.4 message names, `0xNN` for any tag, and the `<RAW>`, `<NOOP>` and `<EXIT>` commands. Changed or added for the client side: `!: BOLT M.m` is the handshake the harness sends: the magic `60 60 B0 17` plus a single `00 00 m M` proposal, padded with zeros to four proposals. The harness then expects `00 00 m M` back. Without the line, the handshake proposes and expects `4.4`. `!: HANDSHAKE <hex>` sets the expected 4-byte reply. …

clauses.body: Tags must be equal. An expected map matches when every listed key is present with a matching value. Extra server keys are allowed, and the string `"*"` as a map value matches any value. Lists and structure fields match element by element under the same rules, and must have the same length. Scalars match exactly, and an Int never equals a Float. Summary metadata (`type`, `qid`, `t_first`, `bookmark`, `db`) differs from Neo4j's and changes as the server is fixed. Subset maps let each script assert only what its case …

Every read and write has a 10 s timeout, so a server that never answers fails the step instead of hanging the suite. The harness is the Rust integration-test target `bolt_compat` (`tests/bolt_compat.rs`, with the `tests/compat/` module tree). It reuses `tests/common` and the crate's own `packstream` and `protocol::read_message`, and adds no dependency. One test replays …

clauses.body: The four internal-class variants still reach the client only as the fixed message `internal error`, and the server still writes the full error to its stderr. Only their code changes.

The other Neo4j memory codes (`General.TransactionMemoryLimit`, `General.OutOfMemoryError`, `General.MemoryPoolOutOfMemoryError`) are `TransientError`s, and drivers retry those. A retry cannot free memory in an …

clauses.body: `Conflict` maps to the `TransientError` `Neo.TransientError.Transaction.Outdated`, so drivers' managed transactions retry it. The engine still never retries (ADR-0017).
