The executor raises it where it raised the `Type`/`Execution` strings. `ArithmeticFailure::detail()` returns the payload the old variant carried (`/ by zero`, …). `Error::DatabaseNotFound { …

clauses.title: The constants live in `failures.rs`
clauses.body: Each code is one `pub(crate) const` beside the mapping. `REQUEST_INVALID_CODE` sits directly after `UNAUTHORIZED_CODE`; the protocol-semantics decisions of this feature (ADR-0311, ADR-0313, ADR-0314) use the same constant.

clauses.title: Where the new variants are reported
clauses.body: ADR-0319 reports execution failures at the first PULL or DISCARD, classified by `fails_run` in `surfaces/cypherlite-bolt/src/results.rs`. `DatabaseNotFound` is compile-class there, like `ParameterMissing`, and fails the RUN; `Arithmetic` and `Cancelled` are execution failures, reported at the PULL or DISCARD. The code does not depend on where it is reported. Every code was checked against Neo4j's status-code list for 2026.09 (<https://neo4j.com/docs/status-codes/current/errors/all-errors/>) and `Status.java` in …

clauses.title: Where
clauses.body: `Connection::run_query` collects the parameter names the planned statement references (`cypherlite_planner::plan_parameter_names`, a walk of every clause and expression of the `LogicalPlan`, `NEXT` stages, subqueries and pattern payloads included). The check runs after planning and the compile-time gates, after the EXPLAIN early return, and before dispatch. So `EXPLAIN RETURN $p` still plans without values, as in Neo4j, and `PROFILE` checks like a normal run.

clauses.title: What
clauses.body: The error is `Error::ParameterMissing("Expected parameter(s): <names>")`, with each missing name once, in the order of first appearance in that walk, joined by `, `. It renders `semantic error: ParameterMissing: Expected parameter(s): p`. `Error::parameters_missing(names)` in `cypherlite-core` builds it. It is the one spelling of the message.

clauses.title: Nothing executes
clauses.body: No row, no write and no procedure call happens. In an explicit transaction the failure fails the transaction like any other statement error (ADR-0028), so it needs a rollback.

clauses.title: The executor fails too
clauses.body: The `Expr::Parameter` arm returns the same `parameters_missing` error instead of `null`. The plan walk covers every `Expr::Parameter` the plan holds, so the run-time arm only fires for expressions the walk cannot see: the parser-level expressions that catalog commands (`SHOW SETTINGS $p`, `OPTIONS {…}` maps) lower when they run. The catalog commands that read a parameter by name — a schema name (`CREATE INDEX $name …`), `OPTIONS $map`, `SHOW DATABASE $p` — return the same error for an absent parameter instead of a …

clauses.title: Unchanged
clauses.body: The implicit-procedure-arguments path keeps its `MissingParameter: implicit args for <name>` error and TCK Call1 [11]. Path-selector counts (`SHORTEST $k`) keep their existing `ParameterMissing` check. A parameter that is supplied with the value `null` is still `null`, including the `null`-argument rules of `SHOW SETTINGS` and `SHOW DATABASE` under `CYPHER 5` and `CYPHER 25`.

clauses.title: Every surface
clauses.body: The engine is the one policy, so the CLI, Python (`ProgrammingError`, class `ParameterMissing`), the C ABI and its clients, WASM, HTTP (`42N02`), MCP and Bolt (`Neo.ClientError.Statement.ParameterMissing`, ADR-0307) all report it with no surface change.

clauses.title: RUN SUCCESS
clauses.body: is `{fields, columnTypes, t_first}`, plus `qid` inside an explicit transaction (ADR-0311). `t_first` is the engine's `QueryResult.elapsed` in whole milliseconds: the time until the buffered result was available. RUN SUCCESS no longer carries `type`. This reverses ADR-0162 item 3.

clauses.title: A page that leaves records unread
clauses.body: (a PULL or DISCARD with `n` smaller than the remaining rows) answers exactly `{has_more: true}`.

clauses.title: The SUCCESS that ends a result
clauses.body: (the PULL or DISCARD that consumes its last row) carries `type` (`"r"`, `"w"`, `"rw"` or `"s"`, the ADR-0162 vocabulary, from `QueryResult.query_type`), `t_last` (whole milliseconds spent streaming or discarding the result, summed over its PULL and DISCARD messages) and `db` (the namespace the statement ran in, ADR-0117 §7). It adds `stats` when any counter is non-zero, and `bookmark` after an auto-commit statement (ADR-0310). A DISCARD that ends a read answers `{type: "r", t_last: 0, db: "neo4j"}` plus the …

clauses.title: `stats`
clauses.body: holds Neo4j's kebab-case counters, only the non-zero ones: `nodes-created`, `nodes-deleted`, `relationships-created`, `relationships-deleted`, `properties-set`, `labels-added`, `labels-removed`, `indexes-added`, `indexes-removed`, `constraints-added`, `constraints-removed`, plus `contains-updates: true` whenever any counter is present. A statement whose counters are all zero (every read) sends no `stats` key. The keys are derived from the canonical `cypherlite_model::wire::STAT_COUNTERS` table (snake_case to …

clauses.title: Engine change: schema counters
clauses.body: `QueryStats` gains `indexes_added`, `indexes_removed`, `constraints_added` and `constraints_removed`. The write overlay counts them where it records the schema change: an index created or dropped by index DDL, and a constraint created or dropped by constraint DDL (including the constraints a graph-type change derives or purges). The range index that backs a `UNIQUE`/`KEY` constraint is part of that constraint and does not count as an index. An `IF [NOT] EXISTS` statement that changes nothing counts 0.

clauses.title: Engine change: Neo4j's update counters
clauses.body: The existing label and property counters follow the openCypher TCK's graph diff: `labels_added` counts label *names* new to the graph (two `:A` nodes count 1), an overwrite counts one property set and one removed, and a deleted node counts its properties removed and, as the last carrier, its labels removed. Neo4j's counters, which drivers compare, count differently (`CREATE (:A), (:A)` is `labels-added: 2`; `DETACH DELETE` counts no labels or properties; `REMOVE n.p` is one `properties-set`). The TCK needs the …

clauses.title: `query_stats_to_wire`
clauses.body: renders Neo4j's counters: `labels_added` and `labels_removed` from the per-node counters, `properties_set` from `properties_written`, and the four schema counters, which it no longer hard-codes to 0. Bolt renders that same snapshot, so the HTTP, FFI, Python, MCP and WASM `stats` objects change with it (AGENTS result-metadata parity). The Rust `QueryStats` keeps both families.

clauses.title: Issued bookmarks
clauses.body: The SUCCESS that ends an auto-commit result (last PULL or DISCARD, ADR-0309) carries `bookmark` when the statement committed a write. COMMIT SUCCESS is `{bookmark}` (before, `{}`) when the transaction wrote, `{}` when it committed nothing. ROLLBACK SUCCESS stays `{}`. Inside an explicit transaction no PULL or DISCARD SUCCESS carries `bookmark`.

clauses.title: Value
clauses.body: `"cypherlite:<n>"`, where `n` is the engine's commit sequence (ADR-0502 §7): the value `QueryResult::bookmark` carries for an auto-commit write and `Connection::commit` returns for a transaction — the same value the C ABI's `cypherlite_result_bookmark` and `cypherlite_conn_commit` report. Bolt mints nothing: a statement or transaction that committed nothing (a read, a write that changed nothing, an empty transaction) carries no bookmark, because the engine reports none.

clauses.title: Received bookmarks
clauses.body: in the BEGIN or RUN extra `bookmarks` are accepted and ignored: there is no wait and no `InvalidBookmark` failure, because every bookmark is already satisfied.

clauses.title: Bookmarks are Bolt protocol data, not QueryResult metadata. The HTTP
clauses.body: Bookmarks are Bolt protocol data, not `QueryResult` metadata. The HTTP surface keeps ADR-0232's empty bookmarks array.

clauses.title: Inside an explicit transaction every RUN opens its own result
clauses.body: A later RUN never discards an earlier open one. This reverses ADR-0110's "a new RUN discards pending rows" for explicit transactions.

clauses.title: `qid`
clauses.body: RUN SUCCESS carries `qid: Int`, 0 for the first RUN after BEGIN and one more for each RUN in that transaction. A failed RUN uses no qid.

clauses.title: Addressing
clauses.body: `PULL {n, qid}` and `DISCARD {n, qid}` address the result with that qid. `qid` absent or `-1` means the most recent RUN's result. Each result keeps its own cursor and its own ending SUCCESS (ADR-0309). DISCARD honours `n` like PULL (`n = -1` discards the rest), so a DISCARD that leaves rows answers `{has_more: true}`.

clauses.title: A qid that names no open result
clauses.body: while other results are open answers FAILURE `Neo.ClientError.Request.Invalid` with the message `no open result with qid <qid>`, and the session enters the failed state. A PULL or DISCARD with no open result at all is a protocol breach (ADR-0314).

clauses.title: Lifetime
clauses.body: A result closes when its ending SUCCESS or its FAILURE is sent. COMMIT, ROLLBACK and RESET drop every result still open. BEGIN starts with no open results and restarts qids at 0.

clauses.title: Auto-commit is unchanged
clauses.body: An auto-commit RUN SUCCESS carries no `qid`, and a new auto-commit RUN replaces the previous result.

clauses.title: Memory cap
clauses.body: The ADR-0110 `--max-result-bytes` cap bounds the sum of the logical bytes of all open results on the connection. A RUN whose result would push the sum over the cap fails with the ADR-0110 message. Engine change: `cypherlite_core::logical_bytes_within` returns the summed logical bytes when they stay within a budget, with the same early stop as `logical_bytes_exceed`, which now delegates to it.

clauses.title: HELLO SUCCESS
clauses.body: is `{server, connection_id, hints: {"connection.recv_timeout_seconds": 120}}`. This reverses ADR-0293's hints-omitted bullet. `server` and `connection_id` are unchanged.

clauses.title: Keep-alive
clauses.body: While a request's engine work (RUN execution, or COMMIT) has gone one keep-alive interval without its reply, the server writes a NOOP chunk `00 00` and repeats it every interval until the reply is written. NOOPs go only between messages, never inside a chunked message: the reply is not started until the engine returns.

clauses.title: One constant pair
clauses.body: The interval is 60 s and the hint is twice the interval, in whole seconds rounded up. `ConnLimits.keep_alive_interval` carries the interval (default 60 s) so tests can inject a short one; it is a library knob, not a CLI flag. The hint is always derived from it.

clauses.title: Engine change (public Rust API)
clauses.body: `cypherlite::Heartbeat` is a callback the waiting caller runs on its own thread once per elapsed interval while a statement executes on the connection's query worker. It is built with `Heartbeat::every(interval, tick)`, which rejects a zero interval (ADR-0334; amended in place while this ADR is still `Proposed`). `Connection::query_staged` (ADR-0319) takes an optional heartbeat; `Connection::commit_with_heartbeat` takes one (a commit without a heartbeat is `commit`). The worker wait becomes a timed wait only when …

clauses.title: A NOOP write that fails (the client went away) stops
clauses.body: A NOOP write that fails (the client went away) stops further ticks; the request still completes, and the failed write closes the connection afterwards. The ADR-0110 idle timeout is unchanged.

clauses.title: A HELLO whose extra map has no string user_agent (absent,
clauses.body: A HELLO whose extra map has no string `user_agent` (absent, `null` or not a string) is rejected **before** the ADR-0126 auth check: FAILURE `{code: "Neo.ClientError.Request.Invalid", message: "Illegal value for field \"user_agent\": Expected value to be non-null"}`. No session opens and the ADR-0139 failed-auth delay does not apply.

clauses.title: The connection stays open in a rejected-HELLO state. Every message
clauses.body: The connection stays open in a **rejected-HELLO state**. Every message except HELLO and GOODBYE answers IGNORED. A second HELLO answers FAILURE `Neo.ClientError.Request.Invalid` with `Message of type HelloMessage cannot be handled by a session in the AUTHENTICATION state.`, and the server closes. GOODBYE closes.

clauses.title: A HELLO with a string user_agent behaves as before: the
clauses.body: A HELLO with a string `user_agent` behaves as before: the ADR-0126 auth check, then the ADR-0293 metadata (plus the ADR-0312 hints).

clauses.title: The code constant is REQUEST_INVALID_CODE in failures.rs, the one
clauses.body: The code constant is `REQUEST_INVALID_CODE` in `failures.rs`, the one line shared with the failure-code mapping work.

clauses.title: In-tree HELLO senders without user_agent (the bolt crate's test
clauses.body: In-tree HELLO senders without `user_agent` (the bolt crate's test helpers, the shared test-support helpers, the CLI's Bolt e2e tests and the dataset loadtest client) gain one.

clauses.title: The breach checks run in the Bolt session from its
clauses.body: The breach checks run in the Bolt session from its own state, before any engine call: COMMIT or ROLLBACK with no open transaction; BEGIN inside an open transaction; PULL or DISCARD with no open result at all (ADR-0311 covers a qid that misses while other results are open).

clauses.title: A breach answers exactly one FAILURE {code:
clauses.body: A breach answers exactly one FAILURE `{code: "Neo.ClientError.Request.Invalid", message: "Message of type <Name> cannot be handled by a session in the <STATE> state."}` and the server closes the connection without reading further. `<Name>` is Neo4j's message class name. `<STATE>` is the Neo4j 4.4 state the session is in: `READY` (no transaction, no open result), `STREAMING` (no transaction, an auto-commit result open), `IN_TRANSACTION` (a transaction, no open result) or `TX_STREAMING` (a transaction with open …

clauses.title: The ADR-0110 failed-state gate runs first, so in the failed
clauses.body: The ADR-0110 failed-state gate runs first, so in the failed state these messages answer IGNORED, not a breach. DISCARD joins the gate: in the failed state it answers IGNORED like PULL, as in Neo4j's FAILED state.

clauses.title: The code constant is REQUEST_INVALID_CODE in failures.rs (shared
clauses.body: The code constant is `REQUEST_INVALID_CODE` in `failures.rs` (shared with ADR-0313). The engine's `Connection::begin`/`commit`/`rollback` contract (ADR-0028) is unchanged; the session no longer reaches its "no transaction" and "already in a transaction" errors.

clauses.title: A message whose structure signature is not a Bolt 4.4
clauses.body: A message whose structure signature is not a Bolt 4.4 request, or a message that is not a structure at all, is a fatal decode error. The server sends no FAILURE, logs one stderr line naming the signature, and closes the connection at once.

clauses.title: The ADR-0126 pre-HELLO auth gate keeps precedence: before a validated
clauses.body: The ADR-0126 pre-HELLO auth gate keeps precedence: before a validated HELLO with auth enabled, any message other than HELLO and GOODBYE (an unknown one included) answers the Unauthorized FAILURE and closes, as before.

clauses.title: The request vocabulary is one typed enum in the session.
clauses.body: The request vocabulary is one typed enum in the session. The signature table, Neo4j's message class names (ADR-0314) and the decode step are derived from it, so no second list of tags exists.

clauses.title: This reverses ADR-0260 item 2's "the unknown-tag FAILURE is
clauses.body: This reverses ADR-0260 item 2's "the unknown-tag FAILURE is unchanged". ADR-0260's Later references note is added with the failure-code work that also revises that ADR.

clauses.title: An empty chunk received where a message would start is
clauses.body: An empty chunk received where a message would start is a NOOP. The server skips it and keeps reading. Any number of NOOPs may precede or separate messages.

clauses.title: A NOOP counts as connection activity for the ADR-0110 idle
clauses.body: A NOOP counts as connection activity for the ADR-0110 idle timeout: it re-arms the wait for the next message. It is not a message, so it gets no reply and does not change session state.

clauses.title: The NOOP rule lives in the one chunk-framing helper that
clauses.body: The NOOP rule lives in the one chunk-framing helper that both the server's message reader and the public `protocol::read_message` use, so test clients skip the server's ADR-0312 keep-alive NOOPs by the same rule.

clauses.title: The server frames every complete message already received before it
clauses.body: The server frames every complete message already received before it handles the next one. It reads from the socket into a connection buffer, and one read returns whatever has arrived; each batch is the complete messages in the buffer at that point.

clauses.title: When a batch contains a RESET, each message queued ahead
clauses.body: When a batch contains a RESET, each message queued ahead of the last RESET in the batch that has not started answers IGNORED (no RECORDs). RESETs in that range are answered normally (SUCCESS, rolling back an open transaction and clearing the failed state and open results), and the messages after the last RESET run normally. For one write of `RUN, PULL, RESET, RUN, PULL` the replies are IGNORED, IGNORED, SUCCESS, then the second RUN's SUCCESS, RECORD and SUCCESS.

clauses.title: HELLO and GOODBYE are never interrupted. The ADR-0126 pre-HELLO auth
clauses.body: HELLO and GOODBYE are never interrupted. The ADR-0126 pre-HELLO auth gate and the ADR-0315 fatal decode keep precedence.

clauses.title: A request already executing when RESET arrives is not interrupted:
clauses.body: A request already executing when RESET arrives is not interrupted: the connection thread runs it and has no concurrent reader.

clauses.title: The batched framing keeps the 16 MiB message cap (a
clauses.body: The batched framing keeps the 16 MiB message cap (a chunk header that would cross it fails before its body is read), the per-chunk idle deadline re-arm (ADR-0110), and NOOP skipping (ADR-0316).

clauses.title: ROUTE answers SUCCESS {rt: {servers: [{addresses: [<self>], role:
clauses.body: ROUTE answers `SUCCESS {rt: {servers: [{addresses: [<self>], role: "WRITE"}, {addresses: [<self>], role: "READ"}, {addresses: [<self>], role: "ROUTE"}], ttl: 300, db: <db>}}`.

clauses.title: db is the extra map's db when it names one
clauses.body: `db` is the extra map's `db` when it names one (a non-empty string), else the home database `"neo4j"`, the same default RUN and BEGIN use (ADR-0117 §7).

clauses.title: The roles come in the order WRITE, READ, ROUTE.
clauses.body: The roles come in the order WRITE, READ, ROUTE.

clauses.title: <self> (ADR-0140), ttl 300, the failed-state exemption and the
clauses.body: `<self>` (ADR-0140), `ttl` 300, the failed-state exemption and the ADR-0126 auth gate are unchanged.

clauses.title: This reverses ADR-0269's db default and role order.
clauses.body: This reverses ADR-0269's `db` default and role order.

clauses.title: Report point
clauses.body: A failure raised while executing an already planned statement (the engine's dispatch phase) is reported at the first PULL or DISCARD of that result. RUN answers `SUCCESS {fields: <planned columns>, columnTypes, t_first}` (plus `qid` in a transaction), with `columnTypes` `"ANY"` per column (ADR-0224's no-rows stamp: a failed execution yields no rows). The PULL or DISCARD then answers FAILURE with the error's code and message and no RECORDs, the result closes, and the session enters the failed state.

clauses.title: What still fails the RUN
clauses.body: Failures before execution: parse, semantic validation, planning, missing parameters, an unknown database, the ADR-0177 parameter conversion, and the ADR-0110 max-result-bytes cap.

clauses.title: The phase comes from the engine
clauses.body: Engine change (public Rust API): `Connection::query_staged(cypher, params, token, heartbeat)` returns `Err(error)` for a failure before dispatch, and `Ok(Executed)` otherwise. `Executed::Rows(QueryResult)` is a finished result; `Executed::Failed(ExecutionFailure)` carries the planned columns, their `ANY` column types, the query type, the namespace, the elapsed time and the error. The planned columns come from a new planner function, `cypherlite_planner::plan_output_names`, the same output-name analysis semantic …

clauses.title: One Bolt classification
clauses.body: A dispatch-phase error still fails the RUN when its typed variant is compile-class in Neo4j even though the engine raised it while executing: `Syntax`, `ProcedureNotFound` and `ParameterMissing`. Every other variant defers to PULL. This is one exhaustive `match` over `cypherlite::Error` in the Bolt session module, with no wildcard arm, so a new engine variant fails to compile until it is classified. No message text is inspected.

clauses.title: Transactions
clauses.body: The engine already marks an explicit transaction failed when a statement fails (ADR-0028 item 6), so a RUN or COMMIT sent before that PULL fails with the engine's `transaction failed; rollback required`.

clauses.title: ADR-0110 stays
clauses.body: RUN still executes eagerly and buffers; only the report point moves, so nothing is superseded.

clauses.title: Offset or region
clauses.body: A `DateTime` is a region datetime when its zone names an IANA region; every other zone (none, `Z`, a numeric offset, any other spelling) is offset only. The engine helper `cypherlite_core::temporal::zone_region` makes the call on the same `zone_kind` classification the ISO formatter uses, so the Bolt surface compares no strings.

clauses.title: Exact inverses
clauses.body: The fields are exactly what ADR-0177's decoders read, so a temporal parameter echoes back as the same structure. Examples: `date('2024-01-02')` is `0x44(19724)`, `time('03:04:05.123456789+01:00')` is `0x54(11045123456789, 3600)`, `datetime('2024-01-02T03:04:05.123456789+01:00')` is `0x46(1704164645, 123456789, 3600)`, `datetime('2024-01-02T03:04:05[Europe/Stockholm]')` is `0x66(1704164645, 0, "Europe/Stockholm")`, and `duration('P1Y2M3DT4H5M6.5S')` is `0x45(14, 3, 14706, 500000000)`.

clauses.title: Civil days
clauses.body: `CivilDate` and `CivilDateTime` reuse the engine's one days-from-civil count, `cypherlite_core::temporal::civil_epoch_days` (the count civil-date arithmetic already used).

clauses.title: Range
clauses.body: A component that does not fit a PackStream Int (i64), for example a duration whose seconds exceed i64, fails the encode with an error naming the structure. It never falls back to a string or a clamped value.

clauses.title: Vector and UUID results are unchanged: they stay strings (ADR-0272,
clauses.body: Vector and UUID results are unchanged: they stay strings (ADR-0272, CIP-246). Point results are ADR-0326.

clauses.title: The value
clauses.body: `cypherlite_core::Value` gains `Bytes(Arc<[u8]>)`, a shared payload like `String` (ADR-0170). No Cypher expression creates one. It enters only as a query parameter (the Bolt surface, or a Rust caller passing `Value::Bytes`) and flows through expressions, lists and maps into results.

clauses.title: Semantics
clauses.body: Equality, hashing and DISTINCT/grouping keys are byte-wise. Bytes never equal a list of the same integers. `<`/`>` compare byte-wise (element by element, then length, like a list). ORDER BY places BYTES directly after LIST: Neo4j orders a byte array as a sequence value. `valueType()` reports `LIST<INTEGER NOT NULL> NOT NULL` (`LIST<NOTHING> NOT NULL` when empty), and `IS :: LIST<INTEGER>` holds, as for a Neo4j byte array. `IS :: PROPERTY VALUE` is false. `toString()` rejects it like a homogeneous list …

clauses.title: Statement-scoped
clauses.body: Storing a byte array (or a list holding one) as a node or relationship property fails before any write with the typed `Error::TypeError` (Display `type error: TypeError: byte array values cannot be stored as node or relationship properties; they live only inside a statement (parameter to result)`). CREATE, MERGE, `SET n.p`, `SET n = map` and `SET n += map` share the one check (`check_property_value`). The tagged WAL/checkpoint encoder and the JSON snapshot bridge reject a byte array explicitly as a second line of …

clauses.title: Other surfaces
clauses.body: `CypherValue` (cypherlite-model) gets no new variant. `value_to_cypher` crosses a byte array as the `LIST<INTEGER>` of its byte values 0-255, the shape ADR-0219 already gives Python `bytes`, so the FFI clients (JS, Java, Go, C), Python, WASM, HTTP, MCP and the CLI render it as that list. `to_cypher_literal`, `to_display_string` and `to_json_plain` use the same list. None of those surfaces can supply a byte array today (their parameters are JSON or ADR-0219's list), so only a Rust embedder or Bolt reaches this …

clauses.title: A PackStream Bytes parameter, at any depth (top level, list
clauses.body: A PackStream Bytes parameter, at any depth (top level, list element, map value), decodes to `Value::Bytes` with the same bytes. ADR-0177's Bytes rejection and its message row are removed. The other ADR-0177 rules (struct tags, map keys, the params envelope) are unchanged.

clauses.title: A Value::Bytes result, at any depth, encodes as PackStream Bytes
clauses.body: A `Value::Bytes` result, at any depth, encodes as PackStream Bytes with the shortest length marker: `CC` up to 255 bytes, `CD` up to 65535, `CE` beyond.

clauses.title: The value is statement-scoped (ADR-0327): storing it as a property
clauses.body: The value is statement-scoped (ADR-0327): storing it as a property fails the statement with the typed `TypeError`, which Bolt answers as `Neo.ClientError.Statement.TypeError`. The spec cites the Linear follow-up "Engine: persist bytes (byte-array) values as node and relationship properties (WAL, snapshot and Parquet/JSON checkpoint codecs)".

clauses.title: Negotiation
clauses.body: When HELLO's extra has `patch_bolt` as a list and one of its string entries is `utc`, the connection applies the utc patch. HELLO SUCCESS then carries `patch_bolt: ["utc"]`. Only patches the server applies are echoed: unknown entries, non-string entries and a non-list `patch_bolt` apply nothing, and with no patch applied there is no `patch_bolt` key. The patch set is a typed per-session value, set by the HELLO that validates.

clauses.title: Results under the patch
clauses.body: An offset datetime encodes as `0x49` DateTimeUTC `[UTC epoch seconds, nanoseconds, offset seconds]`, a region datetime as `0x69` DateTimeZoneIdUTC `[UTC epoch seconds, nanoseconds, zone id]`. `datetime('2024-01-02T03:04:05.123456789+01:00')` is `0x49(1704161045, 123456789, 3600)`. Every other temporal structure (ADR-0325) is unchanged.

clauses.title: Parameters under the patch
clauses.body: `0x49` decodes with `utc = seconds + nanoseconds` and `zone: None`. `0x69` decodes the UTC instant and resolves the zone's offset at that instant, which is never ambiguous (the new engine helper `zone_offset_at_utc`, beside ADR-0178's wall-clock `zone_offset_at`). An unknown zone fails with ADR-0177's unknown-timezone message. The legacy `0x46`/`0x66` are rejected with ADR-0177's unsupported-struct message.

clauses.title: Without the patch
clauses.body: nothing changes: `0x49`/`0x69` stay rejected and results use `0x46`/`0x66`.

clauses.title: The session only stores the flag (set by the HELLO
clauses.body: The session only stores the flag (set by the HELLO that validates), echoes it and hands it to the one RECORD encoder (`results::write_record`) and to parameter decoding. The patch vocabulary and the structure choice live in the `patches` and `value_structs` modules.

clauses.title: deploy-pages.yml gains a workflow_call trigger. Its existing triggers
clauses.body: `deploy-pages.yml` gains a `workflow_call` trigger. Its existing triggers stay: pushes to `main`, `workflow_run` of a manually dispatched "Update website", and `workflow_dispatch`.

clauses.title: release.yml gains a deploy-pages job that calls it with
clauses.body: `release.yml` gains a `deploy-pages` job that calls it with `needs: [create-release, docs, update-website, publish-releases-json]`, that is, after every job that writes `gh-pages`. The caller job grants `contents: read`, `pages: write` and `id-token: write`, the permissions `actions/deploy-pages` needs.

clauses.title: The job runs unless the release run was cancelled, and
clauses.body: The job runs unless the release run was cancelled, and only if `create-release` succeeded: `if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.create-release.result == 'success' }}`. The deploy copies whatever `gh-pages` holds. When one writer fails (for example, the website agent), the files the other writers published still go live. The failed writer still fails the release run.

clauses.title: The pages concurrency group moves from workflow level to job
clauses.body: The `pages` concurrency group moves from workflow level to job level in `deploy-pages.yml`. It then applies to the job the same way whether the workflow is called or run on its own, as with `publish-releases-json.yml`.

clauses.title: The w vs rw criterion in cypherlite_planner::query_type
clauses.body: — `plan_output_names(plan)` non-empty. No write and no schema clause → `r`; schema DDL with no data clause alongside → `s`; a write with no returned columns → `w`; a write with returned columns → `rw`. This supersedes ADR-0162 item 2's "reads and data writes → `rw`" criterion; the rest of ADR-0162 (the `QueryResult.query_type` stamp, the pinned four-value set) is unchanged.

clauses.title: One place, no per-surface re-derivation
clauses.body: The classification stays the single plan-derived `query_type` in the planner; every surface reads the stamped `QueryResult.query_type` (Bolt's ending-SUCCESS `type`, the FFI's `cypherlite_result_query_type`, Python's `query_type`, the JS/Java/Go clients over the C ABI). A surface that recomputed the split from its own knowledge of the result would be a second classification table (AGENTS result-metadata alignment).

clauses.title: The shared access fold is unchanged
clauses.body: The write/schema flags and the schema-vs-data-mix decision (a schema clause mixed with data clauses across NEXT stages still counts as a write) keep coming from the one fold the ADR-0116 §4 namespace gate shares (`cypherlite_planner::access`); only its projection into the query type changes. A `CALL` of a writes-flagged procedure stays a write and — the built-in write procedures are all void, and a bare `CALL`'s plan-time output names are empty — a bare one stays `w`.

clauses.title: EXPLAIN and PROFILE keep reporting the wrapped statement's type
clauses.body: The classification is plan-based and pre-execution, so `EXPLAIN CREATE (n)` answers `w` (a write with no returned columns) without executing anything — unchanged behavior, now for the new criterion too.

clauses.title: The interval contract is enforced by construction
clauses.body: `Heartbeat::every(interval, tick) -> Result<Self>` is the only constructor; the fields are crate-private. A zero `interval` returns `Error::Semantic("heartbeat interval must be non-zero")` — a typed error, not a panic, so a surface with a configured interval (the Bolt server's `ConnLimits.keep_alive_interval`) can refuse the request instead of aborting a connection thread.

clauses.title: A tick panic cannot unwind the waiting frame while the worker runs
clauses.body: `JobSlot::wait_ticked` — the ticked half of `JobSlot::wait` — wraps each tick in `std::panic::catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(...))`, stashes the payload, stops ticking, and finishes the wait untimed — the timer is dropped with the tick, so no wakeup survives a dead tick. Only after the worker sets `finished` does `run_with_heartbeat` `resume_unwind` the payload. If the job also panicked in that window, the caller's tick panic takes precedence and the worker's stashed payload is cleared, so it cannot surface as a …

clauses.title: The wait keeps one discriminator
clauses.body: `JobSlot::wait` branches once on the single `Option<Heartbeat>`: `None` is the untimed `Condvar::wait`, `Some` hands the guard to `JobSlot::wait_ticked` for the timed loop over a plain `Instant` deadline. No mirrored `Option` pair is re-checked on every wake. A stashed tick panic breaks out of the timed loop into the same untimed wait for the rest of the job, so the mode can only change once, timed → untimed, and only for a tick that can never fire again: it panicked, or its deadline is unrepresentable.

clauses.title: The dead nullable mode is removed
clauses.body: `Connection::commit_with_heartbeat` takes `Heartbeat<'_>` non-`Option`; `commit()` remains the no-heartbeat path. The Bolt COMMIT arm and the docs use the constructor.

clauses.title: An unrepresentable deadline can neither fire nor panic
clauses.body: The timed loop computes each deadline with `Instant::checked_add`; when it returns `None` the tick is unreachable — every later `now` overflows too — so the wait drops the timer and finishes untimed, the same shape as the dead-tick path. The addition is fallible, so an oversized interval can never unwind the waiting frame.

clauses.title: One vocabulary
clauses.body: `cypherlite_core::Error::undefined_variable(name)` builds the error, rendering byte-identically to the front-end's scope-check error: `syntax error: UndefinedVariable: variable '<name>' not defined` (the front-end raises the same `EngineError::semantic(ErrorKind::UndefinedVariable, …)` text, which `lower_statement` maps to `Error::syntax`). The TCK bridge classifies it as `UndefinedVariable` through the same message scan as the plan-time error.

clauses.title: Both arms
clauses.body: `Expr::Variable` returns `Error::undefined_variable(name)` on a row miss; `MapProjectionItem::Variable` does the same instead of inserting `Value::Null`.

clauses.title: Run-time-lowered predicates surface it
clauses.body: `exec/catalog.rs`'s `project_catalog` WHERE filter propagates the evaluator's error instead of swallowing it (`matches!(eval(…), Ok(Value::Bool(true)))` treated every error as "row filtered out"). A `SHOW … WHERE` predicate that names no yielded column now fails the statement with the typed error.

clauses.title: A bound name is unchanged
clauses.body: The arm only changes a row miss; a variable bound to `null` still evaluates to `null`, and the row-sharing fast path (`eval_operand`, ADR-0170) is untouched.

clauses.title: The two sites with deliberately incomplete rows bind their names
clauses.body: Two executor paths evaluate expressions against rows that are legitimately missing names, and Neo4j reads those names as `null` there; each site now states that binding itself instead of relying on the evaluator's fallback: a quantification predicate sees a non-local singleton declared later in the pattern as `null` (CIP-28 [5], Neo4j-verified), so `gpm/qpp.rs` binds the predicate's unbound names to `null` for the evaluation row; a void `OPTIONAL CALL` over a zero-row driving table yields one unit row on which …

clauses.title: Error::Arithmetic's attribute becomes
clauses.body: `Error::Arithmetic`'s attribute becomes `#[error("{}", arithmetic_detail(.0))]`; `arithmetic_detail` composes the legacy full text: `TYPE_ERROR_PREFIX: / by zero` and `TYPE_ERROR_PREFIX: % by zero` for the division failures, the bare `ArithmeticError: rounding necessary` for `RoundingNecessary`.

clauses.title: TYPE_ERROR_PREFIX (the type error token) is the one spelling,
clauses.body: `TYPE_ERROR_PREFIX` (the `type error` token) is the one spelling, consulted by `Error::Type`'s `#[error("{}", type_error_display(.0))]` and by `arithmetic_detail` — the `CONSTRAINT_VALIDATION_FAILED` pattern.

clauses.title: ArithmeticFailure's Display becomes f.write_str(self.detail()):
clauses.body: `ArithmeticFailure`'s `Display` becomes `f.write_str(self.detail())`: `/ by zero`, `% by zero`, `ArithmeticError: rounding necessary`. `Error::Arithmetic(…).to_string()` is byte-identical to before, so the `cypherlite::Error` rendering, the Bolt status mapping (`ArithmeticFailure::detail()` is what ADR-0307's mapper reads) and the TCK bridge do not move. `ArithmeticFailure::detail()` is unchanged.

clauses.title: property_value_invalidity(v) -> Option<PropertyInvalidity> is the one
clauses.body: `property_value_invalidity(v) -> Option<PropertyInvalidity>` is the one walk: `None` when `v` can be stored, `Some(HoldsBytes)` when a byte array appears anywhere inside the value (a list nested at any depth included), `Some(Other)` for every other non-storable shape. A list is storable when its non-null items are one level of homogeneous scalar values; a nested list of scalars stays `Other`.

clauses.title: check_property_value(v) matches the verdict:
clauses.body: `check_property_value(v)` matches the verdict: `HoldsBytes` → the typed `TypeError` with `BYTES_PROPERTY_DETAIL` (module-private to `props.rs`), `Other` → `Type("InvalidPropertyType")`. `valid_property_value` is deleted; `sanitize_props` moves to `props.rs`.

clauses.title: Value::Vector { .. } stores without re-listing VectorCoordKind:
clauses.body: `Value::Vector { .. }` stores without re-listing `VectorCoordKind`: the policy is "any vector value stores".

clauses.title: The null-transparency contract lives once, on
clauses.body: The null-transparency contract lives once, on `check_property_value` (`Value::Null` is `Ok`): `write.rs` drops its dead `!val.is_null()` guards instead of re-stating the policy per call site.

clauses.title: One extra-accessor family
clauses.body: (`extra`, `extra_str`, `extra_int`) in `session.rs` replaces the four bespoke copies. `extra` is the one map lookup; `extra_str` extracts a non-empty string; `extra_int` returns `Result<Option<i64>, String>` where `None` means only "the key is absent" and a present value of another type is an error naming the found kind.

clauses.title: Absent keeps the documented default; present-but-malformed fails
clauses.body: A key that is absent (or an empty string, which every string field treats as absent) applies the documented default: `-1` for `n`/`qid`, the home database `neo4j` for `db`, the connection's local address for ROUTE's `address`. A present value of the wrong type fails the message with `Neo.ClientError.Request.Invalid` and the failed state, exactly like the ADR-0177 parameter path: `unsupported extra value for <key>: <kind> (must be an Int)`.

clauses.title: The RUN statement field is required
clauses.body: An absent or non-string statement is the same malformed-request failure: `unsupported request value for statement: <kind> (RUN statement must be a string)`, or `missing RUN statement (RUN statement must be a string)` when the field is absent. Nothing executes and the session enters the failed state.

clauses.title: An empty `user_agent` is rejected like an absent one
clauses.body: (ADR-0313): `extra_str` treats `""` as absent, and HELLO requires the field, so an empty string gets the same `Illegal value for field "user_agent"` text.

clauses.title: The -1 sentinel is only a default, never a malformed-value
clauses.body: , and the same policy covers `n` and `qid` (a malformed `qid` no longer silently addresses the most recent result).

clauses.title: `cypherlite::ResultHeader` (in `result.rs`) is the one home
clauses.body: for the result-metadata vocabulary: `columns`, `column_types`, `query_type`, `namespace`, `elapsed`.

clauses.title: Both result shapes embed it
clauses.body: `QueryResult { header: ResultHeader, rows, stats }` and `ExecutionFailure { header: ResultHeader, error }`. Construction stamps the same values as before; no behavior changes.

clauses.title: The field paths change with it
clauses.body: : `result.columns` becomes `result.header.columns`, and so on for the other four fields. This is a breaking change to the public Rust API of the released `cypherlite` crate; every in-tree consumer (the Bolt server, CLI, FFI, HTTP, load tool, MCP, Python bindings, the test harnesses and examples) is updated in the same change, and `docs/api/rust/spec.md` documents the new shape.

clauses.title: A PlanNode tree is the engine's plan representation for EXPLAIN
clauses.body: A `PlanNode` tree is the engine's plan representation for EXPLAIN and PROFILE: `{ id, operator, details, identifiers, children, estimated_rows, metrics { rows, db_hits, time_ns, memory_bytes } }`. Operator names follow the Neo4j vocabulary where a mechanism has an analog (NodeByLabelScan, NodeIndexSeek, Expand, VarLengthExpand, EagerAggregation, ProduceResults) and this engine's own names where it does not (FarNodeProbe, ExistsProbe, AggFold, GpmMatch, VectorSearchMatch, BulkWritePlan).

clauses.title: EXPLAIN returns the tree with estimated_rows filled from ADR-0218
clauses.body: EXPLAIN returns the tree with `estimated_rows` filled from ADR-0218 stats and no execution; PROFILE returns the same tree with actual `metrics` (later phases: rows + time first, db-hits counters, then estimates-everywhere, then memory).

clauses.title: The tree is built only on the EXPLAIN/PROFILE path. The
clauses.body: The tree is **built only on the EXPLAIN/PROFILE path**. The regular execution path never constructs `PlanNode`s: phase 1 is pure opt-in (no hot-path reads, no allocations). Later PROFILE phases use RAII scope guards gated behind a collector `Option` so the non-profiled path pays one predictable-null check per operator, nothing more. A loadtest comparison accompanies each phase that touches the hot path.

clauses.title: Per-op memory bytes, Indexes Used/Ordered by columns are deferred;
clauses.body: Per-op memory bytes, `Indexes Used`/`Ordered by` columns are deferred; page-cache stats and planner-implementation metadata are omitted entirely (not meaningful for an embedded in-memory engine — emit nothing rather than constant zeros).

clauses.title: CLI: EXPLAIN/PROFILE print the Neo4j-compatible fixed-width ASCII
clauses.body: CLI: `EXPLAIN`/`PROFILE` print the Neo4j-compatible fixed-width ASCII tree — columns `Operator | Id | Details | Estimated Rows | Rows | DB Hits | Memory (Bytes)`, tree glyphs `+`/`| |`/`|\`, and the footer totals line — omitting the Page Cache column (ADR-0344). The ASCII rendering is also carried as the node's `string-representation` argument so any structured consumer can show the text form.

clauses.title: Bolt: EXPLAIN/PROFILE responses carry the plan as SUCCESS summary
clauses.body: Bolt: EXPLAIN/PROFILE responses carry the plan as SUCCESS summary metadata (`plan` / `profile`), in the Neo4j dict shape.

clauses.title: HTTP Query API: the response envelope carries queryPlan (EXPLAIN) /
clauses.body: HTTP Query API: the response envelope carries `queryPlan` (EXPLAIN) / `profiledQueryPlan` (PROFILE) with the recursive node shape.

clauses.title: The _profile_ data-row columns are deprecated: phase 1 stops adding
clauses.body: The `_profile_*` data-row columns are deprecated: phase 1 stops adding them to EXPLAIN output; their removal from PROFILE lands with phase 2 (PROFILE tree + metrics) so the metrics they approximated remain available in a non-corrupting shape in between.

clauses.title: The PROFILE per-operator metric set is extended to
clauses.body: The PROFILE per-operator metric set is extended to `{ rows, time_ns, db_hits, memory_bytes }`, collected in the dispatch loop through the same sink (`PlanMetricsSink::record_clause` now takes one `ClauseMetricsRecord` bundle). The off-path budget stays one branch per clause: the store-access snapshot and the row-size walk run only when a sink is attached.

clauses.title: db_hits is the clause's store-access count: the delta of the
clauses.body: `db_hits` is the clause's store-access count: the delta of the executor's existing graph-walk counters (`HOP_EXPANDS` + `NEIGHBOR_WALKS`) across the clause's arm — the hop expansions and neighbor walks it performed. It rides the existing counters; no second per-clause counting mechanism, no new instrumentation sites. A clause that walks nothing (a projection, a filtered-out scan) reports an honestly counted zero.

clauses.title: memory_bytes is defined as row-materialization bytes: the summed
clauses.body: `memory_bytes` is defined as **row-materialization bytes**: the summed logical size of the rows the operator produced — each binding's key counted as an ADR-0042 string, each value at its `Value::logical_bytes` (`rows_logical_bytes`, the one canonical helper beside the `Row` type). Stateful operators' non-row state — aggregation tables, sort buffers, distinct-tracking sets — is **a follow-up**, not covered by this metric.

clauses.title: The estimated-vs-actual ratio renders in a text-table column
clauses.body: The estimated-vs-actual ratio renders in a text-table column (`Est/Actual`) on PROFILE trees that carry estimates, computed only on nodes carrying both an estimate and actual rows; an estimate overshoot of 10x or greater flags a warning marker (`25.0x !`). An undefined ratio (no actual rows) renders the shared unavailable spelling, never a fabricated number.

clauses.title: An operator with 0 rows in and 0 rows out
clauses.body: An operator with 0 rows in and 0 rows out — never executed — renders the Neo4j-style `(never executed)` marker in its metric cells, never zeros. It is **derived**, not recorded: the plan tree's bottom-up nesting makes each earlier clause the child of the one it feeds, so an operator's input rows are its first child's `rows` (`never_executed`, the one policy in `wire::plan_table`, shared by the engine renderer and the formatter). The tree's root is exempt by construction: the projection always executes, and its …

clauses.title: The wire form (args) carries DbHits and MemoryBytes beside
clauses.body: The wire form (`args`) carries `DbHits` and `MemoryBytes` beside `Rows`/`TimeNs`, emitted together with the same saturation policy (`metric_i64`); the text table gains the `Db Hits` and `Memory (Bytes)` columns through the existing column-gating vocabulary (`METRIC_COLUMNS`).

clauses.title: New output mode `speedscope`
clauses.body: (`--mode speedscope`, `--format speedscope`, `-mode speedscope`): a `PROFILE` statement's plan tree exports as exactly one speedscope evented-profile JSON document on stdout. One frame per operator, named `"{operatorType} {id}"` with the tree's pre-order ids — the same ids the rendered table's `Id` column and the wire form's `args.Id` show. One `O` and one `C` event per operator; `unit: nanoseconds`; `exporter: cypherlite@<version>`.

clauses.title: The timeline is an approximation, documented as one
clauses.body: The PROFILE tree carries per-operator inclusive times only — no offsets, no exclusive times — so each parent's interval is its own inclusive time and its children are laid out sequentially within it. When the children's inclusive times sum past the parent's (whole-arm measurement can double-count shared work), the children's intervals are scaled down proportionally so every parent's interval contains its children's and the event order stays balanced — the property speedscope's importer requires.

clauses.title: No silent empty export
clauses.body: A plain query (no plan tree) or an `EXPLAIN` statement (a tree without PROFILE metrics) is an error — `speedscope mode requires a PROFILE statement: per-operator times are what it exports (...)` — on stderr, exit code 1. There is no synthesized empty profile.

clauses.title: Docs, help text, and tests land in the same change
clauses.body: (AGENTS.md §2/§3): the hand-written `--help` text, the `docs/api/cli/spec.md` flag table and Speedscope export section, the formatter unit tests, the CLI speedscope e2e test, and the CHANGELOG.

clauses.title: The traversal hot path's candidate checks stop materializing
clauses.body: The traversal hot path's **candidate checks stop materializing strings**: `node_ok` checks static label conjunctions (the common case — the planner synthesizes `label_expr` even for plain `MATCH (n:Person)`) label-by-label via `node_has_label`, paying one interner lookup per (candidate, label) with no `Vec<String>`; genuinely dynamic label expressions take the `node_labels` + `label_expr_matches` path, whose `None` is its own visibility read; a pattern with no `label_expr` checks bare visibility via `node_exists`. …

clauses.title: The core graph maps use FxHash (rustc-hash, CoreMap<K, V> =
clauses.body: The **core graph maps use FxHash** (`rustc-hash`, `CoreMap<K, V>` = `DashMap<K, V, BuildHasherDefault<FxHasher>>`): every map in the graph module is keyed by dense integers or integer pairs, where SipHash's defense buys nothing. The procedures map stays on the default hasher (string keys, cold path).

clauses.title: The agg-fold walk reuses buffers: bindings are extended by
clauses.body: The agg-fold walk **reuses buffers**: bindings are extended by save/restore of the two slots rather than a per-hop `to_vec()`, and the neighbor buffer is one `Vec` reused across the start nodes.

clauses.title: Placement
clauses.body: : the Bolt `plan`/`profile` pair rides the SUCCESS that **ends** the result — the PULL or DISCARD that consumes its last row, the same SUCCESS ADR-0309 gives `type`, `t_last`, `db`, `stats` and `bookmark` (and the depth-truncation marker of ADR-0353) — never the RUN SUCCESS, which stays ADR-0309's `{fields, columnTypes, t_first}` plus the transaction `qid`. The ending SUCCESS repeats `t_first` (Neo4j carries it on both), and a DISCARD that ends the result carries the plan pair too.

clauses.title: Neo4j-shaped plan args
clauses.body: : `PlanNode::to_neo4j_value(&self, statement) -> Value` — the engine hosts the one decoration, the lowest shared module for its three sibling surfaces. Called on a result's plan **root** (the callers hold it as `result.plan: Option<Box<PlanNode>>` and destructure their own `Option` once, which they need anyway for the `is_profiled` key pick): the decoration is root-only by intent — the representation renders the whole statement's plan and the planner/runtime identity is a root fact — never a child node. It adds …

clauses.title: The engine's own wire form stays unchanged
clauses.body: : `Id`, `Details`, `EstimatedRows` (integer), `Rows`, `TimeNs`, `DbHits`, `MemoryBytes`. The mirroring lives in the separate `to_neo4j_value` entry, never in `to_value`, and every surface calls it before converting the value to its own wire type — so Bolt, the HTTP Query API and the CLI's machine modes carry the same plan metadata without `to_value` growing Neo4j-specific fields.

clauses.title: The driver smoke (python_driver_smoke.py) pins the placement and the
clauses.body: The driver smoke (`python_driver_smoke.py`) pins the placement and the decorated args through the official driver.

clauses.title: Statement retention is accounted
clauses.body: : an open result keeps the RUN's statement text for the ending summary's plan pair, and that text counts against `--max-result-bytes` (ADR-0110) beside the rows' logical bytes — reserved in both the buffered and the execution-failed arm — so a transaction full of huge statements cannot park unbounded text outside the cap.

clauses.title: The direct route is tried first
clauses.body: `upgrade` fetches `SHA256SUMS` from `https://github.com/neo4j-labs/cypherlite/releases/download/{tag}/{asset}` before anything else. That one manifest request is the probe; there is no separate probe request.

clauses.title: A 2xx probe serves the whole upgrade
clauses.body: The signature and the binary then come from the same direct route and no GitHub API request is made at all. This is the tokenless path for the public future and stays API-free.

clauses.title: A 404 on the probe, with GITHUB_TOKEN set, falls back
clauses.body: Asset ids are resolved with `GET https://api.github.com/repos/neo4j-labs/cypherlite/releases/tags/{tag}` (consuming only `assets[].name` and `assets[].id`, and failing closed when one of the three required names is absent), then each asset is downloaded from `GET https://api.github.com/repos/neo4j-labs/cypherlite/releases/assets/{id}` with `Accept: application/octet-stream` and the bearer token.

clauses.title: A 404 on the probe without a token aborts
clauses.body: with a single `Error: upgrade: …` line naming `GITHUB_TOKEN` and the documented reinstall one-liner (exit 1, nothing downloaded, nothing modified) — the same actionable shape `install.sh` prints when its release lookup fails.

clauses.title: Any other probe failure aborts exactly as today — no fallback
clauses.body: 403, 5xx, network and read failures are not a route signal; only the typed HTTP 404 status triggers the fallback, never string matching on an error message.

clauses.title: The `Authorization` header is sent only on `api.github.com` requests
clauses.body: (and on the direct request when a token is set); it is never forwarded to the asset CDN on a redirect.

clauses.title: The ADR-0115 verification chain is unchanged
clauses.body: — SSHSIG over the exact manifest bytes against the pinned key, then the checksum over the binary — and runs before the binary is trusted, whichever route delivered the bytes.

clauses.title: Two base-URL test seams join the existing `CYPHERLITE_RELEASES_JSON_URL`
clauses.body: : one overriding the direct-route base (default `https://github.com/neo4j-labs/cypherlite/releases/download`) and one overriding the GitHub API base (default `https://api.github.com`). Both are documented dev/test seams; an empty value means the default.

clauses.title: No publisher change
clauses.body: `releases.json` keeps its schema (no asset ids) and no backfill publish is needed: the CLI resolves asset ids at upgrade time from the release tag it already has.

clauses.title: The engine emits the plan tree only
clauses.body: `plan_node/render.rs` is deleted; `PlanNode` exposes its structured value (`to_value`, `to_neo4j_value`) and its typed accessors, never rendered text.

clauses.title: `EXPLAIN` no longer returns a plan-as-string-lines data column
clauses.body: (ADR-0345 §1 superseded). The plan rides `result.plan` as the tree; the plan-column shape was a rendering smuggled into the result shape.

clauses.title: Every boundary renders the plan text on demand through
clauses.body: — the CLI table, the Bolt `string-representation`, the HTTP plan text. Surfaces may depend on the formatter (ADR-0103 R3: `surfaces/*` may target `surfaces/*`); the engine may not, which is why the renderer cannot live there.

clauses.title: `string-representation` is composed at the surface boundary
clauses.body: from that one rendering (ADR-0357 §2's engine-side composition superseded); the tree/args decoration itself stays in the engine, only the text moves.

clauses.title: One layout, one text
clauses.body: : the formatter's grid (`plan_table` + `layout`) is the only plan layout; the header (`Query:` echo + `Plan:` marker) is rendered by the same module, so every channel shows the same bytes.

clauses.title: One workspace rand major
clauses.body: The root `Cargo.toml` declares `rand = "0.9"` (resolved to 0.9.5). `cypherlite-executor`, `cypherlite-datasets`, `cypherlite-auth` and the optional CLI `telemetry` feature keep consuming `rand = { workspace = true }`; no per-crate version is pinned and no compatibility shim or wrapper is added.

clauses.title: The rename surface is applied at every call site
clauses.body: `thread_rng()` → `rng()`, `gen_range` → `random_range`, `gen` → `random`, `gen_bool` → `random_bool`. The already-compatible spellings listed above stay as they are: `rand::random()`, `StdRng`, `SeedableRng::seed_from_u64`, `RngCore::fill_bytes` and `IteratorRandom::choose_multiple`.

clauses.title: wasm32 wiring is target-scoped in `cypherlite-storage`
clauses.body: rand 0.9's getrandom 0.3 dependency needs the `wasm_js` backend on `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, beside the existing getrandom 0.2 `js` entry. The storage crate's `[target.'cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")'.dependencies]` carries both (the ADR-0085 pattern, so every wasm consumer of storage inherits the fix): The target-scoped entry resolves to getrandom 0.3.4 (the manifest's `0.3.4` requirement; `Cargo.lock` pins 0.3.4): … As of getrandom 0.3.4, the Cargo `wasm_js` feature alone selects that backend. The `--cfg …

clauses.title: The frozen envelopes are re-frozen by CI, not hand-edited
clauses.body: The RNG swap changes generated dataset content and therefore the logical-bytes figures recorded in the frozen fraud/identity baselines. Re-freeze is CI-owned per ADR-0071: dispatch `.github/workflows/create-loadtest-baselines.yml` from the PR branch; the workflow opens its envelope PR with `--base "$GITHUB_REF_NAME"`, so it bases back onto that branch. clauses.title: The residual dual version is accepted and bounded

clauses.title: The grid takes a total-width budget
clauses.body: When the measured widths exceed it, the widest columns give up width first, down to a floor (`MIN_COLUMN_WIDTH`), and the cell renderer **wraps** their content over as many lines as the column needs, at word boundaries — falling back to a character boundary for a word wider than its column, never splitting a multi-column character. A row whose cells all fit still renders as one line.

clauses.title: The budget is the terminal width, and it is explicit
clauses.body: `cypherlite --width N` sets it; otherwise the terminal width (`COLUMNS`) applies when stdout is a terminal; a piped or redirected run keeps the natural width, so its output stays byte-stable and diffable.

clauses.title: `markdown` ignores the budget
clauses.body: A GFM table has no wrapped cells, so markdown lays out at its natural width.

clauses.title: The dead per-column `.width` knob is retired
clauses.body: — the truncate-with- ellipsis path, its `ELLIPSIS` marker and the `column_widths` field go with it. A total budget is what a terminal actually provides, and wrapping preserves the data the knob discarded. The wrapping lives in the one shared layout engine, so the data table and the plan table wrap by construction — no renderer re-implements it.

clauses.title: Inputs negotiation
clauses.body: Negotiate from the raw Accept-Encoding request header (RFC 9110 section 12.5.3 list syntax) with one pure function: split on commas, trim OWS, split each element on ';', compare the coding token case-insensitively, and parse an optional q parameter (0, 1, 0.0-0.999 or 1.000; an unparsable or out-of-range q makes that element q=0). Exactly two representations exist: gzip (the legacy x-gzip alias is accepted too) and identity. gzip's effective q is the explicit gzip/x-gzip element when present, else the '*' element …

clauses.title: Vary
clauses.body: Add 'vary: Accept-Encoding' to every response written by the Query API reply seam, identity responses included, so a shared cache never serves a gzip variant to a client that did not advertise it and keeps the gzip variant keyed. `write_reply` appends it to its local header list beside the CORS echo and the WWW-Authenticate challenge, so http::write_response stays unchanged. Responses outside the seam - the GET / discovery document, the body-less 204 preflight, and the MCP transport - are never gzip and carry no …

clauses.title: q=0
clauses.body: An explicit 'gzip;q=0' (or 'x-gzip;q=0') disables gzip for that request even when '*' has q>0: the more specific entry wins. q=0 on any other coding only excludes that coding, which we never send anyway. 'identity;q=0' and '*;q=0' do not produce a 406 and do not force gzip: when gzip is not selected the response is identity, because encoding is best-effort and must never fail a query that would otherwise succeed. Any effective q>0 selects gzip; no comparison against identity's q is needed because there is exactly …

clauses.title: Wildcard
clauses.body: '*' with q>0 makes gzip acceptable when no explicit gzip/x-gzip element exists ('Accept-Encoding: *' selects gzip when the body clears the threshold and shrinks). An explicit gzip element overrides '*' in both directions: 'gzip;q=0, *;q=1' is identity; 'gzip;q=1, *;q=0' is gzip. '*;q=0' with no explicit gzip entry leaves gzip's effective q at 0, so identity. Empty list elements are ignored, not treated as a wildcard.

clauses.title: Threshold (`threshold_bytes = 1024`)
clauses.body: threshold_bytes = 1024, inclusive: gzip only when the serialized JSON body is at least 1024 bytes. Below it, gzip's ~18-byte framing and encoder CPU cost more than they save, and the small fixed replies (201/202, 404/405/406, 401/403/415) stay identity; at or above 1 KiB a JSON query answer typically shrinks 5-10x. The 'gzip output must be smaller' check runs after the threshold, so an incompressible 1 KiB body still goes identity.

clauses.title: Scope
clauses.body: Every JSON reply the Query API surface writes through its single reply seam - POST /db/{databaseName}/query/v2 (200 success envelope), POST /db/{databaseName}/query/v2/tx (201), POST .../tx/{id} and .../tx/{id}/commit (200), DELETE .../tx/{id} (202), and all 4xx/5xx error envelopes including the pre-body 400/401/403/415 gate answers - whose serialized body is >= threshold_bytes; GET / discovery, the body-less 204 preflight, and the MCP transport stay identity.

clauses.title: `FollowGapPolicy` on `OpenOptions`
clauses.body: `Reload` is the default and is ADR-0137 unchanged: `WalCatchUp::Gap` and a torn redo batch call `follow::reload`. `Yield` does not load a snapshot. It records a permanent follow failure whose error is `Error::resource_limit` (`Error::FOLLOW_GAP`, limit 0, `retryable: true`) and returns that error. clauses.title: The loaded graph stays
clauses.body: `Yield` does not swap it out and does not build another one. A torn apply is fenced by the same latch, so a query that has not yet passed `check_healthy` does not read the torn graph. A statement already past that check runs to completion on it.

clauses.title: The host reopens
clauses.body: CypherLite does not drop its own `Database` or open a replacement under `Yield`. The embedding process observes `needs_reopen`, finishes or closes work that holds the `Arc`, drops the engine, and opens a new follower. Embedded callers that do not do that keep `Reload`.

clauses.title: Charge sites
clauses.body: Charge sites **`regexReplace` imprecision.** The replacement allocation happens inside the `regex` crate and has no interception point. The site charges `input.len() × (replacement.len() + 1)` before the call — a sound upper bound when the pattern can match at most once per byte, and deliberately conservative when it matches less (including not at all). That can refuse a result that would have fit; it is the documented trade for not intercepting the allocator.

clauses.title: Default limit 500
clauses.body: `cypherlite_core::MAX_TRAVERSAL_DEPTH` is 500 hops: an explicit `max_hops` (a `RelPattern`'s `max_hops`, including CIP-28 Form 5, or a `QuantifiedPathPattern`'s `quantifier.max`) above it fails at statement admission. 500 is five times the largest legitimate explicit bound anywhere in the repo, corpus, and docs (100), and far below every measured abort bound, including the 16 MiB WASM stack.

Resolution is the flag or `Some(n)`, then the environment, then 500, resolved in the open preflight before the store lease (the CSV-policy shape). Valid values are 1 through **2000** (`MAX_TRAVERSAL_DEPTH_CEILING`): the ceiling leaves headroom below the smallest measured abort (≈2,700 on the debug WASM stack). Raising it is a deliberate act; values …

It scans every `PatternElement::Relationship` and, recursively, every `QuantifiedPathPattern` even inside another quantified group. clauses.title: Errors defer, never prune — walk-wide
clauses.body: A conjunct that raises is deferred for the rest of the walk: skipped at every later binding point, never re-evaluated early, never pruning. The untouched post-filter reproduces the error on whatever rows survive, so which errors surface never changes (ADR-0469's poison rule, carried from allReduce folds to plain conjuncts).

clauses.title: Selector stand-down
clauses.body: Under any path selector (`ANY`, `SHORTEST k`, `ALL SHORTEST`, …) no conjunct evaluates early and the ADR-0469 allReduce inliner stands down too: a selector chooses among the pattern's FULL candidate set and a MATCH-WHERE predicate narrows the already-selected path (CIP-60 scenario 8) — mid-path pruning would change which path the selector picks. Every conjunct stays a post-filter.

clauses.body: Dialect note Safe mode does not change the Cypher dialect. The same statements parse and plan identically; the refusal happens after parsing and before lowering, and is a policy error, not a syntax-grammar divergence from Neo4j.

Everything else declines to the unchanged DFS — fail-through, answers identical, pinned by …

clauses.body: — default-pool exactness (DIFFERENT RELATIONSHIPS ⇒ TRAIL pool). The prototype's measured divergence: on SF0.1 `knows{1,2}` the engine's trail answers count 855 distinct endpoints, the frontier 856 — the delta is the seed, re-reached by a rel-reusing 2-walk whose shortest *trail* falls below `min`; the engine's own true-walk spelling returns exactly 856. A re-arrival that reaches an already-visited (node, state) pair is accepted only when a trail to that endpoint within `[min, max]` exists — a bounded local check …

clauses.title: Row order for capped paths
clauses.body: LIMIT without ORDER BY has no order contract. ADR-0475's cap rider promises "the rows the materializing walk would emit, in the same order — only sooner" because it halts the engine's own enumeration; that promise does not extend to frontier-served capped emission: BFS-discovery order replaces DFS order, and the *set* of first-cap rows can differ from the DFS's (both valid, both contract-free prefixes). Per-level reconstruction approximates the DFS's depth order but is an implementation choice, not a promise.

clauses.title: The unbounded-WALK rejection is unchanged in v1
clauses.body: Unbounded REPEATABLE ELEMENTS keeps its authored `UnsafeRepeatableElements` rejection (Neo4j-2026.05-aligned; ADR-0471 §3's satiety cap still governs explicit bounds). The frontier could answer unbounded WALK reachability and capped paths soundly in milliseconds — spec fidelity wins: the 42 timeouts are all default-pool shapes. Relaxing the rejection is a behavior change visible to users and is noted here as a possible future ADR, not taken.

Kernel-served queries also tick the nested-evaluation budget once per evaluation, exactly like the kernel arm in `exists_probe.rs` (one evaluation = one tick, never on decline). Declined shapes keep the DFS and its separate walk-step …

clauses.body: It answers with the generic unknown-flag error — no alias, no migration hint (AGENTS.md §3's rule for removed spellings). No users were known at removal.

clauses.body: `AggSeat`'s `Option<(slot, prop)>` becomes plan.rs's `CountSeat::{Star, Prop { distinct, slot, prop }, Whole { distinct, slot }}` — the seat's value source IS the compiled count operand, carried from plan to runtime with no second source enum beside it, and `distinct` unrepresentable beside `Star` — so the per-binding feed `offer_aggs(&mut [(CountSeat, StreamAgg)], &[NodeId])` stays a pure function of the binding's node ids with no row intermediate, and `StreamAgg::count_of(distinct)` is the one distinct→prototype …

clauses.title: The seam is shaped for morsel-parallel scans but implements no
clauses.body: Bindings are independent; the only shared state is the group map `IndexMap<Vec<GroupKey>, (Vec<Value>, Vec<(CountSeat, StreamAgg)>)>`; and every `StreamAgg` variant is mergeable (counts add, `SumAcc` adds, `DistinctAcc` unions). A later node can partition bindings into morsels that each fold into a thread-local group map and merge maps accumulator-wise — the walk, the seats, and the feed signature are unchanged. clauses.title: LABS-685 (radix-partitioned hash aggregation over ADR-0468 Chunks) is

Choosing the `agg_fold` extension deliberately avoids inventing a second accumulator set in the batch substrate, so LABS-685 adopts `StreamAgg` rather than competing with it.
