clauses.title: The compile's structural rule generalizes from "exactly one
clauses.body: The compile's structural rule generalizes from "exactly one top-level `Quantified` element" to **one regular pattern over the closed vocabulary with at most one range-quantified region**: any number of exact-count regions (`min == max`, zero included — a pure concatenation chain), at most one region whose count is a range or unbounded, plain rels elsewhere. The soundness argument is unchanged: an exact-count region contributes a fixed length and unrolls acyclically, so the global hop interval still pins at most …

clauses.title: Exact counts unroll; ranges keep the cycle
clauses.body: A quantifier with `min == max` compiles through the existing structural unroll (k copies, linear states) instead of the cycle form. Per-level frontier sets are then the unrolled automaton's states — the (node, state) pair with state = depth — carried by the existing ever-visited pair set and sparse tables (ADR-0521); no new data structure. In an exact-only pattern every pair is reachable at exactly one level, so the below-min candidate class cannot arise (accepting states sit at depth k) and the dedup filter never …

clauses.title: Everything else rides unchanged: the matcher's gates (spine, pinned
clauses.body: Everything else rides unchanged: the matcher's gates (spine, pinned bindings, conjunct vocabulary, carrying row, mode), the consumer decode, the pools, the emission, the work budget, the cost gate, and the re-arrival rule — which is also the default-pool rel-uniqueness argument for fixed chains (a node-simple representative chain is rel-distinct; the rest take the bounded search, exactly as for quantified shapes). The ladder pre-gate shares the compile's generalized count fact, one spelling.

clauses.title: One typed vocabulary
clauses.body: `KernelRung` names the rung that served a clause: the chain (with its hop count), the hub-star, the frontier-NFA rung, or the per-row walker. It lives in the executor's shared context module beside the other PROFILE vocabularies, and its stable names are single-sourced for the wire.

clauses.title: Recorded per clause, from the clause's own operator decision
clauses.body: The operator ladder returns the rung that took the `MATCH` clause — and the walker when every rung declines — and the clause's PROFILE tick records that returned value; a `SEARCH` `MATCH`, which calls the walker directly, records the walker too. The rung is therefore the clause's own fact: a nested evaluation (`CALL`, `EXISTS`, `FOREACH`) cannot contribute or overwrite one, and no per-row work runs. A clause with no `MATCH` operator carries no rung.

clauses.title: Reported on the plan tree and the wire
clauses.body: The public per-clause metric set gains the rung; the wire emits it (with the chain's hop count) only when a rung served the clause, and the text plan's details cell marks it. Presence-only, like the existing metric facts. Every surface that carries the structured plan — the Bolt summary, the HTTP Query API v2 envelope, the CLI's machine modes — carries the rung through the shared plan presentation, so no surface-specific encoding exists or is needed.

clauses.title: The static half is the engine mode
clauses.body: Every `MATCH` operator of an EXPLAIN and a PROFILE tree carries the store's pattern-engine mode (`auto`, `nfa`, or `walk`) as a plan arg. This is the one engagement fact that is decidable without executing. Deliberately not done: a plan-time prediction of the kernel rung in EXPLAIN. The ladder's riders — the entering row count, the cap and sink projection, and the batch chain ahead of the kernels — are runtime facts, so a prediction can disagree with execution; stating the mode and reporting the executed rung …

clauses.title: The loadtest stops at fixed counts. Flat is 120,000 nodes.
clauses.body: The loadtest stops at fixed counts. Flat is 120,000 nodes. Fanout is 52,016 nodes and 52,000 relationships. Ring is 46,000 nodes and 46,000 relationships, including the closing edge. Dense ring is 5,000 nodes and 100,000 relationships. Base stays empty. The 32 MB logical limit stays as a ceiling. Reaching it before the count fails the run. The report is schema 2. Each shape stores Given / When / Then / Outcome. Sizes print as MB, or GB once a value reaches 1024 MB.

clauses.title: baselines/memory-shape.json is a min/max envelope, schema 1, frozen
clauses.body: `baselines/memory-shape.json` is a min/max envelope, schema 1, frozen by `make baseline-memory-shape` inside `create-loadtest-baselines`. It is separate from `baselines/memory-shape-loadtest.json`, which `make baseline-loadtests` still owns. The freeze runs the loadtest `BASELINE_RUNS` times and keeps min and max per shape for logical bytes, disk, attributed RSS, and the ratio. The ratio is attributed RSS divided by logical bytes.

clauses.title: make compare-memory-shape judges one run. Counts that miss the
clauses.body: `make compare-memory-shape` judges one run. Counts that miss the targets are a regression. Logical bytes, disk, and attributed RSS are lower-is-better, with a 15% band and a 1 MB floor. The ratio is lower-is-better, with a 5% band. A regression clears the top by both the band and the floor. An improvement clears the bottom the same way and fails until the envelope is re-frozen. The document states Baseline, Validated, and Report for every shape, including a green run. An environment-class or knob mismatch is …

clauses.title: The pull-request job is the Sonic stage memory-shape on
clauses.body: The pull-request job is the Sonic stage `memory-shape` on `vars.LOADTEST_RUNNER`. It posts one comment marked `<!-- relate:memory-shape -->`. The nightly cadence runs the same stage, writes the summary, and does not comment. A local freeze is not the envelope. The first pull request reports `no-baseline` until the freeze runs on the x86_64 runner.

clauses.title: Fine split, extending the existing vocabulary
clauses.body: (not a second one): `PhaseTimings` gains `lex_parse` (lexing + AST build), `rewrite` (the ADR-0382 `DEFINE`-block resolver pass), `lower` (validation + lowering) — sub-windows of PARSE — and `result_generation` — a sub-window of EXECUTE. Two requested boundaries stay fused, each for an architectural reason: the lexer and the parser share the parser's one tokenizing constructor (timing them apart means pre-tokenizing, which runs the tokenizer twice — the lexer is ~31–36% of a 1.5–1.9 µs parse, so that tax is real) …

clauses.title: Always-on, decided by measurement
clauses.body: : one clock stamp costs ≤ 33 ns on arm64; the four extra stamps are ~130 ns theoretical, and the measured point-read p50 (16 µs wall, 12 µs engine, pokec-shaped fixture behind a range index, plan-cache path) is unchanged before vs after — the delta sits below the p50's resolution. No PROFILE gating, no flag, no thread-local arming.

clauses.title: Plan-cache outcome, one enum the admission path already knows
clauses.body: : `hit-template` / `hit-raw-fastpath` / `replan-generation-mismatch` / `miss` / `bypassed`, beside the timings on every result header. A hit rejected for literal-shape safety reports `miss` (no cached plan served); its own rejected arm is unobservable — such a statement fails its own original compile, so no result carries it.

clauses.title: Envelope keys, one rendering policy per surface family
clauses.body: (the fact is one: the `TimingStampMs` projection): the canonical envelope extends its flat `_ms` family (MCP, WASM, the C-ABI wire form); the CLI machine modes and the HTTP v2 envelope — which had no timing keys — carry one nested `timings` object plus the `planCache` outcome beside it, so a later phase joins the object and never the top level; Bolt extends its Float-seconds family (`lex_parse_time`, …, `result_generation_time`) plus `plan_cache`.

clauses.title: HTTP v2 carries them
clauses.body: (reversing ADR-0491's exclusion): the keys sit after the Neo4j members, whose reference order is untouched; drivers ignore unknown members. The values are per-request, so byte-identity comparisons across requests must exclude the timing block.

clauses.title: CLI machine-mode shape change, accepted
clauses.body: : `--mode json` wraps every plain run's rows as `{"data": […], "timings": …, "planCache": …}`; `--mode jsonl` closes every statement's stream with a keyed timing line (a zero-row statement emits exactly that line); `--mode toon` renders terminal `timings:` / `planCache:` entries. The strict text formats and the human table mode are unchanged — the `.timer` line stays the human rendering.

clauses.title: Resolve names to token ids once per plan compile
clauses.body: A resolution step runs at the start of planning, over every label, relationship type and property key the statement mentions, against the store's interner. The cached, store-independent statement tree stays id-free; ids live only in the compiled plan.

clauses.title: One token space, one resolver seam
clauses.body: The id type and a narrow resolver trait live in the lowest shared engine crate; the store implements the trait, and the planner receives it beside its statistics seam. The planner never depends on the executor.

clauses.title: A resolved name keeps its text
clauses.body: Operators carry the name and an optional id. Absent means "no committed element carries this name": the executor fails the check without a store read, except where a write overlay is present, in which case the string arm answers. The text stays for plan display and error messages.

clauses.title: Statistics and index probes take ids
clauses.body: The planner's statistics methods gain id-keyed forms so a cardinality or index decision costs no string lookup. Name-keyed forms remain for callers that have no plan.

clauses.title: Executors consume ids without re-resolving
clauses.body: Per-stage resolution in the kernels and per-hop resolution in the walkers collapse into reading the plan's ids; no executor path interns a name from a plan.

clauses.title: Hidden dot commands in the `relate` CLI
clauses.body: Eggs are REPL dot commands resolved after the built-in dot commands, in the CLI surface only. They are not part of the engine, the C ABI, or the extension system.

clauses.title: One registry, one hook, one crate
clauses.body: The seam lives in a new surface crate, `relate-eggs`: a single table mapping each dot-command name to its handler, the shared terminal-capability and refusal types, and the sprite kit. Each egg is its own module there. The crate depends on the engine only, never on the CLI. The CLI's session carries one dispatch call plus the banner and prompt calls, through a small adapter that also supplies the CLI's own first-party rows (Archie), which need CLI facilities. The dispatch searches both tables through one lookup. …

clauses.title: The `eggs` Cargo feature
clauses.body: pulls in `relate-eggs` as an optional dependency, in the `full` bundle only — never `agent`, `minimal`, or bare `serve`. Without it the adapter compiles to inert stubs and every egg name is an ordinary unknown command.

clauses.title: A closed gate
clauses.body: An egg runs only on the interactive REPL with a human at it (never in agent mode, whether detected or explicit) and only when stdout is a terminal. Where the gate is closed the name is an unknown command, so a hidden command is indistinguishable from a missing one. With the gate open, an egg degrades: plain output without colour, or a typed refusal on stderr (exit 1) where it cannot draw at all, such as a non-UTF-8 locale. Never garbled escape sequences. One-shot and piped runs never print banners (ADR-0407).

clauses.title: Documentation stance
clauses.body: Hidden means hidden: eggs are not listed in `.help` or `--help` and the CLI spec does not enumerate them. The spec states that hidden commands exist in `eggs` builds and are unlisted, documents the `eggs` feature and the environment variables that configure them, and nothing more. The hand-written `--help` therefore matches the spec, and a registry test pins that no egg name appears in `.help`.

clauses.title: Archie assets are editable text files
clauses.body: , one character per pixel and one line per row, embedded at build time. One legend table maps each symbol to its colour and its plain shade glyph, so later variants add rows. Two renderers exist: 24-bit half-block colour, and plain shade characters (doubled width). Colour is used only when the terminal advertises 24-bit colour and neither `NO_COLOR` nor `TERM=dumb` is set; a non-UTF-8 locale gets no art. The three tone colours are the brand's logomark values, kept in one palette constant.

clauses.title: First-run banner
clauses.body: On the first interactive human start the large logomark prints beside the unchanged banner line, once per install, tracked by its own marker file in the config directory, claimed by exclusive create. It does not reuse the telemetry first-run claim, since opting out of telemetry must not disable it. The marker is claimed last, so a start that could not draw does not burn it; where no marker can be created the banner is not shown unforced. `RELATE_BANNER=1` forces it, `RELATE_BANNER=0` suppresses it, other values …

clauses.title: Prompt glyph, opt-in
clauses.body: `RELATE_PROMPT=archie` makes the primary prompt the single glyph U+2229; the continuation prompt is unchanged. Colour is applied through the line editor's prompt-highlighter hook, because the editor measures the raw prompt string for cursor placement and escape sequences inside it would miscount width. It falls back to the classic prompts on a non-UTF-8 locale or under `NO_COLOR`.

clauses.title: Exit = one local append
clauses.body: `flush` writes the run's pending envelopes to the run's own spool file — one JSONL file per process under the config directory, one local write, no thread handoff, no network. The spool is bounded and drops past the bound, mirroring the in-memory overflow semantics; no fsync at exit, telemetry stays best-effort.

clauses.title: Next-run drain
clauses.body: An enabled run spawns one detached drain thread at its first recorded event — a run that records nothing (the `off` command above all) never starts a delivery — which claims spool files, renaming each to a unique claim name, sweeping claim files left by crashed or concurrent drains too, and POSTs them in bounded batches while the run's own work proceeds, taking at most a bounded set of files per sweep and dropping the excess past a bounded set of pending files. The sweep takes regular files only: a planted …

clauses.title: No in-run delivery
clauses.body: The bounded channel and its worker thread disappear; a run's events sit in a bounded in-memory backlog and spool at exit. The 2 s HTTP timeout governs the drain POSTs. A session's events report one run late — immaterial for aggregate metrics, since event `time` is stamped at emit.

clauses.title: The flush budget and `RELATE_TELEMETRY_FLUSH_MS` are removed
clauses.body: — nothing on the exit path needs a network bound.

clauses.title: Opt-out
clauses.body: Disabled runs spool and drain nothing. `telemetry off` is one ordered transition — disarm the run's pipeline, persist the key, clear any existing spool — so the run that turns telemetry off neither delivers, records, nor leaves a spool file of its own: turning telemetry off means no further transmissions, pending ones included.

clauses.title: Windows config directory
clauses.body: Resolution gains `%APPDATA%\relate`, then `%USERPROFILE%\.config\relate`, after the existing XDG/HOME order. Strictly additive — `None` becomes a path on Windows — giving Windows a persistent install ID, a working first-run notice, and extension-registry discovery (ADR-0429 §6).

clauses.title: Portability rules
clauses.body: Spool mechanics use std-only primitives: claims by exclusive create and atomic rename, short-lived opens only (Windows denies rename of files another process holds open), no advisory file locks, no platform-conditional code.

clauses.title: Docs and guardrail, same change
clauses.body: The CLI spec's usage-metrics section and privacy listing name the spool and its bounds; the env table loses the removed knob. A cold-start-to-first-query benchmark lands with the change and runs per-OS.

clauses.title: Raw mode on the alternate screen
clauses.body: A game switches the terminal to raw mode, enters the alternate screen and hides the cursor; on exit all three are undone. One shared module owns this and the game loop (a tick timer, key polling, a full redraw of the frame the game renders); each game is pure rules plus a small renderer, so the rules are testable without a terminal.

clauses.title: The terminal is always given back
clauses.body: Restoration lives in a guard's drop, so it runs on normal exit, on an I/O error and on unwinding. Ctrl-C arrives as a key press in raw mode and ends the game through the normal path. A panic inside a game is caught at the loop's edge: the default panic hook is silenced meanwhile (its message would print into the screen that is about to vanish), the guard restores the terminal, the hook is put back, and the failure is reported as an ordinary error on the restored terminal. Key presses still queued at exit are …

clauses.title: Refuse rather than garble
clauses.body: A game refuses, with a typed error on the restored terminal and before touching the screen, when stdin or stdout is not a terminal or the window is smaller than the game's fixed layout. While running, a window shrunk below the layout shows a one-line notice and the game pauses. Colour is used only under the capability rules of ADR-0543; otherwise cells fall back to ASCII. Life needs a UTF-8 locale for braille and refuses without one.

clauses.title: A `games` feature of the eggs crate
clauses.body: is the only thing that links `crossterm`. The CLI's `eggs` feature enables it, so the dependency exists in the `full` bundle alone and never in `agent`, `minimal` or bare `serve`.

clauses.title: Bounded work
clauses.body: The frame size, the Life grid and the Snake board are capped, so per-tick work and output are bounded by constants, not input.

clauses.title: Adopt `proptest` 1.11 as a dev-dependency of `relate-executor`
clauses.body: , at the storage crate's pin. No `proptest-state-machine`: the suite drives a plain generated vector of operations, like the other storage suites.

clauses.title: Boundary ruling
clauses.body: The workspace dependency rules of ADR-0103 (R1–R5, enforced by the boundary check) govern workspace-internal edges by kind; external dev-dependencies are not edges the checker evaluates, and proptest's tree has no native/C++ build, async runtime, or networking, so the heavy-dependency trigger does not apply. The placement is boundary-clean, and the suite reaches the crate-internal structures it guards — the home an external test could not provide.

clauses.title: Observable-semantics guard
clauses.body: The property compares observable adjacency (visibility-filtered iteration), not physical hop vectors: deletes are MVCC tombstones that never touch adjacency today, and the rework may change those internals while this suite stays green.

clauses.title: The standing rules of the storage-only adoption apply unchanged in
clauses.body: The standing rules of the storage-only adoption apply unchanged in this crate: 256-case default with `PROPTEST_CASES` override (no pinned case count), committed regression files, and the rand 0.8 / rand 0.9 dual-major separation (no test mixes the two RNG families).

clauses.title: The operator boundary is a stream
clauses.body: What one operator hands its consumer is either a pull stream of rows or a stream of bounded batches of rows. A batch holds at most 1024 rows; the default is in the low hundreds, sized to the cache, not to the result. A producer whose walk is recursive may instead push each completed row into its consumer's fold; that is the same contract seen from the other side and is equally allowed.

clauses.title: An unbounded result is never accumulated
clauses.body: No operator may return, or hold, a vector whose length grows with the number of intermediate rows, unless it is a declared breaker (rule 3).

clauses.title: Breakers are explicit and charged
clauses.body: Sorting without a limit, a retaining aggregate (collect, percentiles), a distinct set, and a hash join build side may hold state proportional to their input. Each does so deliberately, charges that state to the retaining-container budget (ADR-0463), and prefers a bounded form where one exists (a top-k heap for ordered limits, a seen-set of keys for distinct instead of retained operands).

clauses.title: Small, closed results may stay vectors
clauses.body: Catalog listings, procedure output, and a statement's final bounded page are not intermediate results and need no streaming.

clauses.title: New operators follow this rule from the first commit
clauses.body: A change that adds an operator or clause arm returning an unbounded vector of rows is rejected in review; existing vector-returning operators migrate incrementally, outermost consumers first (aggregation, then projection with early exit, then the remaining generators and match rungs).

clauses.title: Peak memory is observable
clauses.body: The profiling output reports the working set of a streamed operator as one batch, not the retained total, so a regression to accumulation is visible.

clauses.title: Resolved endpoints
clauses.body: The route resolves each unbound endpoint's property map through the node-candidates funnel, the same seek path the pattern walkers use. A row-bound node is a one-element side; a map that reads a variable the row does not bind yet, a bare label and an unbound variable stay scan territory and are not materialized.

clauses.title: Pair product within a bound
clauses.body: When both sides are resolved and their candidate product stays within a fixed small limit, the route runs the pair partition for each combination, exactly as for row-bound ends. Past the limit it fans from the shorter side. With only the end side resolved, it drives a backward fan only while that list is within the limit; otherwise the start candidates fan forward as before.

clauses.title: One hop walk
clauses.body: The neighbour walk yields each relationship with the node it reaches from a single version-chain read; the rel-only walk is its projection. A read-only view skips the write overlay's per-hop existence check and dedup set. The kernels, the GPM hop walk, the path fold and the shortest searches read this one walk. Both-direction dedup stays keyed on the relationship id, because a reused id can repeat within one adjacency list.

clauses.title: Dense-id hashing
clauses.body: The pair search's trees and the layered search's reach and predecessor tables use the keyless dense-id hasher, under the existing rule that engine-allocated ids never need a keyed hash. Result order, tie-breaking and the shapes the route declines are unchanged; this decision only changes which search answers a shape.

clauses.title: The ops are serialized once, at admission
clauses.body: The committing thread encodes the `ops` array of the record into one buffer, off the serial path and in parallel with other committers. The buffer begins with fixed slack for the record header sized for maximum-width LSN and timestamp, and ends with the record's closing brace.

clauses.title: The leader only stamps the header
clauses.body: When the group assigns LSNs and timestamps, the header is written into the slack in place and the frame is the bytes from the header to the end. The payload is byte-identical to the record the single-pass encoder produced; the record format, checksum, and frame layout are unchanged. No JSON is produced inside the leader.

clauses.title: The cap and its refusal are unchanged
clauses.body: The bound is checked while encoding, over the whole prospective record including the maximum-width header slack, so a record is refused at the same size with the same typed capacity refusal and the same figures as the admission count produced. The refusal now happens before the commit joins the queue; the leader can no longer meet an oversized record.

clauses.title: Accounting keeps its shape, with one shift
clauses.body: The workspace reservation is the buffer's size, equal to the previous admission figure, taken before the commit enqueues and held until its waiter completes. Because the size is only known after encoding, the reservation follows the encode rather than preceding it; the serializer's growth is bounded by the cap, and the buffer is trimmed to its length before it is charged.

clauses.title: One canonical path
clauses.body: Every writer reaches the WAL through the same encoder: group commit, the replicated apply path, direct append, and bulk batches. The direct append entry point encodes with the shared helper and then runs the same preflight; there is no second copy of the size policy. The count-only sink is removed.

clauses.title: Typed ops remain
clauses.body: Apply continues to consume the typed redo; this decision does not make apply read the encoded form.

clauses.title: The encoding owns its ops' facts
clauses.body: Encoding runs the redo ID and ontology-envelope validation and records whether an ontology op is present, so the preflight takes no typed ops and a body cannot be paired with ops it was not made from. Invalid redo is now refused at admission.

clauses.title: Unchanged:
clauses.body: the ontology segment rotation rule, stale-proof checks, read-only and poisoned behavior, and the ADR-0094 acceptance and uncertain-outcome rules.

clauses.title: Charge before every growth
clauses.body: The encoder takes the caller's workspace charge and extends it before each growth of its buffer, then allocates exactly that capacity. A refused charge aborts the encoding at once with the workspace's own typed refusal; nothing beyond the granted charge was allocated.

clauses.title: Steps
clauses.body: The buffer grows in powers of two from 1 KiB, or to the next power of two that holds a single large write, clamped to the record cap.

clauses.title: The copy transient is charged
clauses.body: While a growth copies, the old and the new buffer are both resident, so both are charged for that moment and the charge then settles at the new capacity. Concurrent writers are thereby bounded by the limit itself, with no allowance for the reallocation.

clauses.title: The cap is checked first, in the same sink
clauses.body: The record cap is admitted before any growth is charged, so the cap's refusal, its figures and its text are unchanged, and it fires at the same write.

clauses.title: The retained buffer is charged at its capacity
clauses.body: The trimming copy of ADR-0558 decision 4 is dropped for records that outgrew the first step: their charge equals the buffer's capacity (at most twice the record), held until the commit's waiter completes as before. Records that fit the first 64 KiB are still trimmed to their length, which is a cheap copy.

clauses.title: Every caller supplies the charge
clauses.body: Admission, the replicated apply path, the trait-level write engine and the one-call preflight each pass a charge; with no workspace ledger installed it is a no-op.

clauses.title: A rejection decided from statically known types or values is
clauses.body: A rejection decided from statically known types or values is a compile-time SyntaxError. This covers literal argument types (`vector`, `vector.similarity.*`, `char_length`, temporal patterns), literal value domains (vector dimension, `replace()` limit, path-selector count, `IN TRANSACTIONS` concurrency), literal parse failures, call arity, statically non-boolean predicates and operands, and the statement-shape rejections with no runtime input (empty input, multiple graph targets, page bounds outside RETURN/WITH).

clauses.title: A rejection that depends on a per-row value stays the
clauses.body: A rejection that depends on a per-row value stays the runtime TypeError (or the argument-value class for value-domain faults).

clauses.title: The decision lives in the front-end static-literal validator, which
clauses.body: The decision lives in the front-end static-literal validator, which owns "what the statement text decides"; the planner and executor keep only runtime backstops, so the two layers cannot disagree on a shape the front end rejects.

clauses.title: A feature gate's own rejection (preview not enabled) keeps its
clauses.body: A feature gate's own rejection (preview not enabled) keeps its authored class; this ADR says nothing about gated constructs.

clauses.title: A second, larger cap on the full listing
clauses.body: The both-sides-over case lists each side through the capped funnel with a fixed listing limit far above the pair bound, rather than the uncapped funnel.

clauses.title: Typed refusal at the cap
clauses.body: A side matching more than the listing limit fails the statement with the capacity family's error, in a new `CapacityKind::SeekCandidates`, carrying the match count the scan reached (a lower bound) and the limit. There is no silent truncation, and no fallback to the unbounded path.

clauses.title: The pair-bound probe is under the same contract
clauses.body: It stops one match past the pair bound on every endpoint shape it probes: a bare map, a label and a map, a label disjunction, and a declared-index seek. Over the bound is a routing signal, not a result, so the probe raises no error; the answer is never wrong, since only the list's length is read. Only shapes whose scan answers with exact matches are probed: a negated or dynamic label falls to the all-nodes tail, a superset whose length is not a match count, and stays fan territory.

clauses.title: Postings and buckets are streams
clauses.body: The declared index's equality postings are read as a stream the consumer stops pulling; the unbounded id set is that stream collected, one policy. The capped funnel streams the shortest posting and checks each candidate against the snapshot, never building an id set sized by the index. A scan copies the shortest label bucket's ids under one short guard and visits them outside it, so the guard is never held across a node read; the copy is a flat id list sized by the bucket, not by the matches. A vanished index (a …

clauses.title: Db Hits count the work performed
clauses.body: Every node a scan examines and every index posting read counts, whether or not it matches, including on the stop-at-bound and refusing paths; an answer served whole from postings counts what it returned. PROFILE never reports the full set an unbounded scan would have read, nor only the matches of a long scan.

clauses.title: Surface mapping is unchanged
clauses.body: The refusal is the memory-limit class on every surface, like the other capacity kinds (ADR-0494).

clauses.title: Selectors are physical operators
clauses.body: Every shortest selector is a physical operator of the one pattern evaluator, chosen by plan shape. The ADR-0186 route, with ADR-0189's shared search and ADR-0556's pair search, is formalized as the engine's BFS operator. Enumeration followed by selection is the fallback operator for shapes the BFS cannot follow, such as multi-relationship or quantified bodies. The routed shapes, selector set and result contract of ADR-0186 are unchanged; this decision adds no behaviour. Operators obey ADR-0555 (streaming) and …

clauses.title: The expression form normalizes onto the pattern machinery
clauses.body: The front end lowers the shortest expression onto the same pattern plus selector form the clause uses, and the expression form's private search driver is deleted: one evaluator, one set of semantics. The unified engine takes the global shortest across all start and end candidates. Two accidental behaviours of the expression form are removed: `shortestPath` stopping at the first start candidate that has a trail, and `allShortestPaths` letting the first candidate fix the length cap (a result that depended on …

clauses.title: Witness choice is unspecified
clauses.body: Among equally short paths, which one a single-path selector returns is not part of the contract. No Neo4j-parity or newest-first tie-break is promised; ADR-0203's order stays an implementation detail of enumeration, not a guarantee. Lengths, row counts and all-shortest result sets stay exact.

clauses.title: Native shortest on the frontier NFA is a separate research track
clauses.body: The design note on that question stands. It does not gate this decision and a later ADR must carry any change of the operator set.

clauses.title: Resolution
clauses.body: The metadata URL is `https://relatedb.ai/releases.json`, overridable through `RELATE_RELEASES_JSON_URL` with the same empty-means-default rule `upgrade` documents (ADR-0250 §1), and it is the only source consulted: no fallback. The request carries no `Authorization` header (the file is public and on a different origin, ADR-0250 §5). The tag is `latest.tag` and must be a `vX.Y.Z` release tag — the stable-tag invariant the schema fixes and the publisher selects by (ADR-0250 §2); anything else is a malformed …

clauses.title: Asset ids
clauses.body: One per-tag request (the releases/tags endpoint, never the latest-release endpoint), with the `GITHUB_TOKEN` bearer header while the repository is internal (ADR-0068 §6). The response's `tag_name` must equal the requested tag: the API must describe exactly the release the metadata named. The asset download route is unchanged.

clauses.title: Failure behavior
clauses.body: Every resolution failure dies before any download with a one-line message naming the failed source, mirroring ADR-0250 §4's aborts; the `GITHUB_TOKEN` hint moves to the per-tag fetch failure — the one request the token can help. The ADR-0457 binding, the legacy window, and the verify-before-download ordering are unchanged; only the tag's provenance changes.

clauses.title: Harness
clauses.body: The offline harness pins the contract: the stub serves an extension release at the old endpoint in every mode, so any request of it fails the install loudly; a case serves the publisher's committed output fixture as the metadata document end to end, so a serialization the installer's parse cannot read fails the suite instead of the one-liner; and section-0 drift guards hold the URL literal and the env-var name to the CLI's `releases_json.rs` constants.

clauses.title: The import seam gains a bulk spelling
clauses.body: The row-at-a-time calls stay, with a default implementation that loops them, so every existing implementation keeps working. The executor overrides the bulk calls with a window-local builder.

clauses.title: Node windows install in parallel; the publication boundary stays the
clauses.body: Windows are id-disjoint by construction, so workers can each build one and hand the result over. Nothing half-installed is ever visible.

clauses.title: Relationship adjacency is not a disjoint-unit problem
clauses.body: Rel windows are rel-id-disjoint, and a relationship's hop lands in its endpoints' chunks, so a high-degree node's chunk receives hops from relationships spread across many windows. Installing relationship adjacency in parallel therefore needs a merge discipline: per-worker local per-(node, type) slices merged at install, or a two-pass split that installs version state per window and groups adjacency by endpoint afterwards.

clauses.title: A window-local build lands in the existing chunk shape
clauses.body: The walk kernels read the per-(node, type) chunks the row-at-a-time path fills, in the same timestamp order, so the bulk path must produce exactly those chunks. The win is the removed per-hop search and per-row interning, not the insert's memmove, which the bulk path still pays.

clauses.title: Decode parallelizes on row groups, scheduled on the page envelope
clauses.body: A row group is the unit the writer already batches by and is far too small to schedule individually, so decode units coalesce to the writer's page-envelope row count. A row group's id range is read from its id column, never computed by stride: the encoder skips ids invisible at the read timestamp before batching, so groups have gaps.

clauses.title: Syntax
clauses.body: `term~`, `term~N`, `term^B` and `field:term~N^B` are parsed into typed clause fields (an optional edit bound, a boost defaulting to 1). A bare `~` is 2 edits; an integer above 2 clamps to 2; `~x` with `0 <= x < 1` is a minimum similarity, an edit bound of `floor((1 - x) * term length)` capped at 2 (`~0` is exact). A non-integer of 1 or more (`~1.5`) is a syntax error. Text after a `~` that is not a `^` boost is a separate word (`term~1x` is a bare `~` plus the term `1x`), and a detached `~1` or `^2` binds to the …

clauses.title: Expansion
clauses.body: A fuzzy clause expands, per field, against that field's vocabulary (the document-frequency table already built per scan) by a bounded Damerau-Levenshtein distance (optimal string alignment: insert, delete, substitute, adjacent transposition each cost one; early exit past the bound). Lucene defaults apply: no pinned prefix, at most 50 expansions, ordered closest, then most frequent, then lexicographic so results are deterministic. The expansions form an any-of group, so `AND`/`OR`/`NOT`/required semantics are …

clauses.title: Scoring
clauses.body: Each expanded term scores with the existing calibrated BM25, multiplied by a closeness weight of `1 - edits / min(query length, term length)`; exact terms weigh 1. A candidate whose weight would be zero is not a match. The clause's boost multiplies its score last; boost never changes which rows match.

clauses.title: Reuse
clauses.body: The distance routine is a small crate-private module so a future Cypher string-similarity function can share it.

clauses.title: Calibration
clauses.body: The suffix grammar, clamping, the closeness weight (0.875 at one edit and 0.75 at two on an eight-character term, scores exactly weight times BM25), exact boost scaling and the AND/NOT behaviour were confirmed on Neo4j 2026.09-enterprise. Not modelled: Lucene's document-frequency blending across expansions, and a fuzzy word that analyzes to several tokens applies the suffix to each token.

clauses.title: The vocabulary gains one entry: <> between the pattern's two
clauses.body: The vocabulary gains one entry: `<>` between the pattern's two named boundary variables, in either order. It is admitted only for the distinct-endpoint consumer, whose answer is the set of (seed, endpoint) pairs, and is decided per pair at arrival: a pair whose endpoint is its own seed (re-reached by a cycle or self-loop, or the zero-length arrival of a zero lower bound) does not answer; endpoints compare by node identity. The default pool's trail-existence proof is unchanged, so the admitted endpoint set is …

clauses.title: The PROFILE record's decline field carries a typed reason that
clauses.body: The PROFILE record's decline field carries a typed reason that is either a plan-time gate (`FrontierDecline`) or a run-time decline (`FrontierRunDecline`), as one public sum, `FrontierDeclineReason`, re-exported by the `relate` crate. It is recorded for clauses with one quantified pattern whose family is not stood down; the first decline per clause wins. The wire vocabulary of the existing reason field grows from the two run-time names to those plus one kebab-case name per plan-time gate; the plan table marks it …

clauses.title: Which analyzer folds
clauses.body: Only `standard-folding` folds; the other probed names do not. (`german` matches `muller` through its own German normalisation, which is not modelled.) The fold is Lucene's ASCII folding: Latin diacritics drop, and ligatures and letter variants expand (`ß` to `ss`, `æ` to `ae`, `œ` to `oe`, `ø` to `o`, `ł` to `l`, `þ` to `th`), as do full-width forms. Greek and Cyrillic are untouched. It is a small hand-written table over the Unicode normalisation crate the executor already depends on, so no dependency is added. A …

clauses.title: Where folding applies
clauses.body: To the index's stored tokens (the index's configured analyzer is now read) and to analyzed query terms. Without `WITH ANALYZER` a query uses the index's folding but not its stemming, because stored tokens remain unstemmed (the ADR-0578 shortcut stands). `WITH ANALYZER` changes the query side only, as live does: a folded query term against an unfolded index still misses.

clauses.title: Fuzzy terms are not folded
clauses.body: Live lowercases them only and measures distance from the raw term to the folded stored term: `eifrém~0` misses on a folding index while `eifrém~1` reaches `eifrem`. The existing behaviour is therefore kept; the distance is not measured after folding.

clauses.title: Wildcard syntax
clauses.body: `*` is any run (including none), `?` exactly one character, a leading wildcard is allowed, `**` equals `*`, and a backslash makes the next character literal. A wildcard term is lowercased and never stemmed or stop-filtered. **Deliberate deviation from live 2026.09:** live lowercases wildcard terms only, so on a folding index `mull*` finds `Müller` and `Müll*`, `MÜLL*` and `EIFRÉ*` find nothing. Here, under an analyzer that folds, the literal parts of the pattern are folded like the stored tokens and plain terms …

clauses.title: Matching and scoring
clauses.body: A wildcard is matched against each document's tokens in the fields it selects, as one any-of clause, so `AND`/`OR`/`NOT`, `field:` filters and boost compose unchanged. A field scores a constant 1.0 when it holds any matching term, however many terms or occurrences, summed over fields and clauses and times the boost. There is no expansion cap: live expands 3000 distinct terms with no clause-limit error, so a silent cap would drop real hits.

clauses.title: Errors
clauses.body: A wildcard term of more than 256 parts (after `**` collapses) is a typed syntax error, checked once at parse so matching stays free of a per-document budget; Lucene bounds a wildcard by its automaton's determinization work and tantivy by the regex size limit, both at compile time. Suffix errors keep ADR-0578's typed syntax errors; a wildcard-only word may carry a boost; a stored analyzer name the engine does not know is reported as index-definition drift.

clauses.title: One Cypher version: 25
clauses.body: The `CYPHER 25` statement preamble is an accepted no-op — it parses and changes nothing; an unprefixed statement already speaks Cypher 25.

clauses.title: Every other CYPHER <n> integer fails with one authored
clauses.body: , `CYPHER 5` included. Settled text, `<n>` the requested integer: `UnsupportedCypherVersion: CYPHER <n> is not supported; the only supported Cypher version is CYPHER 25` The preamble fails it at parse, the language value at command execution — where each is checked today.

clauses.title: `ALTER DATABASE … SET DEFAULT LANGUAGE` admits only `CYPHER 25`
clauses.body: (ADR-0116 §2, narrowed). The stored value stays display-only catalog state (§8 unchanged); no store format changes and a value an older binary wrote is not rewritten.

clauses.title: The version machinery is removed as unreachable
clauses.body: The dialect fact, the gate allowlist, the create-self-reference stand-down (ADR-0513 Decision 1's arm), the SHOW-family version branches and the version threading through the AST, lowering, IR, plan and query context exist to tell 5 from 25; with 25 the only admitted version none can fire.

clauses.title: One transport
clauses.body: `releases.json` remains the only metadata source (ADR-0571); its tag and the asset names determine every URL. Any non-2xx answer dies with the request and the HTTP status — the same pinned status text the CLI's release channel carries. The transport is TLS-only: the seam's base is gated to `https://` before the first request of any kind — deliberately narrower than the CLI seam's `approved_transport` loopback plain-http carve-out, because the installer is the end-user pipe-to-bash surface and its own test rig …

clauses.title: No token
clauses.body: `GITHUB_TOKEN` is not read: the direct route cannot be helped by a token at either repository visibility, and curl would forward a custom Authorization header across the route's cross-host redirect to the asset CDN.

clauses.title: One seam
clauses.body: The base is overridable through `RELATE_RELEASE_DOWNLOAD_URL` — the same seam `upgrade` documents — with empty meaning the canonical default and no fallback between the two; a harness drift guard holds it to the CLI's constant.

clauses.title: The integrity chain is unchanged
clauses.body: `releases.json` selects but is never trusted; SSHSIG verification (ADR-0115), the signed version-header binding (ADR-0457) and the checksum gate run before the binary is trusted, whichever route delivered the bytes.

clauses.title: Maintenance
clauses.body: rides the seams the other counts ride, under the bundle's one guard: node create and node delete bump the node's set; a label add or remove moves one node from its old set to its new one in a single guarded step, so a reader never sees the intermediate state. Abort, restore and open recompute the map in the wholesale count rebuild, in the same pass that folds the label and total counts. Drained entries leave the map, and the same loud pairing contract applies (a removal without its paired add is a broken store and …

clauses.title: Charging
clauses.body: Entries are query-controlled, so each entry charges the memory accounting on creation and refunds on drain, at a per-entry constant plus the key's width, and the structure recount reads the same constant. The admission estimate prices a batch's set creations and drains the same way.

clauses.title: Recognition
clauses.body: A new shape recognizer answers only the statement of exactly one plain, variable-bound node match returning group keys plus one `count(*)` or `count(n)`, where every key depends on the node only through its label list (`labels(n)`, `size(labels(n))`, a literal subscript of it, or a label predicate on it). `ORDER BY` items must name an output column or repeat an output expression; `SKIP`/`LIMIT` are unrestricted. Anything else declines to the scan.

clauses.title: Evaluation
clauses.body: Each key expression is evaluated by the ordinary expression evaluator over one stand-in node per distinct label set, so semantics (errors, nulls, subscript bounds, label predicates) are the evaluator's, not a second implementation. Counts are summed per output key (grouping equivalence is the aggregation's own key), then the ordinary projection finishes ordering and paging over the grouped rows. The copy of the set map and the group table charge the expression budget as they land, so a paged statement refuses at …

clauses.title: Visibility
clauses.body: The map describes the latest committed state, as the other counts do. It answers only for a view that sees exactly that state, under the same two-step check as the counting operator (no scratch overlay, no write in flight, snapshot equal to the latest commit, re-checked under the bundle guard). Any other view, including an explicit transaction and a pinned older snapshot, declines to the scan, which reads its own snapshot. A graph whose sets approach its node count (above a fixed floor, fewer than a few nodes per …
